title: Shared platform Google service account can surface other tenants' Shared Drive files
claim: One platform service account (GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY) is added as fileOrganizer to every Workspace tenant's auto-created Shared Drive (cloud_init.py:1214-1244). When no per-user Google grant exists or no user_id is passed (admin test search cloud_admin.py:465, tenant sync_all), cloud_search._get_google_token (cloud_search.py:1516-1527) and cloud_sync._get_token (cloud_sync.py:833-864) return the service-account token. _search_google_drive then queries corpora=allDrives with no driveId when there is no matter folder (cloud_search.py:666-676), fetch_contents downloads the hits (1098-1138), and there is no post-filter on drive_id (333-347). The prefer_service_account probe (google_service_account.py:213-258) only checks access to this tenant's drive and does not scope the query. Result: firm A's chat or index can include firm B's Shared Drive titles and content, a cross-tenant confidentiality breach.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/google_service_account.py:49-82 loads one deployment-global key from settings.GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY. backend/app/services/cloud_init.py:1214-1244 creates a Shared Drive per tenant and adds that same service_account_email() as a member. This runs automatically on Workspace connect (cloud_init.py:236-248, GOOGLE_AUTO_SHARED_DRIVE=True at config.py:173). docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:61-63 describes adding 'LawHand's central service account' to each drive. In cloud_search.py:1516-1527, _get_google_token uses the user's own token when one exists. Otherwise it passes the tenant token through prefer_service_account, and google_service_account.py:231-251 returns the SA token when the tenant has an org_shared_drive binding and the probe of this tenant's drive succeeds. The probe does not scope any later query. In cloud_search.py:206-231, search() calls _search_google_drive with folder_id=None when the matter has no Drive folder. That query (cloud_search.py:664-676) sends corpora=allDrives and includeItemsFromAllDrives with no driveId, so it covers every Shared Drive the SA belongs to. Lines 333-344 only dedupe hits; nothing filters them by drive. _fetch_google_drive_content (1098-1136) downloads each hit with the same token. cloud_admin.py:465 and 470 call search and fetch_contents with no user_id, so they always take the tenant/SA token. rag.py:1889-1905 (from chat.py:2626-2644) does the same for any user without a personal Google grant.
reviews.correction: The exposure depends on configuration. GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY is empty by default (config.py:166), and the leak needs at least two tenants with an SA-bound org Shared Drive. The repo does not show whether production sets the key, although the storage-root docs present it as the intended production path. The live chat and admin-test search-and-fetch path is certain. The 'index' part is less certain: sync_google_drive uses corpora=user (cloud_sync.py:356), not allDrives. Whether that corpus includes files the SA created in other tenants' drives depends on Drive semantics. One point is understated: cloud_sync._get_token applies prefer_service_account even when a user token exists (cloud_sync.py:854-862). Matter-folder-scoped searches ('folder' in parents) are not affected.
reviews.fix_sketch: Whenever the resolved Google token is the service-account token, scope Drive calls to the tenant's own drive. In _search_google_drive, set corpora=drive and driveId=<binding.drive_id>. Optionally also require the root folder in parents. Have _get_google_token return a (token, scope) tuple so callers know when the SA is in use. In _fetch_google_drive_content, first fetch files.get(fields=driveId) and refuse to download when driveId differs from the tenant's drive. Apply the same corpora=drive+driveId scoping in cloud_sync.sync_google_drive and _sync_google_drive_folder. Also drop search hits whose driveId is not the tenant's. Add regression tests asserting that SA-token queries always carry driveId. Longer term, give each tenant its own identity (per-tenant SA or delegated subject). Review provider/audit logs for past cross-tenant hits.

reviews.evidence: The mechanism is real. cloud_init.py:1214-1244 (_provision_org_shared_drive) adds the single platform service account (GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY, config.py:165-166) to every tenant's auto-created Shared Drive. google_service_account.py:248-293 (prefer_service_account) returns that account's token for any org_shared_drive tenant after a probe of only that tenant's drive. cloud_search.py:1552-1564 (_get_google_token; the claim's line numbers are stale) and cloud_sync.py:843-875 (_get_token) fall back to it. The claim's premise was valid on origin/main (unscoped corpora=allDrives search, corpora=user plus includeItemsFromAllDrives sync, no driveId check on content fetch). HEAD, however, includes commit 0a483e4 'fix(security): pin service-account Drive access to the requesting tenant', which is on this branch and NOT in origin/main. That commit adds service_account_drive_scope (google_service_account.py:213-245). Drive search now returns [] when no tenant drive is bound and uses corpora=drive&driveId=<tenant drive> (cloud_search.py:643-649, 683-685). Content fetch verifies driveId before download (cloud_search.py:1109-1123 and 1136-1147). The tenant-wide sync is pinned the same way (cloud_sync.py:333-339, 364-366). Tests are in backend/tests/test_service_account_drive_scope.py. The admin test search (cloud_admin.py:465-472) and sync_all go through these guarded functions. Residual gaps on HEAD: (1) POST /matters/{id}/cloud-folder/context (routers/matters.py:3195-3260) needs only a normal user, not admin. It resolves an arbitrary folder ID/URL with the service-account token (cloud_init.py:1445-1468 → build_matter_folder_metadata 1289-1310) and never checks item.driveId against the tenant's drive. Context folders then feed sync_google_drive_folders (cloud_sync.py:1226-1231, 216-226, 432-445), and _sync_google_drive_folder (cloud_sync.py:940-970) lists '<folder>' in parents with the service-account token and no drive pin. A user who knows another firm's folder ID can therefore index that firm's file titles and owners into their own cloud_metadata_index. Live search and content fetch remain blocked by the driveId pin. The admin-only remap (matters.py:3106-3182) can also upload a marker file into such a folder (matter_folder_marker.py:103-109). (2) Rows indexed from other tenants' drives before the fix are not purged. (3) The service-account-token check compares the token string with the current cached token (google_service_account.py:239-241). If the cache re-mints (60s before expiry, lines 124-127) between the prefetch and the comparison, drive_scope becomes None and the search reverts to allDrives.
reviews.correction: Line refs are stale, and the claim ignores that HEAD already contains the fix (0a483e4). The fix covers the named paths: search, content fetch, tenant sync and admin test search. The claim is still valid for origin/main, which is presumably what production runs until this branch merges. The exposure also requires a platform service-account key to be configured (off by default, config.py:166) and two or more org Shared Drive tenants. Remaining on HEAD: the context-folder metadata-indexing vector (needs a user who knows the foreign folder ID), leftover index rows, and a narrow token-rotation race. High is kept because the unmerged fix leaves main exposed to a cross-tenant confidentiality breach.
reviews.fix_sketch: Merge 0a483e4 to main promptly. In resolve_cloud_folder_reference/build_matter_folder_metadata, reject any Google folder whose driveId differs from the tenant's bound drive when the service-account token is in use, and apply the same pin in _sync_google_drive_folder. Run a one-time audit and purge of cloud_metadata_index rows and search caches for Google objects that are not in the tenant's drive; also query production for object_ids indexed under more than one tenant to assess whether an incident occurred. Detect the service-account token robustly: have prefer_service_account return a typed result (token plus pinned drive_id) instead of comparing strings with the live cache. Longer term, consider per-tenant service accounts or domain-wide delegation so one credential never spans customers.

title: Live cloud search/fetch falls back to the connecting admin's delegated token for every user
claim: cloud_search._get_microsoft_token (cloud_search.py:1529-1543) and _get_google_token (1516-1527) fall back to token_vault.get_fresh_token (the tenant credential, i.e. the delegated refresh token of the admin who connected) when the requesting user has no personal grant. rag._connected_providers treats that tenant credential as connected for every user (rag.py:344-376) and RAG calls connected-source search for any user (rag.py:1889-1906). Consequently Graph /search/query message hits search the admin's mailbox (cloud_search.py:941-986) and _fetch_outlook_content downloads full MIME from /me/messages/{id}/$value (1329-1362); driveItem search returns anything the admin can see; Gmail search (751-850) and full-body fetch (1140-1167) are not matter-scoped; matter-scoped searches still keep 'outlook' in the global query (_microsoft_sources_without_scoped, 1745-1764). Any firm user's chat can therefore return the admin's private email bodies and OneDrive/SharePoint/Drive files, bypassing provider permissions and ethical walls. The Hub copy's 'Confirm the ... mailbox boundary' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:100) has no backing control.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_search.py:1529-1540: _get_microsoft_token uses the user's token when one exists and otherwise returns get_fresh_token(tenant). token_vault.py:413-435 returns the TenantCredential access token. routers/integrations.py:584-611 shows that credential is the connecting admin's authorization-code grant (intent=admin), requested with delegated MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES that include Mail.Read, Files.ReadWrite.All and Sites.Read.All (integrations.py:241-243). The Google admin grant includes gmail.readonly (245-248). rag.py:342-373 (_connected_providers) counts any active TenantCredential as connected for every user. chat.py:2626-2644 calls hybrid_rag_query with each user's id, which reaches cloud_search.search and fetch_contents (rag.py:1886-1905). The Graph /search/query message entity group (cloud_search.py:919-975) therefore runs against the admin's mailbox. _fetch_outlook_content (1329-1358) downloads /me/messages/{id}/$value. Gmail search (760-790) hits /users/me/messages and _fetch_gmail_content (1140-1167) returns the full body, neither scoped to a matter. _microsoft_sources_without_scoped (1745-1764) keeps 'outlook' in the global query when OneDrive/SharePoint are folder-scoped. cloud_search.py and cloud_sync.py have no ethical-wall or owner check. IntegrationsHub.jsx:100 tells admins to 'Confirm the permitted site, drive, or mailbox boundary', but no such control exists in the backend.
reviews.correction: On the Google side, tenants with an SA-bound org Shared Drive (and the key configured) have the admin token replaced by the Drive-only service-account token (google_service_account.py:231-251). For them the admin's Gmail is not reachable and the D01 cross-tenant Drive issue applies instead. Admin Gmail and Drive exposure applies to tenants without that binding. The Hub copy at IntegrationsHub.jsx:95 does disclose that search 'does not create a separate permission boundary', so the UI is only partly misleading. 'Bypassing provider permissions' more precisely means results use the admin's permissions instead of the requesting user's.
reviews.fix_sketch: In user-context calls (user_id present), stop falling back to the tenant credential for mail sources. Only search Outlook and Gmail with the requesting user's own grant. For files, allow the tenant token only when the query is scoped to org-owned storage roots (the tenant's SharePoint library or Shared Drive root folder), never global driveItem search. Change _connected_providers to report per-source availability (mail requires a user grant). Have the admin test search use the admin's own user token and label results accordingly. Replace the Hub 'mailbox boundary' step with text describing the real control. Add tests showing that a user without a grant gets no outlook/gmail hits and no /me fetch.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_search.py:1553-1578 (current lines; claim's 1516-1543 have shifted): _get_google_token and _get_microsoft_token try get_fresh_user_token, then fall back to get_fresh_token(db, tenant_id, provider). token_vault.py:413-435 get_fresh_token loads the active TenantCredential. routers/integrations.py:586-641 shows that row holds the authorization_code (delegated) token of the admin who connected (granted_by_user_id=admin_user_id). integrations.py:242-258: admin scopes include Mail.Read, Files.ReadWrite.All and Sites.Read.All on Microsoft, and gmail.readonly and drive on Google, so /me is the admin. rag.py:344-376 _connected_providers counts any active TenantCredential as connected for every user. rag.py:1842 and 1880-1893 call cloud_search_service.search and then fetch_contents with the requesting user_id. chat.py:2625-2645 runs hybrid_rag_query for every chat user, with include_private=not public_general. config.py:569 has CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED=True by default. cloud_search.py:898-1027 _search_graph POSTs /search/query with entityTypes ['message'] and ['driveItem','listItem'] using the fallback token. cloud_search.py:1367-1395 _fetch_outlook_content GETs /me/messages/{id}/$value (full MIME). cloud_search.py:761-800 searches Gmail /users/me/messages, and 1178-1204 fetches format=full. search() adds the Gmail task whatever the matter folder scope is (cloud_search.py:208-245). _microsoft_sources_without_scoped (1783-1802) keeps 'outlook' (and 'sharepoint' when only OneDrive is scoped) in the global Graph query. A second path is matters.py:221-257: the matter Cloud Files panel calls the same search with user_id, so an unprovisioned matter runs a global drive/onedrive/sharepoint search with the admin token. The IntegrationsHub.jsx:94-101 copy admits 'does not create a separate permission boundary' and asks admins to 'Confirm the permitted site, drive, or mailbox boundary'. A grep finds no such boundary setting and no fallback opt-out in backend/app.
reviews.correction: The line numbers have drifted: the token getters are now at cloud_search.py:1553-1578, and the scoping helper is at 1783-1802. There is one partial mitigation, for Google only. google_service_account.prefer_service_account (google_service_account.py:248-286) swaps the tenant fallback for a Drive-scoped service-account token, but only when the tenant has an org Shared Drive binding and the service account can reach it. In that setup, Gmail search and fetch fail and Drive results are limited to what the service account can reach. Tenants without a Shared Drive binding (the default), and every Microsoft tenant, are fully exposed. Users who have their own grant are not affected on the live path.
reviews.fix_sketch: For user-initiated retrieval, never fall back to the tenant credential for mail. Resolve Gmail and Outlook only with the requesting user's own token (exact_user). Allow the tenant or service token for file sources only in folder-scoped searches under a matter binding the user can access (can_access_matter). Drop global driveItem/listItem/Drive searches on the tenant token. Change _connected_providers to count only per-user tokens for mail sources, so the planner never asks for gmail or outlook without a personal grant. Pass the resolved identity into fetch_content so it can't re-resolve to the admin. Show a 'Connect your account to search your mail' prompt in the UI.

title: Scheduled cloud sync indexes the admin's personal mailbox into the tenant-wide search index
claim: sync_all calls sync_outlook_mail(db, tenant_id) with no user_id (cloud_sync.py:153-160), so _get_token uses the tenant (admin) delegated token and /me/messages is the admin's mailbox (cloud_sync.py:725-830); the 200 newest subjects, participants and 500-char bodyPreview are upserted into cloud_metadata_index. The Gmail path does the same for the admin's last 7 days of mail (cloud_sync.py:128-134, 455-568; also noted in google#D1 and sync#D1). search_index filters only on tenant_id and provider/object_type (cloud_search.py:471-507) with no owner ACL, RAG calls it for every user (rag.py:1889-1905), and the scheduler runs it on an interval (scheduler.py:804-810). Partner/HR/privileged mail subjects and snippets become retrievable by every user.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_sync.py:152-159: sync_all runs sync_outlook_mail(db, tenant_id) with no user_id. The Gmail call at 128-134 does the same. _get_token (833-864) falls back to get_fresh_token, the admin's delegated grant (integrations.py:584-611, with Mail.Read at 241-243). sync_outlook_mail (738-826) pages /me/messages, keeps the 200 newest, and upserts subject, participants and a 500-char bodyPreview into cloud_metadata_index. sync_gmail_metadata (468-563) does the same for the last 7 days of /users/me/messages, using snippet and headers. The scheduler registers cloud-sync every CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN=15 minutes when CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED=True, and both are defaults (scheduler.py:804-813, config.py:569 and 583). run_cloud_sync (scheduler.py:1740-1776) calls sync_all for every tenant with an active credential. search() always appends search_index (cloud_search.py:322-331). _search_index_impl (444-507) filters only on tenant_id and provider/object_type, with no owner or ACL check, and adds a matter-scope condition only when a matter_cloud_folder is passed. RAG reaches it for every user (rag.py:1889-1905).
reviews.correction: The Gmail half does not apply to tenants with an SA-bound org Shared Drive. For those, cloud_sync._get_token swaps in the Drive-only service-account token (cloud_sync.py:859-861), so Gmail listing fails. Matter-scoped chats restrict the index to the matter scope, so the leak appears in general (non-matter) chats. In practice it is worse than stated: an indexed Outlook hit is then passed to fetch_content. For a user without a personal Microsoft grant, that call downloads the full message body through the same admin token (cloud_search.py:1329-1358).
reviews.fix_sketch: Remove mail sync from the tenant-credential sync_all path. Index mail only per user, with the user's own token, into rows that carry owner_user_id (a new nullable column and migration). Filter search_index email rows to owner_user_id == requesting user. Add a data migration or one-off job that deletes existing object_type='email' rows created by tenant syncs. Add tests showing sync_all performs no /me/messages calls and that search_index hides other users' email rows.

reviews.evidence: cloud_sync.py:113-160: sync_all calls sync_gmail_metadata(db, tenant_id) and sync_outlook_mail(db, tenant_id) with no user_id. cloud_sync.py:843-874 _get_token then falls back to get_fresh_token (the admin's delegated grant, per integrations.py:586-641). cloud_sync.py:735-841 GETs /me/messages sorted receivedDateTime desc, capped at MAX_EMAILS=200 (line 60), and upserts subject, from/to/cc and bodyPreview[:500] as object_type='email'. cloud_sync.py:465-578 does the same for Gmail: last 7 days, headers plus snippet. _upsert (876-930) keys rows on tenant only, with no owner or user column. cloud_search.py:441-500 _search_index_impl filters only on tenant_id and (provider, object_type). search() always appends search_index, whatever the user's token (cloud_search.py:319-330). scheduler.py:804-815 schedules run_cloud_sync every CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN (default 15, config.py:583) when CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED (default True). scheduler.py:1740-1776 runs it for every tenant with an active TenantCredential. rag.py:1880-1893 reaches this from any user's chat. Even users who have their own grant get the snippets: _fetch_outlook_content (cloud_search.py:1375-1395) falls back to hit.snippet when their own token can't open the admin's message id. A user with no grant gets the full MIME through the admin token.
reviews.correction: The exposure is limited to searches that are not matter-scoped. When matter_cloud_folder is set, _matter_metadata_scope_condition (cloud_search.py:1704-1757) admits only file and sharepoint_file rows, so email rows are dropped. General chats pass matter_cloud_folder=None (chat.py:2455-2457), as do matters without a cloud_folder, and those do see the tenant-wide email rows. The indexed content is subject, participants and at most 500 chars of preview per message. On Google tenants with a working Shared Drive service-account binding, prefer_service_account returns a Drive-only token, so the Gmail sync fails there.
reviews.fix_sketch: Remove Gmail and Outlook mail from the tenant-wide sync_all. If mail indexing is kept, run it per user with exact per-user tokens and store owner_user_id on cloud_metadata_index rows. Filter email rows in search_index to owner_user_id == requesting user. Add a migration that purges existing object_type='email' rows (following the AGENTS.md migration head protocol), and cover it with a test that one user's mail rows never reach another user.

title: Task calendar pushes write every assignee's deadlines into the connecting admin's calendar
claim: google_calendar._get_token (google_calendar.py:18-38) and microsoft_calendar._get_token (microsoft_calendar.py:23-44) return the tenant (admin) token whenever the assignee has no per-user token or its refresh fails, because upsert_task_event does not pass exact_user. push_task_to_calendars fires upsert_task_event to both providers for every dated task (task_notifications.py:270-317), so events land in the admin's /me/events or primary calendar (microsoft_calendar.py:132-181). Titles/descriptions include matter and client names. The assignee gets nothing, revocation is masked, and the admin's calendar (and anyone it is shared with) sees other lawyers' matters, including walled ones.

reviews.evidence: google_calendar.py:18-38 and microsoft_calendar.py:23-44: `_get_token` tries get_fresh_user_token, then returns get_fresh_token (the tenant credential) unless exact_user=True. upsert_task_event calls `_get_token(tenant_id, user_id)` with no exact_user (google_calendar.py:89, microsoft_calendar.py:133), then POSTs or PATCHes /me/events (microsoft_calendar.py:171,177) or calendars/primary/events (google_calendar.py:136-147). The tenant credential is the admin's delegated grant: integrations.py:584-619 (MS) and 806-838 (Google) store granted_by_user_id=admin, and MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES and GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES include Calendars.ReadWrite and auth/calendar (integrations.py:241-252), so these writes succeed. push_task_to_calendars (task_notifications.py:270-317) fires both providers for every dated task. The user is the assignee, falling back to the creator (task_notifications.py:53-55). It is called from notify_task_created (473) and notify_task_updated (515). The only guards are the demo-tier check and the SMS check; there is no config flag. A failed per-user refresh returns None (token_vault.py:466-469), so the push falls back to the admin, which masks revocation. exact_user is used only by revocation cleanup (test_sms_unit.py:179-254).
reviews.correction: Some details are overstated. (1) Event titles do not include matter names: push_task_to_calendars never passes matter_name (the kwargs at task_notifications.py:292-306), so the subject is just the task title. Descriptions contain task.description plus 'Customer: <contact>', and the customer line appears only on the create path (473-480); the update path at 515 passes no customer_name. (2) 'Including walled ones' is overstated. Only an admin can do the admin connect, and matter_access_predicate gives admins every matter (matter_access.py:30-37), so the admin can already see them. The real exposure is to people who share or delegate the admin's calendar, and to a granting user who later loses the admin role. (3) Events only appear for providers that have a tenant credential. The core is real: the assignee gets nothing, events land in the admin's calendar, and revocation is hidden. IntegrationsPanel.jsx:959-962 now tells admins that calendar features 'act as' the connecting admin, but nothing tells the assignee.
reviews.fix_sketch: In both upsert_task_event functions, call _get_token(tenant_id, user_id, exact_user=True) whenever user_id is set, and skip the push when user_id is None, so there is never a silent tenant fallback. Log or surface a 'connect your calendar' state for users with no token or a revoked one. Keep the tenant fallback in delete_task_event (or run a one-off cleanup job) so events already written to the admin's calendar are removed: search clarity_task_id events on the admin calendar for tasks not assigned to that admin. Add tests for no-user-token -> no event, and revoked-token -> no event.

reviews.evidence: google_calendar.py:18-38 and microsoft_calendar.py:23-44: _get_token returns the tenant token unless exact_user is set. token_vault.py:470-473 get_fresh_user_token returns None when a refresh fails, so a revoked grant also falls back silently. microsoft_calendar.py:107-177 upsert_task_event calls _get_token(tenant_id, user_id) without exact_user and writes to /me/events. The Google equivalent (google_calendar.py upsert_task_event, around line 89) posts to calendars/primary/events. task_notifications.py:268-317 push_task_to_calendars fires both providers for every task with a due_date, with user_id = assignee or creator (task_notifications.py:53-55). Callers are at task_notifications.py:473-480 (create) and 515-517 (update). The only guards are demo-notification suppression and SMS-task exclusion (task_notifications.py:464-470, 497-503). There is no matter-wall or restricted-matter withholding. An exact-user variant already exists but only the SMS cleanup uses it (require_exact_user=True at task_notifications.py:340-356; google_calendar.py:174-181; microsoft_calendar.py:206-213).
reviews.correction: The event subject does not include the matter name. push_task_to_calendars never passes matter_name (task_notifications.py:286-301), so the subject is the task title (which users may still write with a matter reference). The description carries the task description, 'Customer: <contact>' (create path only) and the task link. The 'walled matters' angle is overstated for the admin personally. The connecting account must be an admin (integrations.py:356-357), and admins bypass matter-access checks in the app (matter_access.py:30-37, 69-78), so they can already see these tasks. What leaks is a copy outside LawHand's access control, visible to calendar delegates or anyone the calendar is shared with, plus a functional failure: assignees silently get nothing and a revoked grant is hidden.
reviews.fix_sketch: Pass exact_user=True in upsert_task_event and delete_task_event for task pushes, reusing the existing require_exact_user path. Skip the push when the assignee has no calendar token, and surface 'connect your calendar' or a reconnect-needed state for revoked grants. Add a one-off cleanup that deletes events carrying the clarity_task_id extended property from the admin calendar.

title: Microsoft admin connect omits openid, so tier stays 'unknown' and Entra directory sync is permanently blocked
claim: MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES (integrations.py:241-244) lacks openid/profile, so the admin callback (integrations.py:568-615) receives no id_token; claims is None, detect_microsoft(None) returns ('unknown', None), and apply_detection still stamps account_detected_at (account_detect.py:184-189), so backfill_unknown_credentials skips the row forever (account_detect.py:140-141). capabilities._directory_sync returns unavailable for an unknown tier (capabilities.py:98-103) and user_sync._directory_sync_blocked turns every Microsoft sync into not_applicable (user_sync.py:122-124). service_account_email is never set, so send_admin_notification never uses Graph (email_admin.py:106) and 'Granted by' is blank. Reconnecting cannot fix it; no test covers the MS admin callback token response.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/integrations.py:241-244: MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES = 'offline_access User.Read.All Mail.Read Mail.Send Files.ReadWrite.All Sites.Read.All Calendars.ReadWrite', with no openid/profile/email. _admin_scopes (355-363) only appends Teams scopes. The authorize URL (482-494) and the token request (523-534) both use this set. Microsoft v2 returns id_token only when openid is requested. Callback 568-582: id_token_raw is None, so claims=None and service_email=None. Lines 591-604 never set service_account_email. Lines 614-615 call detect_microsoft(None), which returns ('unknown', None) (account_detect.py:45-47), and apply_detection then stamps account_detected_at (account_detect.py:184-189). backfill_unknown_credentials skips any row with account_detected_at set (account_detect.py:140-141). It is called from integrations.py:1844 and admin.py:323, and neither caller ever retries. capabilities.py:94-101: tier None/'unknown' makes directory_sync unavailable with 'reconnect to confirm directory access'. user_sync.py:23-55 and 120-124: sync_microsoft_users returns not_applicable. Reconnecting takes the same path and gives the same result. email_admin.py:106 requires ms_cred.service_account_email, so Graph is skipped. IntegrationsPanel.jsx:956-958 hides the 'Granted by' line (it is omitted rather than blank). A grep of tests shows no MS admin-callback token-response test. test_google_onboarding_callback.py covers only Google admin and MS user cancellation. Also, the admin scopes lack User.Read, so the legacy /organization backfill may not work either.
reviews.correction: Minor: 'Granted by' is hidden rather than shown blank, because the UI renders it only when service_account_email is set. Everything else holds.
reviews.fix_sketch: Request 'openid profile email' (and User.Read) on the MS admin authorize and token calls. Keep them in a separate MICROSOFT_ADMIN_OIDC_SCOPES constant so the status endpoint's missing_scopes audit (integrations.py:1854, which uses MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES as required) does not flag every existing tenant for reconnect. Verify the id_token with the existing verify_microsoft_id_token instead of decoding base64 without verification. In the callback, if claims are missing or the tier is 'unknown', call account_detect.backfill_microsoft(access_token), and do not stamp account_detected_at for an 'unknown' result (or let backfill_unknown_credentials retry unknown rows with a backoff). Add a one-off data repair (Alembic migration pinned to the current head) that clears account_detected_at for microsoft rows with account_type='unknown'. Add callback tests for token responses with and without id_token.

reviews.correction: The claim is accurate for origin/main, where it is high: every Microsoft 365 tenant is stuck at tier 'unknown' with directory sync blocked. Commit 672b240 on the current branch HEAD fixes it but is not yet on origin/main. The admin authorize and token requests now include openid email profile, and the callback records the tier only when id_token claims exist. That makes 'reconnecting cannot fix it' false on HEAD, because re-authorizing now overwrites the stuck tier. 'No test covers it' is also false on HEAD: backend/tests/test_microsoft_admin_identity.py was added. One gap remains: tenants already stamped account_type='unknown' with account_detected_at set stay stuck until an admin re-authorizes. No data migration or backfill change resets them, and backfill_unknown_credentials still skips any row with account_detected_at set. Also, on both main and HEAD the MS id_token is base64-decoded without signature verification (integrations.py:595-600). That is acceptable under OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 because the token comes directly from the token endpoint over TLS with the client secret, but it differs from the Google path, which verifies.
reviews.evidence: origin/main backend/app/routers/integrations.py:240-243 MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES has no openid. At origin/main 614-615, detect_microsoft(claims) and apply_detection run unconditionally. backend/app/services/account_detect.py:45-47 returns ('unknown', None) for None claims. 184-189 apply_detection stamps account_detected_at. 140-141 backfill skips rows where account_detected_at is set. backend/app/services/capabilities.py:95-103 makes directory_sync unavailable for tier None/unknown. backend/app/services/user_sync.py:23-47 and 122-124 record not_applicable. backend/app/services/email_admin.py:106 uses Graph only when service_account_email is set. frontend/src/components/IntegrationsPanel.jsx:957 renders 'Granted by {info.service_account_email}'. HEAD: integrations.py:242-250 adds MICROSOFT_IDENTITY_SCOPES='openid email profile'. 371-375 _admin_request_scopes adds them to the authorize request (510-512) and the token request (546-558), while the audit still uses _admin_scopes (543-545). 636-643 applies detection only when claims is not None. Tests are at backend/tests/test_microsoft_admin_identity.py:90,102,134. git merge-base: 672b240 is not an ancestor of origin/main. No migration in 672b240 (git show --stat).
reviews.fix_sketch: Merge 672b240. To heal existing tenants without re-consent, let backfill_unknown_credentials retry once for provider='microsoft' rows where account_type='unknown' (Graph /organization via backfill_microsoft). Alternatively, a one-off data migration can null account_detected_at for those rows; follow the AGENTS.md migration head protocol.

title: Microsoft Auto mode stores firm matter files in the connecting admin's personal OneDrive
claim: In Auto mode an active Microsoft connection binds storage to 'onedrive' (matter_file_store.py:150-153, 199-204; integrations.py:1996-2002). Every admin connect creates the LawHand root in the admin's /me/drive via _ensure_cloud_root (integrations.py:2398-2438; cloud_init.py:148-166, 1506-1508), and all reads/writes use the tenant delegated token against /me/drive/items/{parent} (matter_file_store.py:42-56, 832, 866-871). No sharing to other firm users exists on the OneDrive path, so 'Open cloud copy'/co-authoring is access-denied for other staff; storage_root_ownership rates it at_risk but only surfaces that in onboarding, contradicting the org-owned-root design (docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:12-14, 28). When the admin leaves, is disabled or hits Conditional Access, all matter storage fails, and OneDrive retention after account deletion can destroy firm records.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/matter_file_store.py:146-210: in Auto mode (no primary_cloud_provider) with an active microsoft credential, it returns ('onedrive', True). integrations.py:2040-2046 (storage-readiness) mirrors this. integrations.py:2443-2485 _ensure_cloud_root runs after every admin connect (called at :682, :906). cloud_init.py:147-168 creates ROOT_FOLDER_NAME under the OneDrive 'root' with the tenant delegated token, and :1504-1509 shows the OneDrive URLs are /me/drive. matter_file_store.py:42-56 keeps the delegated token for Microsoft, and :869 and :925 upload to /me/drive/items/{parent}. storage_root_ownership.py:52-58 classifies legacy OneDrive as user_personal_drive (at_risk). It is surfaced only in frontend/src/pages/OnboardingWizard.jsx:517-535 and :672-680 via onboarding.py:191/273. docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:12-14 states the org-owned guarantee, and :28 rates OneDrive 'No — at risk'. REFUTING DETAIL: cloud_init.py:618-652 and :678-697 share_matter_folders invites assigned users to the OneDrive matter folder with the 'write' role through /me/drive/items/{id}/invite. It is called on background provisioning (matters.py:367), on assignment changes (matters.py:940-972), and on sync/provision/update (matters.py:3095, 3188, 3263, 3402).
reviews.correction: The statement 'No sharing to other firm users exists on the OneDrive path' is false. Matter-assigned staff receive write invites to the OneDrive matter folder, so 'Open cloud copy' and co-authoring work for them. Only unassigned staff, and cases where the best-effort invite silently failed, are denied. The custody and availability risk is real and is the default for Microsoft tenants: the root sits in the connecting admin's /me/drive, all access goes through that admin's delegated token, and the at_risk flag is shown only in the onboarding wizard. However, it is a known, documented gap. The design doc's Follow-ups list 'forbid creating business roots in /me/drive' and 'Health surfacing in the admin UI', and the doc says 'Phase 0/1 in progress', so it is not an undocumented contradiction. SharePoint also uses the delegated token (doc lines 92-93), so switching to SharePoint fixes custody but not access. The OneDrive-retention data-loss point depends on the tenant's M365 retention settings and is outside the code.
reviews.fix_sketch: (1) For business Microsoft tenants in Auto mode, stop defaulting to 'onedrive'. Require an org SharePoint binding, or block matter storage with a clear readiness state until the admin chooses. Keep OneDrive only for personal or consumer accounts, or when explicitly selected with an acknowledgment. (2) Show root_ownership.status=at_risk in the admin Integrations page, the storage-readiness response and the health banners, not only in onboarding. (3) Longer term, add app-only Graph (Sites.Selected, client_credentials) for storage tokens, and offer one-click migration from OneDrive to SharePoint through the existing storage_migration framework.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/matter_file_store.py:192-197: in Auto mode (no TenantSettings.primary_cloud_provider), an active 'microsoft' credential returns ('onedrive', True). backend/app/services/cloud_init.py:148-166 creates the root with _ensure_onedrive_folder(ms_token, ROOT_FOLDER_NAME, 'root'), and cloud_init.py:1503-1508 resolves 'root' to /me/drive/root/children, which is the connecting admin's personal drive. backend/app/routers/integrations.py:2439-2481 (_ensure_cloud_root) runs after every admin connect (called at integrations.py:678 and 902). All Microsoft storage runs on the tenant's delegated token (matter_file_store.py:42-56 says 'Microsoft paths keep the delegated token'). Uploads PUT to /me/drive/items/{parent} (matter_file_store.py:866-869) and reads use /me/drive/items or /drives/{driveId} (matter_file_store.py:273-287). root_ownership reaches only onboarding: routers/onboarding.py:191,273,280 and frontend/src/pages/OnboardingWizard.jsx:526-531. REFUTED PART: the OneDrive path does share folders. cloud_init.py:618-650 and 673-690 (share_matter_folders/_share_onedrive_folder) POST /me/drive/items/{matter_folder_id}/invite with the 'write' role for every assigned user. It is called from matters.py:185-218 (_share_matter_with_assignees), matters.py:960 (create) and matters.py:3095/3188/3263/3402 (provision/remap/context/sync). The design doc already records this limitation: docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:28 rates OneDrive 'No — at risk', lines 87-89 say 'Today the code still uses the delegated admin token', and lines 97-101 list the forbid-/me/drive and migration work as follow-ups.
reviews.correction: 'No sharing to other firm users exists on the OneDrive path' is wrong. share_matter_folders invites every assigned user to the OneDrive matter folder with write access (cloud_init.py:618-690; matters.py:185-218, 960, 3095...). So 'Open cloud copy' and co-authoring work for assignees. Only non-assigned staff (who can still reach the matter in LawHand, because matter routes are tenant-wide) get access denied, and the best-effort invite can fail silently (it only logs a warning). The 'contradiction' with the design doc is overstated: the doc itself rates OneDrive at-risk and lists the fix as a follow-up. SharePoint custody is org-owned, but access still uses the same delegated token (matter_file_store.py:42-56), so 'storage fails when the admin is disabled' applies to both Microsoft backends. What remains accurate: by default, firm matter records are held in one person's OneDrive. Their availability depends on that admin's refresh token, and the at_risk warning appears only in onboarding. OneDrive loss after account deletion depends on M365 retention settings (an external fact, not visible in the code).
reviews.fix_sketch:
1. For Microsoft business tenants, make Auto mode prefer a SharePoint site library, or require an explicit storage choice before the first matter provisioning. Refuse to create new business roots in /me/drive (the design doc follow-up).
2. Show root_ownership.status=at_risk and access_at_risk as a persistent admin health banner in IntegrationsPanel, not only in onboarding.
3. Longer term: app-only Sites.Selected for storage access, plus the documented migration of existing OneDrive roots into SharePoint.

title: Removing a matter assignee never revokes the cloud folder share granted to them
claim: Assignees are invited with write roles via /me/drive/items/{id}/invite (cloud_init.py:617-697, called from matters.py:185-218, 3095, 3188, 3263, 3402), but remove_assignment (matters.py:1772-1825) deletes the row and cleans calendars without calling DELETE .../permissions/{id}; the codebase has no unshare function. A lawyer screened off a matter keeps write access to its OneDrive/SharePoint/Drive folder indefinitely.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/matters.py:185-218 `_share_matter_with_assignees` calls `share_matter_folders` for every assignee email. It is invoked at matters.py:367 (background provisioning), 960 (matter create), 3095, 3188, 3263 and 3402. backend/app/services/cloud_init.py:618-675 grants 'write' on the OneDrive matter folder and 'writer' on the Google matter folder, plus read/reader on context folders. The grant goes through `_share_onedrive_folder` (cloud_init.py:678-695, POST /me/drive/items/{id}/invite) and `_share_gdrive_folder` (cloud_init.py:698-718, POST /files/{id}/permissions). matters.py:1772-1825 `remove_assignment` only cleans up SMS-task calendars, then runs `db.delete(assignment)` and commits (1823-1824). It makes no cloud call. Grepping backend/app for '/permissions' finds only POST (create) calls at cloud_init.py:704 and 1188. There are no DELETE or permission-revoke calls anywhere, and no other code path deletes MatterAssignment rows. native_authorization.py:106-119 shows restricted and ethical-wall matters rely on assignments, so dropping the row revokes LawHand access but leaves the cloud ACL in place.
reviews.correction: Confirmed for OneDrive and Google Drive matter folders, including read shares on context folders. The SharePoint part is overstated. `share_matter_folders` reads only cloud_folder['onedrive'] and cloud_folder['google_drive'] (cloud_init.py:636, 654), so SharePoint-bound matter folders (cloud_folder['sharepoint'], provisioned at cloud_init.py:510-534) are never shared per assignee. Access there comes from site membership, so there is no per-user grant to leak or revoke. SharePoint has a different gap: LawHand cannot screen anyone off there at all. Also note the shares are only created when the connecting account can invite. Failures are swallowed, so the exposure applies only when the invite succeeded.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add `unshare_matter_folders(db, tenant_id, cloud_folder, user_emails)` to cloud_init. For OneDrive: GET /me/drive/items/{id}/permissions (or /drives/{drive_id}/items/{id}/permissions), match grantedToV2.user.email / grantedToIdentitiesV2 / invitation.email against the emails, then DELETE /.../permissions/{perm_id}. For Google: GET /files/{id}/permissions?fields=permissions(id,emailAddress,role)&supportsAllDrives=true, then DELETE /files/{id}/permissions/{perm_id}. Apply this to the matter folder and all context_folders. Optionally store the permission IDs returned by invite/create on the assignment or in cloud_folder to skip the lookup. Call it from remove_assignment before `db.delete`. Follow the existing calendar-cleanup precedent: fail closed with a 503 if revocation is unavailable, or enqueue a durable retry job plus an audit event. Also call it on user deactivation, and when a matter becomes restricted/ethical-wall for non-assigned users. Skip a user who still holds another assignment on the same matter. Add tests that mock Graph and Drive.

reviews.evidence: Grants: cloud_init.py:633-650 builds onedrive_folder_roles ('write' on the matter folder) and google_folder_roles ('writer'). _share_onedrive_folder (cloud_init.py:673-690) POSTs /me/drive/items/{id}/invite, and _share_gdrive_folder (cloud_init.py:693-711) POSTs files/{id}/permissions. These are called for all current assignees from matters.py:185-218, 960, 3095, 3188, 3263 and 3402. Revocation: remove_assignment (matters.py:1772-1825) only cleans up SMS calendar tasks and deletes the MatterAssignment row (line 1823). It makes no provider call. A repo-wide grep for DELETE permissions, unshare or revoke-share in backend/app finds nothing; the only permissions writes are POSTs (cloud_init.py:704, 1188). Guards: none on the cloud side. Ethical-wall policy (native_authorization.py:101-148, security_policy.restricted/ethical_wall plus an assignment relationship) is enforced only in services/smb.py:1263,1556,1886 and services/file_open_intents.py:89. The design doc calls cloud sharing a 'convenience mirror … not the security boundary' (docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:15-17), but that does not revoke the provider ACL.
reviews.correction: SharePoint is overstated. share_matter_folders handles only the 'onedrive' and 'google_drive' keys (cloud_init.py:633-667), so LawHand never grants SharePoint matter-folder shares, and there is nothing of LawHand's to revoke there (SharePoint access follows site membership). The leak is real for OneDrive and Google Drive, and it goes beyond assignment removal: no path revokes shares on LawHand user deactivation or when a matter becomes ethical-wall restricted. There is also a broader gap: the main matters router authorizes only by tenant (_get_matter_or_404, matters.py:125-143; no role or assignment checks), so a removed assignee also keeps LawHand web access to unrestricted matters. The persistent cloud write grant is still direct, unaudited access outside LawHand, and it survives even where LawHand enforces the wall (SMB/file-open intents).
reviews.fix_sketch:
1. At invite time, persist the returned permission IDs per user and folder (Graph invite returns permission objects; Drive returns permission.id).
2. In remove_assignment, user deactivation and the transition to restricted/ethical_wall, delete those permissions: DELETE /drives/{driveId}/items/{id}/permissions/{permId} for OneDrive, DELETE files/{id}/permissions/{permId}?supportsAllDrives=true for Drive. For legacy grants, fall back to listing permissions and matching the user's email.
3. Make revocation fail-visible, like the calendar cleanup: either block the removal with a 503, or enqueue a durable retry plus an admin alert. Add an audit event.

title: Editing a matter document in Word/Drive (as the UI invites) permanently breaks LawHand access with a 409
claim: Download reads cloud bytes with expected_size=doc.file_size (matter_documents.py:750-806) and read_matter_file_bytes enforces the stored size (matter_file_store.py:233-242, 1543-1551), so any edit via the 'Open in OneDrive/Google Drive' link (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1139-1147, 1278-1287) raises an integrity error, marks storage_state='conflict' and 409s every later download. E-sign creation reads with the same check (esignature.py:449-456). Folder sync never updates MatterDocument size/hash and only task-bound AI drafts have an adopt endpoint (tasks.py:1906), while the upload toast says 'Edits happen in the firm's cloud copy' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-444). Edited documents can no longer be downloaded, signed or fed to AI.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/matter_documents.py:750-806: the download endpoint returns 409 immediately if storage_state=='conflict' (763-767). Otherwise it calls read_matter_file_bytes with expected_size=doc.file_size (772-778). On MatterFileIntegrityError it sets storage_state='conflict' and commits, then raises 409 'The cloud document changed and must be reconciled' (779-806). backend/app/services/matter_file_store.py:207-306: persisted_size defaults to document.file_size (enforce_persisted_size=True), and `_validate_read_integrity` (1543-1551) raises MatterFileIntegrityError on any length mismatch. MatterFileIntegrityError subclasses MatterFileReadError (127). esignature.py:450-456 reads with expected_size=doc.file_size. matter_workspace_capabilities.py:681-690 (agent document read) uses the default persisted-size enforcement and maps the error to 'document_unavailable'. matter_fact_extraction.py:445-449 refuses conflict docs outright. MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1139-1147 and 1278-1287 link to doc.cloud_url ('Open' / 'Open in OneDrive'), and 440-444 shows the toast "Edits happen in the firm's cloud copy." cloud_sync.py:876-890 upserts only into cloud_metadata_index, never MatterDocument. The only places storage_state becomes 'verified' again are cloud_artifact_materialization.py:652 and tasks.py:2031, both part of the task-bound AI-draft flow (sync-cloud endpoint at tasks.py:1905-1906). workflow_runs reconcile-cloud and storage_migration reconcile cover other objects. MatterDocumentsTab.jsx has no handling for conflict or storage_state.
reviews.correction: Accurate. One small nuance: for Google Drive, the 'Open' link opens the DOCX in Drive, and only an in-place Office-compatibility edit rewrites it. 'Open with Google Docs' creates a separate copy and leaves the original alone. For OneDrive and SharePoint, Word for the web saves in place, so the claim holds fully. Also, document-text/AI reads fail with a generic 'unavailable' error rather than a 409.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add a reconcile path for ordinary (non-artifact) matter documents. On a size or hash mismatch where doc.generated_artifact_id is null and the document is not approval-bound, re-read provider metadata (eTag/cTag, size, sha256Checksum/quickXorHash) by provider_object_id. If the object is still in the matter folder, adopt the new version: update file_size, document_sha256, provider_etag/version_id and provider_modified_at, invalidate the text cache, and append an integrity/audit event. Reserve hard 'conflict' for approval-bound generated artifacts. Add POST /matters/{id}/documents/{doc_id}/reconcile that does this explicitly for docs already stuck in 'conflict', and show a 'Refresh from cloud' action plus a conflict badge in MatterDocumentsTab. Optionally let the download endpoint adopt automatically when only non-evidentiary metadata changed. If auto-adopt is rejected, change the upload toast so it stops inviting cloud edits.

reviews.evidence: Upload persists file_size=len(file_bytes) and leaves storage_state NULL (matter_documents.py:566; models column matter_document.py:145,168). download_matter_document (matter_documents.py:750-822) returns 409 when storage_state=='conflict'. Otherwise it calls read_matter_file_bytes(expected_size=doc.file_size), and on MatterFileIntegrityError it sets storage_state='conflict' and commits. read_matter_file_bytes enforces the persisted size by default (matter_file_store.py:231-248, enforce_persisted_size=True), and _validate_read_integrity raises on a length mismatch (matter_file_store.py:1543-1560). E-sign creation reads with expected_size=doc.file_size and returns 409 on integrity errors (esignature.py:450-482). AI paths also fail: matter_fact_extraction.py:445-470 rejects conflict docs and otherwise reads with the default size enforcement; the MCP get_matter_document_text read (matter_workspace_capabilities.py:681-690) returns document_unavailable. Folder sync only upserts CloudMetadata rows (cloud_sync.py:876-930) and never touches MatterDocument size, hash or state. The only paths that set storage_state back to 'verified' are artifact materialization (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:652) and the task-bound sync-cloud adopt (tasks.py:1904-2031). UI: an 'Open'/'Open in {provider}' link goes to doc.cloud_url (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1139-1146, 1278-1287), and the upload toast says 'Edits happen in the firm's cloud copy.' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-444).
reviews.correction: Minor overstatements. The document is not lost or inaccessible: the cloud copy stays openable through cloud_url and the /open endpoint (matter_documents.py:720-747 resolves the URL with no integrity check). Only LawHand byte reads break: download, e-sign and AI extraction. Only the download path persists 'conflict'; e-sign and AI fail with 409 or unavailable without marking it. For unverified plain uploads, only the size is checked (the SHA is checked only when storage_state=='verified'), so a byte-identical-size edit would pass, though any real DOCX edit changes the size.
reviews.fix_sketch:
1. Add a 'Refresh from cloud' reconcile endpoint for ordinary MatterDocuments, reusing the sync-cloud adopt machinery: read the current provider bytes, re-run safety inspection, record the new file_size, SHA-256, eTag and version, write a document integrity event, and clear the conflict.
2. Expose it in MatterDocumentsTab next to documents in the conflict state, with a clear message instead of a bare 409.
3. Alternatively, for non-evidence-bound uploads, detect a provider eTag or cTag change at read time and auto-adopt it as a new version.
4. Fix the toast copy until then.

title: Template/agent DOCX drafts default to plain-text edit mode; a save flattens formatting and truncates at 50k chars
claim: propose_document_from_template and propose_matter_document_file build MatterDocumentDraftAction without document_edit_mode (chat_tools/handlers.py:1835-1850), so it defaults to 'lawhand_text' (schemas/chat_action.py:439); only the cloud-sync path sets 'office_snapshot' (tasks.py:2109). A text save (tasks.py:1806-1835) creates a revision from the extracted preview (capped at 50k chars) and re-renders via render_revision_docx with python-docx default styles (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:260-270, 435-440). This contradicts docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:489-491 (snapshots stay read-only so a save cannot flatten formatting). A typo fix strips letterhead, tables, headers/footers and drops content past ~50k chars, and approval binds to the damaged DOCX. Behind WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED/workflow runs.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/chat_tools/handlers.py:1271-1305 (propose_document_from_template) and 1308-1355 (propose_matter_document_file) pass source_docx_bytes into _propose_matter_document_impl. It builds MatterDocumentDraftAction at 1835-1851 without document_edit_mode, so the default applies: schemas/chat_action.py:439 `document_edit_mode ... = "lawhand_text"`. Only the sync-cloud path sets 'office_snapshot' (tasks.py:2109). In the save endpoint, tasks.py:1806-1835 blocks only when document_edit_mode=='office_snapshot'. Otherwise it creates a revision from bound_action.body and calls materialize without source_docx_bytes. cloud_artifact_materialization.py:434-439 then uses render_revision_docx (259-270), which starts from a fresh python-docx Document() with a heading and Markdown paragraphs, so letterhead, styles, tables and headers/footers are lost. The preview is capped by cloud_docx_snapshot.py:27 DEFAULT_REVIEW_PREVIEW_CHARS=50_000 and gets a truncation marker at 113-118. No backend guard blocks saving a truncated preview (grep for preview_truncated shows it is only propagated). Frontend DocumentDraftWorkspace.jsx:85 `textEditable = !approved && !officeSnapshot`, TaskBoard.jsx:1062-1063 derives officeSnapshot from document_edit_mode, and previewTruncated (line 171) only shows a warning. docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:489-491 states adopted Office snapshots are read-only 'so a save cannot flatten the original formatting'. Reachability: both tools have audiences=('workspace_mcp',) (automation_capabilities.py:565-596), and propose_document_from_template is also in the workflow-run contract (workflow_run_contract.py:34). The workflow_runs router is mounted unconditionally (main.py:578). WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED defaults to False (config.py:423).
reviews.correction: Accurate. Scope: Markdown templates are unaffected because they render with source_docx_bytes=None through the same text renderer (document_template_workspace.py:333-348), so only DOCX templates and pushed DOCX files flatten. The previous -r1 file is kept in the cloud as 'superseded' and not deleted, so the original bytes can be recovered, but approval binds to the flattened revision.
reviews.fix_sketch: In _propose_matter_document_impl, set document_edit_mode='office_snapshot' whenever source_docx_bytes is not None, so both template-DOCX and pushed-file drafts stay read-only in the text editor and are edited in Word, then adopted via sync-cloud. The frontend already honours office_snapshot. As a backend belt-and-braces check, also reject text saves in tasks.py when document_preview_truncated is true, or when the bound revision's integrity event or operation shows source_mode=='external_cloud_docx_snapshot'. That check also covers tasks already pending with the wrong mode. Add regression tests for both tools and the 409.

reviews.evidence: handlers.py:1271-1306 (propose_document_from_template) and handlers.py:1309-1355 (propose_matter_document_file) pass source_docx_bytes into _propose_matter_document_impl. That function builds MatterDocumentDraftAction at handlers.py:1835-1851 without setting document_edit_mode, so the schema default 'lawhand_text' applies (schemas/chat_action.py:439). Only sync-cloud adoption sets 'office_snapshot' (tasks.py:2095-2110). The text-save path at tasks.py:1806-1835 rejects only office_snapshot. It then creates a revision from bound_action.body and calls materialize() without source_docx_bytes. Materialization then renders from text with render_revision_docx (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:436-440): a python-docx default Document() plus a heading (lines 260-273). The body is snapshot.review_text, capped at DEFAULT_REVIEW_PREVIEW_CHARS=50_000 with a '[Preview truncated…]' marker (cloud_docx_snapshot.py:27,35,120-127). Truncation does not block the save, and the save hard-codes document_preview_truncated False (tasks.py:1853-1866). The frontend gates editing only on office_snapshot (TaskBoard.jsx:1062-1063; DocumentDraftWorkspace.jsx:85,135,175), so a truncated or formatted template draft is shown as an 'Editable draft'. The docs promise that an adopted Office snapshot is read-only so a save cannot flatten formatting (docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:489-491). Guards: WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED defaults to False (config.py:423). Both capabilities have audiences=('workspace_mcp',) (automation_capabilities.py:565-596). propose_document_from_template is also in the automation service-identity grant list (automation_service_contract.py:23). Saving requires _require_action_reviewer_or_approver and status=='review' (tasks.py:1761-1768). The prior document is marked 'superseded', not deleted (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:661-676).
reviews.correction: The impact is a little narrower than stated. The feature is behind a default-off flag (or an automation service identity granted the template capability), and a reviewer or approver has to actively edit and save. The original formatted DOCX is kept as a superseded MatterDocument and artifact revision, so it can be recovered rather than permanently destroyed. Review is reset, so the flattened DOCX needs re-review, but approval then binds to the flattened bytes if the reviewer does not notice. Markdown templates are unaffected because they have no source DOCX.
reviews.fix_sketch:
1. In _propose_matter_document_impl, set document_edit_mode='office_snapshot' whenever source_docx_bytes is not None.
2. In the tasks.py text-save path, also refuse saves (409) when document_preview_truncated is true.
3. The frontend already honors office_snapshot by showing a read-only view plus 'Refresh edits from cloud'.
4. Add tests covering DOCX-template and pushed-file proposals, and backfill existing pending actions that carry a source-DOCX lineage.

title: /api/email/scan lets any user scan another user's mailbox via body.user_id
claim: email_agent.py:31-65 sets user_id = str(user.id) if not body.user_id else body.user_id with no admin or ownership check; process_emails then loads that user's delegated mail token (email_agent.py:348-364). A paralegal can POST {user_id: partnerId} and receive the partner's inbox subjects, senders, AI summaries and drafted replies, and the scan writes notes/tasks attributed to the partner (IDOR).

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/email_agent.py:31-33 sets user_id = str(user.id) if not body.user_id else body.user_id, and nothing checks role or ownership. The value goes straight to process_emails (router :53-65) and is echoed back at :79-84. backend/app/schemas/email_agent.py:22 exposes user_id as an optional client-supplied field. backend/app/services/email_agent.py:348-360 calls ms_read_mail_user or gmail_read_mail with that user_id. token_vault.py:438-460 and _locked_user_token :213-231 look up UserOAuthToken by (user_id, tenant_id, provider) only, so any same-tenant user's delegated token is used. Results at :405-414 return subject, sender, AI summary and draft reply. _auto_log_and_task (:46, :87, :99, :123) writes the CommunicationLog, MatterNote and tagged task with created_by, author and actor set to the victim's uid. No middleware guards /api/email: module_guard.py and addon_guard.py have no email rules, and demo_quota.py:62-83 only blocks demo tenants. The frontend never sends user_id (frontend/src/api.js:1941-1942), so the field is dead UI surface reachable only by a direct API call. No test covers it: backend/tests/test_demo_outbound_guard.py covers demo blocking only.
reviews.correction: The core claim holds. Scope is narrower than 'the partner's inbox': process_emails drops any message whose sender is not a contact on an active matter (email_agent.py:370-375), so the attacker gets the victim's matter-linked mail, not every message. The victim must also have a connected per-user Microsoft or Google token, and access is limited to the same tenant. Additional aggravation: privacy_mode and premium eligibility come from the attacker (router :46, :63), so the victim's mail can reach the LLM without the PII scrubbing the victim enabled (guardrails.py:72-84).
reviews.fix_sketch: In scan_emails, stop honouring an arbitrary body.user_id. Either remove user_id from EmailScanRequest, or add `if body.user_id and body.user_id != str(user.id): raise HTTPException(403)`. A delegated token should only ever be used by its owner, so there is no legitimate admin-on-behalf case. Add a router test asserting 403 when user_id names another user. Optionally apply the same review to other endpoints that accept a user_id and resolve delegated tokens.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/email_agent.py:26-34: POST /api/email/scan calls get_current_user and then sets user_id = str(user.id) if not body.user_id else body.user_id. It has no role, admin or ownership check. backend/app/schemas/email_agent.py (EmailScanRequest) accepts user_id: str | None from the request body. backend/app/services/email_agent.py:348-364: process_emails calls ms_read_mail_user or gmail_read_mail with that user_id. microsoft_mail.py:19-50 then loads that user's delegated token through get_fresh_user_token and reads /me/messages. token_vault.py:213-231 filters the token row only by tenant_id + user_id + provider, so a cross-tenant request is blocked but any user in the same tenant can be targeted. services/email_agent.py:366-375: only messages whose sender is a contact linked to an open matter are kept (_match_email_to_matters, 143-193), so the returned set is exactly the victim's client/matter correspondence. Lines 376-394 classify each message and draft a reply. Lines 396-403, together with 79-110, write a CommunicationLog (created_by_user_id=victim) and a MatterNote (author_id=victim) into every matched matter. Lines 405-412 and router lines 67-84 return the subject, sender, received time, AI summary and draft reply to the caller. Neither the router nor the service checks the caller's matter access or ethical walls. The router also applies the caller's privacy_mode and premium route (router 44-65) to the victim's mail. The only other guard found is backend/app/middleware/demo_quota.py:72-74, which blocks /api/email/ in demo workspaces. The frontend has no caller (only backend/tests reference /api/email/scan), so exploitation is by direct API call with any valid session.
reviews.correction: The claim is accurate, with two refinements. (1) The caller does not get the whole inbox, only messages from contacts linked to active matters. Those are the most sensitive messages (privileged client correspondence), and they include matters the caller may be walled off from. (2) The exposure is intra-tenant only, because the token lookup is tenant-scoped. There is also a third effect: the victim's privacy_mode is ignored because the caller's flag is used, so mail from a privacy-mode user can go to a non-private LLM route.
reviews.fix_sketch: Remove body.user_id from EmailScanRequest, or ignore it unless it equals the caller. If an admin-on-behalf mode is truly needed, require _require_admin, check that the target is in the same tenant and is active, and write an audit log entry. Add a test in which a non-admin passes another user's id and gets 403 or has the id ignored.

title: Moved or renamed matter key dates leave stale events on Outlook/Google calendars
claim: Key-date pushes (calendar_sync.py:519-628) store no provider event id and dedupe on (subject, start date) read back from the provider. When a key date moves or the matter is renamed, a new event is created and the old one is never updated or deleted, so lawyers see the old court date beside the new one (missed-deadline risk).

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/calendar_sync.py:519-548 _existing_synced_keys builds a set of (subject, start[:10]) read back from the provider, and its docstring (527-533) says "nothing local records which events a previous run created". Lines 593-628 create a new event with subject f"[LawHand] {label}: {matter.matter_name}" at 09:00 and only increment a counter. The returned provider id is discarded, there is no extended-property tag (unlike task pushes in microsoft_calendar.py:153-160 and google_calendar.py:126-130), and there is no PATCH or DELETE path. A grep for "[LawHand]" finds only line 596, so nothing cleans these events up. backend/app/schemas/matter.py:88 and :117 let MatterUpdate change matter_name and key_dates, and routers/matters.py:1476 applies them with setattr. A moved date gives a new (subject, date) key and a renamed matter gives a new subject. Either way a second event is created on the next sync and the old one stays. Pushes happen only when the user clicks Sync: routers/calendar.py:86-94 checks sync_deadlines, which defaults to False (schemas/calendar.py:60), and CalendarPage.jsx:750 handleSync is the caller. The 5-minute poll passes false (CalendarPage.jsx:615). The test at tests/test_calendar_sync.py:478-531 covers only an exact repeat with an unchanged date and name.
reviews.correction: The details are accurate. Scope note: key-date events are pushed only when a user clicks Sync manually (the background poll never pushes). This makes things worse: if a user moves a date and does not re-sync, the provider calendar shows only the old date. Deleted key dates and closed matters also leave their events behind.
reviews.fix_sketch: Tag each key-date event with a stable marker such as clarity_key_date=<matter_id>:<label>: a Google private extendedProperty or a Graph singleValueExtendedProperty (reuse the CLARITY_TASK_PROP pattern with a new GUID). The alternative is a small table (tenant, user, provider, matter_id, label, external_event_id). On sync, look up by marker: PATCH when the date or subject changed, and DELETE marked events whose matter/label no longer exists, is closed, or is outside the window. Add a one-time cleanup that matches legacy untagged "[LawHand] label: name" events. Add tests for a moved date, a rename and a removed key date.

reviews.correction: The mechanism is real. The impact is overstated. The next manual sync also pushes the moved date (within the 90-day window), so the lawyer sees duplicate or contradictory events rather than losing the correct one, and LawHand's own calendar stays authoritative. Push only happens on an explicit user 'Sync' action. Medium fits better than high, and there is no cross-tenant exposure. The claim misses three problems. First, closed matters (filtered out at line 564) and removed key dates are never cleaned up. Second, provider reads cap at 100 events with no pagination, so dedupe fails on busy calendars and re-sync creates duplicates of unchanged dates. Third, a user editing the event title in Outlook or Google causes a duplicate on the next sync. Adjacent privacy note: the sync pushes key dates for every open matter in the tenant with no matter_access check. Every staff member who syncs gets all firm matter names on their provider calendar, and an admin can target another user's calendar (calendar.py:64-68). That matches the tenant-wide list_matters and /calendar/events, but not the owner/assignment/admin model in services/matter_access.py that tasks and SMS use.
reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/calendar_sync.py:519-548 _existing_synced_keys builds (subject, start[:10]) from provider reads, and its docstring says 'nothing local records which events a previous run created'. 550-630 sync_deadlines_to_calendar selects all tenant matters with ~Matter.is_closed (561-566). The subject is '[LawHand] {label}: {matter_name}' (596). It only creates events via ms_create_event/google_create_event, stores no returned id (only already_synced.add at 628), and has no update or delete path. calendar_sync.py:108 uses '$top': 100 and 347 uses 'maxResults': 100, with no nextLink/nextPageToken handling. Triggers: backend/app/routers/calendar.py:58-100 (run_calendar_sync, sync_deadlines flag), 316; backend/app/routers/email_agent.py:125; frontend/src/pages/CalendarPage.jsx:746-750 handleSync -> syncCalendarDeadlines(provider) (frontend/src/api.js:2301-2304). The access model at backend/app/services/matter_access.py:14-58 is not applied here. backend/app/routers/matters.py:559-560 lists matters tenant-wide.
reviews.fix_sketch: Give each pushed key-date event a stable identity, either as a mapping table (tenant, user, provider, matter_id, key_date label) -> provider event_id plus the last pushed date and subject, or as a private marker property (MS singleValueExtendedProperty like the existing CLARITY_TASK_PROP_ID task marker; Google extendedProperties.private) carrying matter_id and label. On each sync, reconcile by that identity: PATCH moved or renamed events, DELETE events for removed key dates or closed matters, and delete only events that carry the LawHand marker. Paginate provider reads. Consider scoping the push to matter_access_predicate for non-admins.

title: Date-only task events are sent to Google Calendar with an empty (end == start) range
claim: google_calendar.py:52-53 sends all-day events with end.date == start.date, but Google's end.date is exclusive, so the range is empty; the Graph path correctly adds one day (microsoft_calendar.py:83-96). The failure is only logged (google_calendar.py:159-166) inside fire-and-forget code (task_notifications.py:36-50), and the unit test encodes end == start. Most deadlines (no due time) never reach Google Calendar and nobody is told. Needs live-API confirmation.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/google_calendar.py:52-53 returns {"start": {"date": due_date}, "end": {"date": due_date}} when due_time is empty. Google's end is exclusive, so this is an empty range, which Google rejects with 400 timeRangeEmpty. The Graph builder at microsoft_calendar.py:83-96 explicitly adds one day ("All-day Graph events require an exclusive end date"). On a non-2xx response, upsert_task_event only calls logger.warning and returns None (google_calendar.py:159-166). It does not raise, so the handler in task_notifications.py:36-50 (_fire_and_log, asyncio.create_task) never fires, and task_notifications.py:308-312 fires it without awaiting a result. tests/test_task_calendar_due_time.py:97-104 asserts end == start. Date-only is the default: frontend/src/components/AddTaskModal.jsx:24 initializes due_time to '', and models/task.py:162 makes due_time nullable.
reviews.correction: The code facts are all confirmed. The 400 rejection comes from Google's documented exclusive-end semantics and the timeRangeEmpty error; I did not reproduce it against the live API. The PATCH path (google_calendar.py:137-142) fails the same way: a task whose due_time is cleared keeps its stale timed event. "Most deadlines" is plausible because due_time defaults to empty, but it is not measured. The impact is limited to tenants/users with Google connected.
reviews.fix_sketch: In _google_schedule, for the date-only case, set end = (date.fromisoformat(due_date) + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat(). Update test_google_event_stays_a_date_without_a_due_time to expect the next day. Optionally record push failures somewhere the user can see (for example a task calendar_sync_error field or a per-user integration health counter) instead of only logging.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/google_calendar.py:46-53: when there is no due_time, _google_schedule returns {'start': {'date': due_date}, 'end': {'date': due_date}}. Lines 122-131 put it into the event body. Lines 133-166 POST or PATCH it, and any non-200/201 response is only logged at warning level and returns None. backend/app/services/task_notifications.py:268-315: push_task_to_calendars passes due_time=None for date-only tasks and schedules the upsert through _fire_and_log (36-50), which swallows failures, so nothing reaches the user. backend/app/services/microsoft_calendar.py:75-96: the Graph path correctly uses an exclusive end of start + 1 day. backend/tests/test_task_calendar_due_time.py:98-102 asserts end.date == start.date, which enshrines the bug. Google's Calendar docs define end as exclusive and say a one-day all-day event must end on the next day.
reviews.correction: The code-level defect is certain. I did not exercise the live Google API rejection here, but Google documents the end date as exclusive, so an equal start and end is an empty range. Two consequences the claim omits. First, a task edited from timed to date-only is PATCHed with the invalid range, so the stale timed event stays on the calendar. Second, completing a date-only task never shows as [DONE]. This is a reliability issue, not a security or privacy exposure. LawHand remains the system of record, and task email notifications are unaffected.
reviews.fix_sketch: In _google_schedule, set end.date to (date.fromisoformat(due_date) + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat() and update test_task_calendar_due_time.py:98-102 to expect the next day. Optionally surface upsert failures, for example through record_integration_sync_run or capture_integration_error, instead of only logging them.

title: Per-user Microsoft tokens break OneDrive matter-folder search, sync and fetch because folders live in the admin's drive
claim: When a user has a personal Microsoft token it is preferred, and folder search, sync and content fetch call /me/drive/items/{adminFolderId}/... (cloud_search.py:1399-1435, esp. 1412; 1182-1184; cloud_sync.py:596-620). For an item in another user's drive Graph returns itemNotFound; _sync_graph_files logs and breaks (cloud_sync.py:1058-1064), and the matter 'Sync folder' route (matters.py:3407-3413) reports 'synced' with 0 files. Users who followed 'Connect Calendar' get empty matter cloud files and AI answers without matter documents, while unconnected users get results via the admin token. Fix requires drive-qualified paths (/drives/{driveId}/items/...).

reviews.evidence: Token choice: cloud_search._get_microsoft_token (cloud_search.py:1567-1577) and cloud_sync._get_token (cloud_sync.py:843-874) both prefer get_fresh_user_token over the tenant token. search() prefetches that token once (cloud_search.py:185-196) and passes it to folder-scoped OneDrive search (262-273). That goes through _search_graph (909-921) to _search_onedrive_folder, which calls GET /me/drive/items/{folder_id}/search (cloud_search.py:1450). On a non-200 it logs and returns [] (1463-1470). Content fetch uses /me/drive/items/{object_id}/content (cloud_search.py:1222) with the same token and falls back to the snippet. Matter folders are created with the tenant-level delegated admin token under /me/drive (cloud_init.py:1271-1285 and 1504-1508; token_vault.get_fresh_token at 413-435 is a refreshable delegated credential). OneDrive folder metadata stores no drive_id (cloud_init.py:1281-1286); only Google stores one (1306). sync_onedrive_folders uses the user-preferred token against /me/drive/items/{folder_id}/children (cloud_sync.py:606-630). _sync_graph_files breaks on a non-200 without raising (1063-1070). sync_matter_folders (167-268) is called from the Sync folder route with user_id=current_user (matters.py:3407-3413), which returns status 'synced' (3418). The Calendar page's Connect Calendar goes to /integrations/{provider}/connect?intent=user (api.js:2309-2311), which requests MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES including Files.ReadWrite.All (integrations.py:262-265). The RAG connected-source path uses the same user_id search and fetch (rag.py:1890-1905), and the matter cloud-files panel does too (matters.py:221-263).
reviews.correction: Line references have moved: the folder search URL is now cloud_search.py:1450 and the content fetch is 1222. Impact is narrower than stated. It affects only tenants whose matter storage provider is 'onedrive'; SharePoint uses drive-qualified /drives/{id} paths and Google IDs are global. It does not affect the connecting admin. LawHand-managed MatterDocument reads through matter_file_store use the tenant storage token (matter_file_store.py:274-295), so document-level features and MCP document tools keep working. The loss is in cloud search, the matter cloud-files panel and the RAG connected-source context. The local metadata index still runs, but it holds matter-folder rows only if someone synced with a working token, and content fetch for those hits still 404s for the user.
reviews.fix_sketch: Option A (small): for matter-folder-scoped OneDrive operations (folder search, folder sync, and content fetch of hits from those folders), use the tenant storage token, consistent with matter_file_store, since the folder scope is already matter-authorized. Option B (full): capture parentReference.driveId when building OneDrive matter folder metadata (cloud_init.build_matter_folder_metadata) and backfill existing matters with GET /me/drive using the admin token. Then call /drives/{driveId}/items/{id}/search, /children and /content everywhere, and record drive_id on CloudHit/CloudMetadata. Also make _sync_graph_files raise on itemNotFound, so the Sync folder route reports failure instead of 'synced' with 0 files. Add regression tests with a user token plus an admin-drive folder.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_search.py:1568-1578 _get_microsoft_token prefers get_fresh_user_token over the tenant token.
