Change MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES from Files.ReadWrite.All to Files.Read.All, and add an alias in _scope_is_granted so a stored Files.ReadWrite.All satisfies Files.Read.All. Otherwise every existing per-user row is flagged missing_scopes, because the audit is exact string match. Fix the ConnectedAccountsCard 'save' copy. Drop offline_access from the sign-in scope. Decide separately whether admin Mail.Read and the admin-mailbox index fallback should remain.

title: Google scope sets exceed what the code uses (restricted Gmail, full Drive, full Calendar), including for the per-user 'Connect Calendar' grant
claim: All Google modes request gmail.readonly and full drive (restricted scopes needing annual CASA) plus full calendar (integrations.py:245-272). Code only touches calendars/primary/events (calendar.events suffices) and mostly app-created Drive files (drive.file suffices except drives.create and whole-Drive search/sync). The per-user grant (integrations.py:260-265) is launched from a 'Connect Calendar' button (api.js:2305-2307). GOOGLE_SOLO_SCOPES only drops directory, contrary to the 'least-privilege' claim (docs/onboarding-hotfix-review-2026-09-16.md:17). Consent abandonment and verification cost result.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/integrations.py:245-272: the admin, user and solo sets all include gmail.readonly, gmail.send, calendar and drive. GOOGLE_SOLO_SCOPES differs from admin only by dropping admin.directory.user.readonly. Calendar calls hit only calendars/primary/events (google_calendar.py:102-201; calendar_sync.py:354-514), so calendar.events would suffice. But full drive is actually used: drives.create (cloud_init.py:1165), shared-drive permissions (cloud_init.py:704, 1188), allDrives search (cloud_search.py:672-680), and per-user whole-Drive download (document_sync.py:360-367). Gmail read is used for mail filing and search (cloud_sync.py:489-513, cloud_search.py:788-860, google_mail.py:29-115). The per-user grant is launched from the 'Connect Calendar' button at CalendarPage.jsx:866-871 via connectCalendarIntegration (api.js:2309-2311; the cited 2305-2307 has drifted) with intent=user, which uses GOOGLE_USER_SCOPES. ConnectedAccountsCard.jsx:1-25 now spells out the full mail, calendar and Drive grant. docs/onboarding-hotfix-review-2026-09-16.md:17 says 'least-privilege Gmail/Drive/Calendar scopes' for Personal mode. auth.py:95-98 requires the full 'calendar' scope.
reviews.correction: Mostly overstated. The restricted Gmail and full-Drive scopes back shipped features: mail filing and search, shared-drive creation and permissions, and allDrives search. The claim itself concedes that drive.file cannot cover these. Narrowing them would drop features, and the CASA burden stays as long as those features do. Two parts hold: calendar→calendar.events is a clean reduction, though both are 'sensitive' rather than restricted, so it brings no CASA saving; and the 'Connect Calendar' button launches a grant that includes Gmail and full Drive. The 'least-privilege' wording in the hotfix doc is inaccurate.
reviews.fix_sketch: Use Google incremental authorization. Have CalendarPage's 'Connect Calendar' request only calendar.events plus openid/email with include_granted_scopes=true, and request gmail.readonly/gmail.send/drive on demand when the user turns on mail filing or Drive search (or relabel the CalendarPage button 'Connect Google account' and route it to ConnectedAccountsCard). Replace 'calendar' with 'calendar.events' in all Google scope sets and in auth.py CALENDAR_REQUIRED_SCOPES, and add an alias so a stored 'calendar' satisfies 'calendar.events'. Correct docs/onboarding-hotfix-review-2026-09-16.md:17.

title: Per-user Microsoft/Google connect has no identity or tenant/domain check
claim: The user-intent callbacks store whatever account completed consent: Microsoft uses the 'common' authority (config.py:108) with no openid, no /me lookup and no comparison to the user's Entra tid/oid or email domain (integrations.py:616-646); the Google user flow requests no openid/email so no id_token/hd is available (integrations.py:779-783). connected_mail then sends approved client correspondence from whichever account was connected (connected_mail.py:350-379), so privileged mail can go out from and be captured from a personal @gmail.com/Outlook.com account.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/config.py:108: MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID defaults to 'common'. integrations.py:255-258: MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES has no openid. The user branch at integrations.py:616-646 stores the token in UserOAuthToken with no id_token, no /me call and no tid/oid/domain comparison. integrations.py:709-721: the Google authorize URL has no hd= or login_hint. GOOGLE_USER_SCOPES (260-265) has no openid/email, and the comment at 777-782 says the per-user flow deliberately has no OpenID scope. The user branch at 838-858 stores the token unchecked. _post_connect_redirect (1750-1754) performs no check either. connected_mail.py:329-379 loads the actor's UserOAuthToken and sends via _attempt_provider as that account (firm_mailbox=False). cloud_sync.py:733-743 and _get_token 855-857 read /me/messages with the user token, so mail is also captured from whichever account connected. By contrast, the admin Google flow does verify identity (790-801).
reviews.correction: No change to the core. Caveats: the Azure app registration's supported account types and the production MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID are not visible in the repo, so consumer MSA acceptance depends on deployment config. Solo tenants in Personal Google mode legitimately use @gmail.com accounts, so any check must be relative to the tenant's own credential tier/domain rather than a blanket ban on personal accounts.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add 'openid email' (and 'profile') to MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES and GOOGLE_USER_SCOPES, kept out of the audited required set. Verify the id_token with the existing verify_microsoft_id_token / verify_google_id_token. For Microsoft, require claims.tid to equal the firm's Entra tid, stored on TenantCredential from admin connect or on User.entra_tenant_id from SSO, and reject the consumer tid unless the tenant is in personal mode. For Google, require hd to equal TenantCredential.account_domain for workspace tenants and pass hd=<domain>&login_hint=<user.email> on the authorize URL. On mismatch, redirect with error=account_mismatch and store nothing. Persist the connected account email on UserOAuthToken (new column, via a migration pinned to the current head) and show it in ConnectedAccountsCard. Add callback tests for match and mismatch.

title: Capability matrix hard-codes email/calendar/cloud_storage 'ok' regardless of granted scopes
claim: capabilities.resolve() returns ok for email, calendar and cloud_storage irrespective of scopes (capabilities.py:158-175, esp. 169-171), even when Mail.Send, Calendars.ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All or Google's granularly-declined Gmail/Drive scopes are missing. The scope gap is stored (integration_observability.py:42-56) but per-user rows with missing_scopes are counted needs_reauth forever (integration_observability.py:81); feature calls 403 and return [] with only a warning (e.g. cloud_search.py:678-687); there is no include_granted_scopes or incremental per-feature request. Admin UI shows 'Available' while features silently fail.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/capabilities.py:158-175: resolve() returns _cap(True,'ok',...) for cloud_storage/email/calendar (169-171) and never reads scope_set for them. The only scope-aware entries are directory_sync (120-126) and teams (149-154). resolve() is called from admin.py:1695-1700 (/admin/permissions) and integrations.py:1886-1891 and 1979-1984 (/integrations/status). integration_observability.py:42-55 stores missing_scopes/health. Line 81: USER_TOKEN_REAUTH_HEALTH includes 'missing_scopes', and summarize_user_tokens (84-104) counts those rows as needs_reauth. Per-user rows are audited against the full GOOGLE_USER_SCOPES/MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES (integrations.py:642-644, 865), so a user who declines Gmail stays needs_reauth until they reconnect with every scope granted. cloud_search.py:683-689 logs a warning and returns [] on a non-200 Drive response. A grep for include_granted_scopes in backend/app finds nothing, and the Google authorize URL (integrations.py:741-747) only sets access_type=offline and prompt=consent. However, on the checked-out branch, frontend/src/components/IntegrationsPanel.jsx:63-78 (SCOPE_CAPABILITY) and 1088-1097 already downgrade an 'ok' capability to 'Reconnect needed / Not granted: ...' when a mapped scope appears in missing_required (commit ca6812e, not yet on origin/main). The same card also shows the Missing scope tally, and health is set to missing_scopes (admin.py:1764-1776).
reviews.correction: The backend hard-coding is real. The admin-UI part is overstated. On the current branch the admin integrations card no longer shows 'Available' for declined mail, calendar or storage scopes, because the frontend patches it from missing_required. On origin/main the capability rows do show 'Available', but the same card already lists the missing scopes and flags health as attention_needed, so the problem is a contradiction on the card rather than a silent failure. 'Forever' means until the user reconnects with every scope granted, which follows from having no per-feature optional consent. Failures are not uniformly silent: Drive search returns [] with only a log warning, but mail send reports a reconnect error.
reviews.fix_sketch: Move the SCOPE_CAPABILITY map into the backend (e.g. capabilities.py FEATURE_SCOPES = {email:[Mail.Read,Mail.Send | gmail.readonly,gmail.send], calendar:[Calendars.ReadWrite | calendar], cloud_storage:[Files.ReadWrite.All(+Sites.Read.All) | drive]}). In resolve(), return needs_reauth with a 'Not granted: X' reason when the scopes are missing, and 'unavailable' when there is no credential. Then drop the frontend downgrade shim. Optionally add include_granted_scopes=true to the Google authorize URL, and compute per-user token health per feature so that a user who deliberately declines Gmail is shown as 'partial', not needs_reauth.

title: Plugin integration detection checks scopes LawHand never requests, so OneDrive/Google Drive never show as connected
claim: plugins.py:370-390 detects onedrive only for Files.Read.All and google_drive only for drive.readonly, but the connect flows request Files.ReadWrite.All and the full drive scope (integrations.py:241-259). Scope lists are hand-copied in four places (integrations.py:241-270, admin.py:1604-1622, plugins.py:370-389, integrations.py:2031-2035). Plugin cards (PluginsPage.jsx:88, PluginPage.jsx:159) omit OneDrive/Google Drive for fully connected firms.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/plugins.py:370-389: _capabilities_from_credentials adds 'onedrive' only if 'Files.Read.All' is in the Microsoft scopes (376), and 'google_drive' only if '.../auth/drive.readonly' is in the Google scopes (384). The connect flows request 'Files.ReadWrite.All' and '.../auth/drive' instead (integrations.py:241-271: MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES, MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES, GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES, GOOGLE_SOLO_SCOPES). A grep of backend/app finds 'Files.Read.All' and 'drive.readonly' only in plugins.py. The only test fixture with Files.Read.All is a legacy one (tests/test_onboarding.py:144). The scope lists are copied in admin.py:1605-1624 (SCOPES_REQUIRED_MS/GOOGLE) and in the storage preflight (integrations.py, around 2071-2075 on HEAD; 2031-2035 on origin/main). Results feed PluginInfo.available_integrations (plugins.py:794-827, 1348-1355, 1442-1449) and are shown at PluginsPage.jsx:88 and PluginPage.jsx:159. manifest.py only declares optional_integrations (e.g. 55, 89, 102). No built-in manifest sets required_integrations, so missing_required_integrations (plugins.py:440-444) is never affected.
reviews.correction: The detection bug is real. The impact is display-only: plugin cards and pages omit onedrive/google_drive from 'Integrations'. No plugin requires either integration, so nothing is gated or blocked. Medium severity is overstated; low fits better.
reviews.fix_sketch: In plugins.py, accept the scopes LawHand actually requests: onedrive when Files.ReadWrite.All or Files.Read.All is granted, google_drive when drive, drive.readonly or drive.file is granted. Better, add one shared module (e.g. app/services/provider_scopes.py) holding the requested scope strings and a scope-to-feature map. Import it from integrations.py, admin.py, plugins.py and the storage preflight so the four copies cannot drift. Add a unit test that feeds MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES and GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES through _capabilities_from_credentials and expects onedrive/google_drive.

title: Cancelled or blocked Microsoft/Google sign-in consent renders a raw FastAPI 422 JSON page
claim: microsoft_callback (auth.py:1338-1345) and google_callback (auth.py:1572-1579) declare code: str and state: str as required with no error parameter, so a provider redirect with ?error=access_denied/consent_required fails validation before the @_redirect_refusals_to_login wrapper (auth.py:1128-1142) runs; main.py has no RequestValidationError handler and loginErrors.js has no admin-consent message. The integrations callbacks handle error correctly (integrations.py:512-516).

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/auth.py:1357-1364 (HEAD; 1338-1345 on main): microsoft_callback declares code: str and state: str with no defaults and no error parameter. google_callback at auth.py:1591-1598 is the same. _redirect_refusals_to_login (auth.py:1137-1163) uses functools.wraps and only catches HTTPException raised inside the handler. FastAPI builds query parameters from the wrapped signature, so a redirect of ?error=access_denied&state=... with no code fails RequestValidationError before the wrapper body runs. backend/app/main.py registers handlers only for HTTPException (889), MatterFileStoragePolicyError (914) and Exception (937), and none for RequestValidationError, so FastAPI's default 422 JSON is returned. The login authorize URLs use response_mode=query (auth.py around 1343) and prompt=consent (Google, around 1576), so a provider refusal arrives as query parameters. frontend/src/utils/loginErrors.js has no consent or admin-approval code. backend/tests/test_oauth_login_errors.py only exercises callbacks that include code and state. By contrast, integrations.py (around 528, 'if error or not code: return _error_redirect(...)') handles provider errors.
reviews.correction: Line numbers are shifted by about 19 on the current branch. The substance is accurate.
reviews.fix_sketch: Change both callbacks to code: str | None = None, state: str | None = None, error: str | None = None, error_description: str | None = None. At the top, if error or not code: consume or discard the state, map access_denied (and Microsoft error_subcode=cancel) to 'consent_declined', and map consent_required, admin_consent_required and AADSTS65001/90094 in error_description to 'admin_consent_required'. Return _login_error_redirect(code). Add both codes to LOGIN_ERROR_MESSAGES, for example 'Your Microsoft 365 / Google Workspace administrator must approve LawHand before you can sign in.' Add tests for the error-only query string on both providers. Optionally add a path-scoped RequestValidationError handler for /api/auth/*/callback as a safety net.

title: LawHand text save on an AI draft silently orphans Word Online edits in the superseded file
claim: When superseding, cloud_artifact_materialization.materialize() only marks the previous document 'superseded' (cloud_artifact_materialization.py:661-676) and never reads the previous cloud object's current hash/eTag, while DocumentDraftWorkspace shows 'Open cloud working copy' beside the editable textarea and 'Save as new cloud revision' (DocumentDraftWorkspace.jsx:172-175) and TaskBoard assumes 'verified' storage (TaskBoard.jsx:1064). Word edits stay in the superseded -r1.docx and are missing from the approved revision without warning.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/tasks.py:1806-1835: a text save on a lawhand_text draft calls create_generated_artifact_revision from bound_action.body, then materialize(..., supersedes_document_id=bound_action.document_id) without reading the currently bound cloud object. cloud_artifact_materialization.py:661-676 only loads the previous MatterDocument and sets document_status='superseded'. Nothing compares the provider eTag or hash of that object with document.document_sha256. frontend/src/components/chat/DocumentDraftWorkspace.jsx:172 shows 'Open cloud working copy' and 175 shows 'Save as new cloud revision' while the textarea is editable (line 85). The helper text at 170 does not warn that cloud edits are discarded. TaskBoard.jsx:1064 derives storageState 'verified' from the presence of document_id unless delivery failed, so the client never reflects that the cloud copy has diverged. A recovery path exists but is not enforced: the 'Refresh edits from cloud' button (TaskBoard.jsx:910) calls sync-cloud (tasks.py:1905-2031). The approval readback (task_automation.py:744-764) only checks the new -r2 object, so orphaned Word edits in -r1 are never detected.
reviews.correction: Accurate. The edits are not destroyed: they stay in the superseded cloud file and could be recovered manually. The 'Refresh edits from cloud' button exists, so the loss only happens when a reviewer saves text in LawHand after editing in Word without refreshing first. TaskBoard.jsx:1064 is a secondary display issue, not the cause.
reviews.fix_sketch: In the tasks.py text-save branch for artifact-bound drafts, read the bound document first with read_matter_file_bytes(expected_sha256=document.document_sha256, expected_size=document.file_size), or do a cheaper provider metadata eTag/cTag comparison against document.provider_etag. On mismatch, return 409 with code 'cloud_copy_changed' and do not supersede. Accept an explicit `discard_cloud_edits: true` flag to override, and record an integrity event when it is used. Frontend: on that 409, offer 'Refresh edits from cloud' (the existing sync-cloud) or 'Discard cloud edits and save'. Optionally derive storageState from the server document's storage_state instead of assuming 'verified'.

title: AI draft materialization requires an explicit primary_cloud_provider while uploads auto-bind
claim: cloud_artifact_materialization._configured_provider (276-295) raises CloudNotConfiguredError when the setting is blank, whereas MatterFileStore._resolve_provider_policy falls back to the active Microsoft or Google connection (matter_file_store.py:159-204). Auto-mode firms can save template documents to OneDrive but chat/MCP drafting fails with 'Choose and connect a primary tenant cloud provider'.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_artifact_materialization.py:276-295: _configured_provider reads only TenantSettings.primary_cloud_provider and raises CloudNotConfiguredError ('Choose and connect a primary tenant cloud provider before generating matter documents') when it is blank. It is called unconditionally at 432 in materialize. backend/app/services/matter_file_store.py:142-204: _resolve_provider_policy falls back to 'onedrive' when an active microsoft credential exists, else 'google_drive' (198-202). Auto is a first-class UI option (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:511 'Auto (Microsoft 365 → OneDrive, otherwise Google Drive)'; models/tenant.py:228-232 documents None as auto). Uploads, template saves and chat artifacts pass primary_cloud_provider (possibly None) to MatterFileStore (matter_documents.py:540, document_templates.py:4834, chat_artifacts.py:350). propose_matter_document uses the default audiences ('matter_chat','workspace_mcp') (automation_capabilities.py:192, 549-560), so in-app chat drafting, MCP drafting and workflow-run drafting all go through the strict path. primary_cloud_provider is only written by onboarding root selection (onboarding.py:324), SharePoint binding (cloud_admin.py:404), migration (storage_migration.py:631) and admin settings, not by OAuth connect.
reviews.correction: Accurate. The user-visible message differs from the one quoted. handlers.py:1827-1831 wraps the error as ChatToolError(code='tenant_cloud_not_configured', 'The draft could not be written and verified in tenant storage'), so chat/MCP callers see that generic text and the code. The 'Choose and connect…' string is the internal exception message.
reviews.fix_sketch: Replace _configured_provider with a shared resolver. Either reuse MatterFileStore._resolve_provider_policy or extract it into a module-level `resolve_tenant_storage_backend(db, tenant_id)` that returns the explicit setting or falls back to onedrive (active Microsoft credential) and then google_drive. Call it in materialize, then keep the existing _matter_folder_binding check so a missing matter folder for the resolved backend still fails clearly. Also update the ChatToolError message for tenant_cloud_not_configured so it says which step is missing. Add tests for Auto mode with a Microsoft connection and with a Google connection.

title: Deleting a Shared Drive matter document omits supportsAllDrives (file orphaned) and My Drive deletes bypass trash
claim: _delete_cloud_provider_object (matter_documents.py:261-289) issues DELETE files/{id} without supportsAllDrives=true, unlike the staged-cleanup path (matter_file_store.py:431-435); a Shared Drive item likely 404s, ProviderNotFound is treated as success and the DB record is removed (matter_documents.py:347-348). For My Drive, files.delete is permanent (Graph DELETE goes to the recycle bin). Deleted documents may persist in the Shared Drive, and accidental deletes cannot be recovered. PLAUSIBLE; confirm 404 against a live Shared Drive.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/matter_documents.py:261-310: for google_drive the shim calls google_request('DELETE', f'/{safe_object_id}', base_url='https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files') with no params. google_request (backend/app/services/google_client.py:20-39) adds only the Authorization header, so supportsAllDrives is never sent. The unit test backend/tests/test_workspace_mcp_changed_router_contracts.py:161-200 asserts exactly this bare DELETE. The staged-cleanup path does append ?supportsAllDrives=true (backend/app/services/matter_file_store.py:431-435), as do the upload, read and open paths (matter_file_store.py:273, 341, 1122, 1234). provider_http.py:96-98 maps a 404 to ProviderNotFound, and matter_documents.py:347-348 returns silently on ProviderNotFound. delete_matter_document (matter_documents.py:669-714) then deletes the DB row and commits. Shared Drives are the preferred Google storage path, not an edge case: google_service_account.py:11 and 166-253 prefer the service-account token for an org Shared Drive root, and cloud_init.py:202-247 auto-provisions an org Shared Drive. Drive v3 returns notFound for shared-drive items unless supportsAllDrives=true, so every delete of a Shared Drive document orphans the file while reporting success. The My Drive half is also correct: Drive files.delete is permanent, while Graph DELETE (matter_documents.py:288-307) goes to the recycle bin.
reviews.correction: No factual overstatement. One caveat to add: the service account joins the Shared Drive as fileOrganizer (cloud_init.py:1139, 1228-1237). Drive's permanent files.delete on shared-drive items needs organizer rights on the parent, so adding supportsAllDrives=true alone may turn the silent 404 into a 403. That surfaces as a 502, which is at least not silent. Moving the file to the trash avoids this.
reviews.fix_sketch: In _delete_cloud_provider_object's google_drive branch, move the file to the trash instead of hard-deleting it: google_request('PATCH', f'/{safe_object_id}', params={'supportsAllDrives': 'true'}, json={'trashed': True}, ...). A fileOrganizer can do this, and it matches the Graph recycle-bin behavior. At minimum, pass params={'supportsAllDrives': 'true'} on the DELETE. Update test_cloud_delete_routes_each_supported_provider to assert the params. Optionally add a one-off reconciliation that lists Shared Drive matter folders and finds files with no MatterDocument row, to clean up files already orphaned.

title: Filenames containing '#' or '%' break path-based OneDrive/SharePoint uploads
claim: The filename is interpolated unencoded into ':/{filename}:/content' (matter_file_store.py:866-871), createUploadSession (925) and the SharePoint path (1384-1387); '#' starts a URL fragment, truncating the path and dropping conflictBehavior. The inbound attachment sanitizer keeps '#' and '%' (inbound_email.py:271-283) and failures are logged and swallowed (inbound_email.py:386-400), so attachments like 'Exhibit #3.pdf' silently fail to file.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/matter_file_store.py:867-871 builds f"{GRAPH_BASE}/me/drive/items/{parent_id}:/{filename}:/content?@microsoft.graph.conflictBehavior=rename" with a raw filename. Line 925 does the same for createUploadSession, and lines 1383-1387 do the same for SharePoint. store_matter_file_result (529-700) applies no encoding. I ran the pinned httpx 0.28.1 URL parser (backend/requirements.txt:18) on these names. 'Exhibit #3.pdf' gives path '.../ABC:/Exhibit%20', with '3.pdf:/content?@microsoft.graph.conflictBehavior=rename' moved into the fragment, so the fragment is not sent and the query is dropped. '50% off.pdf' gives the malformed path '50%%20off.pdf'. 'Invoice %20A.pdf' is decoded to 'Invoice  A.pdf', a silent rename. The inbound sanitizer (backend/app/services/inbound_email.py:269-280) strips only control characters and /\:*?"<>|, so '#' and '%' survive. Attachment storage failures are caught, logged and skipped (inbound_email.py:386-414). Folder creation is not affected, because _ensure_onedrive_folder (cloud_init.py:763-797) sends the name in a JSON body. Google uploads send the name in multipart metadata and are also unaffected.
reviews.correction: Scope is broader than stated. Manual uploads (matter_documents.py:543-553) only apply os.path.basename, so '#', '%' and also '?' reach the same unencoded path. Those failures are visible to the user rather than silent. For inbound email the impact is milder than 'silently fail to file': the full .eml, including the attachment, is still filed first (inbound_email.py:330-345). Only the separate attachment document is missing.
reviews.fix_sketch: Percent-encode the name in all three Graph path-addressed URLs with quote(filename, safe='') (urllib.parse.quote is already imported and used for ids): matter_file_store.py:869, 925 and 1385. Keep the raw name in the createUploadSession JSON body. Add parametrized tests using 'Exhibit #3.pdf', '50% off.pdf' and 'a?b.pdf' that assert the outgoing URL path is encoded and the query survives. Optionally make the inbound attachment loop record a storage_error document row instead of skipping it, so failures are visible.

title: Correspondence capture ignores CC, so mail where the party is only copied is never captured
claim: The Graph $select omits ccRecipients (microsoft_mail.py:43-48) and Gmail metadataHeaders are only From/To/Subject/Date (google_mail.py:187-194), while correspondence_capture._email_addresses reads 'cc' (correspondence_capture.py:87-94), which is always empty. Messages copying the client or opposing counsel are missed despite the rules UI promising 'emails involving the matter's parties'.

reviews.evidence: The Microsoft reader's $select is 'id,subject,bodyPreview,from,toRecipients,receivedDateTime,...' with no ccRecipients, and the returned dict has no 'cc' key (backend/app/services/microsoft_mail.py:43-48, 53-76). The Gmail reader requests metadataHeaders ['From','To','Subject','Date'] and returns no 'cc' (backend/app/services/google_mail.py:53-60, 79-91). Line refs in the claim (169-194) are stale because the file is 122 lines, but the substance is the same. correspondence_capture._email_addresses reads email.get('cc') (correspondence_capture.py:87-94). evaluate_matter_rules matches party addresses against that 'all' set (:200-207), and scan_and_capture feeds it these readers' output (:412-419). As a result cc is always [], and CommunicationLog.participants.cc is also always empty (:371-375). The UI promise is at frontend/src/components/MatterCorrespondenceTab.jsx:176 ('Capture emails involving the matter's parties') and user-guide 02-matters-and-documents.md:84. Other paths already fetch cc: cloud_sync.py:757 and 798 fetch ccRecipients, and cloud_search.py:1320 fetches the Cc header. The capture test fixture hard-codes 'cc': [] (test_correspondence_capture.py:38).
reviews.correction: Accurate. Nuance: the separate email-agent matcher is sender-only by design (email_agent.py:148-161). The gap applies to the correspondence-capture path, which clearly intends to use cc. A case-number mention in the subject or preview still captures a cc-only message, so the miss is limited to party-address matching.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add ccRecipients to the Graph $select in ms_read_mail_user and map it to 'cc' the same way as 'to'. Add 'Cc' to the Gmail metadataHeaders and map headers_dict.get('cc') to 'cc'. Add tests where a party is only on cc. Also check the downstream effect: verified staff aliases are in party_addresses (correspondence_capture.py:160-173), so capture volume will rise somewhat.

title: Correspondence capture reads a fixed 50-message/7-day window with no pagination or cursor
claim: Each run reads the top CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_MAX_EMAILS=50 messages from the last 7 days (correspondence_capture.py:406-419; microsoft_mail.py:38-50; google_mail.py:169-180) with no paging and no persisted cursor. More than 50 messages per 30-minute interval, or an outage over 7 days, leaves permanent gaps in the matter file.

reviews.evidence: scan_and_capture sets limit = max_emails or settings.CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_MAX_EMAILS and makes one call to ms_read_mail_user or gmail_read_mail without passing days (correspondence_capture.py:406-419). The config values are CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_MAX_EMAILS=50 and INTERVAL_MIN=30 (config.py:586-588). ms_read_mail_user makes one GET /me/messages with $top=max_results, $orderby desc and a 7-day filter, and never follows @odata.nextLink (microsoft_mail.py:25-50). gmail_read_mail makes one list call with maxResults and after:7 days, and never follows nextPageToken (google_mail.py:22-46). The claim's line refs 169-180 are stale; the substance is at 35-46. No cursor is persisted: the scheduler only records run counts (scheduler.py:1859-1919). The manual 'Scan now' passes max_emails=None (frontend/src/api.js:1949-1955; MatterCorrespondenceTab.jsx:585; matters_correspondence.py:404-411), so it also gets the 50 newest messages across the whole mailbox.
reviews.correction: The core claim holds. The '30-minute interval' applies only when CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_ENABLED is set, and it defaults to False (config.py:586; scheduler.py:818). CI also sets it to false. By default only the manual Scan now runs, and that is subject to the same limits: it considers only the 50 newest messages across all folders from the last 7 days, so relevant mail from earlier in the week is often missed on busy mailboxes.
reviews.fix_sketch: Page through results in both readers, following @odata.nextLink or nextPageToken up to a hard safety ceiling. Persist a per-user, per-provider high-water mark: the last receivedDateTime or internalDate, or a Gmail historyId or Graph delta token. Derive the next window from that mark instead of a fixed 7 days, with a small overlap, since dedupe by external_ref already exists. For manual scan, allow a longer lookback or a query filtered by party addresses. A new cursor column or table needs a migration, so follow the AGENTS.md head protocol, or reuse an existing integration sync-state row if one fits.

title: Email agent and correspondence capture block each other's dedupe and re-spend LLM calls
claim: The email agent writes CommunicationLog(matter_id, external_ref='provider:id') with no document (email_agent.py:57-91); capture's _already_captured (correspondence_capture.py:217-233, 263-269) then skips the message so no .eml is archived. In the other order capture blocks note/task-tag creation (email_agent.py:64-77). process_emails classifies and drafts before any dedupe (email_agent.py:366-394), so every scan re-bills LLM classification and premium drafts.

reviews.evidence: _auto_log_and_task writes a CommunicationLog with channel='email', external_ref '<provider>:<id>', matter_id=matched_matter_ids[0] and no document_id (backend/app/services/email_agent.py:57-92). Capture's _already_captured matches on tenant, matter_id, channel and external_ref and ignores document_id (correspondence_capture.py:217-233). capture_email_for_matter returns False before fetching or storing the .eml when that row exists (:258-269). In the reverse order, capture writes a log with the same external_ref format (:258, 358-378). The email agent's dedupe is tenant-wide on external_ref (email_agent.py:64-77) and returns before any MatterNote or tagged task is created (:94-127). process_emails runs classify_email and draft_response (:376-394) before _auto_log_and_task, the only place with a dedupe (:396-403), so each Communications-page scan (CommunicationsPage.jsx:483 via api.js:1941) repeats the LLM calls for already-logged mail. Only the file_outbound_email path backfills document_id (:595-596); nothing backfills it for inbound mail.
reviews.correction: The mechanism holds; a few details are narrower. The email agent logs only to the first matched matter, and capture's skip is scoped to the matter, so other matters still get the .eml. Repeat LLM spend applies only to matter-linked messages, because unmatched mail is dropped before classification (:370-375). Drafts run only when requires_response is true, and use the premium route only when premium AI is allowed; otherwise they use the standard route (router :46-51). The scheduled capture job is off by default, so the collision comes mainly from manual Scan now and Communications-page scans.
reviews.fix_sketch: (1) In process_emails, look up existing CommunicationLog rows by external_ref in one batched query before classifying. For already-logged messages, skip the LLM calls and return the stored summary, or omit them. (2) In capture, treat a matching row with document_id IS NULL as incomplete: fetch and store the .eml and set document_id on that existing row instead of skipping. (3) In _auto_log_and_task, when a log already exists (for example from capture), still create the MatterNote and tagged task if none exists for that external_ref. That needs a dedupe key on notes, or reuse of the task tag's external_ref. Add cross-path tests for both orders.

title: Outbound client emails are filed twice on the matter
claim: The compose log (matters.py:2807-2818) stores no external_ref: Graph sendMail returns 202 with no id (connected_mail.py:128-138) and the Gmail id is returned but discarded (connected_mail.py:192-199). A later scan captures the Sent Items copy under 'provider:id' (correspondence_capture.py:258-269), producing two log rows and two .eml files per email.

reviews.correction: Accurate as stated. The claim leaves out two conditions. First, a scan has to pick up the Sent copy. The scheduled job is off by default (config.py:586 CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_ENABLED=False, scheduler.py:818), but the per-matter manual 'Scan now' is always available (matters_correspondence.py:387-413) and force-enables rules for that matter. Second, the mail must have gone out through the actor's own connected mailbox. SMTP-fallback sends and firm-mailbox sends leave no Sent copy in a scanned per-user mailbox.
reviews.evidence: matters.py:2807-2818 builds the compose CommunicationLog with no external_ref, and matters.py:2824-2839 then calls file_outbound_email, which writes its own .eml MatterDocument named '<date>_sent_<slug>_<uuid8>.eml' (correspondence_capture.py:537-590). connected_mail.py:128-138: Graph /me/sendMail only checks for 202 and returns no id. connected_mail.py:192-199: the Gmail id goes into provider_message_id, but grep finds no reader of provider_message_id outside connected_mail.py. microsoft_mail.py:50 lists /me/messages, which covers every folder including Sent Items. google_mail.py:42-44 lists /users/me/messages, which includes SENT. correspondence_capture.py:258-265 dedupes only on external_ref 'provider:id' through _already_captured (217-237), so the compose row (external_ref NULL) never matches. capture_email_for_matter (297-374) then stores a second .eml and a second 'outbound'/'sent' CommunicationLog. The client address is in party_addresses (145-155), so evaluate_matter_rules matches.
reviews.fix_sketch: 1) In email_matter_client, carry delivery.provider_message_id through and set log.external_ref = f'google:{id}' for Gmail sends, so _already_captured skips the Sent copy. 2) Microsoft: switch _send_microsoft to create-draft then send (POST /me/messages, then /me/messages/{id}/send) and record the draft's internetMessageId, or send with Prefer: IdType="ImmutableId" and read with the same header. Store it as external_ref, or add internetMessageId to the scan's $select and to the dedupe keys. 3) Fallback: in capture_email_for_matter, skip an outbound message when the matter already has a compose log with external_ref IS NULL and the same subject and recipient within a short window, and backfill that row's external_ref. Add a regression test: compose send, then scan the Sent copy, and assert one log row and one document.

title: Staff aliases count as matter parties, so the alias owner's mail is filed into all their matters
claim: correspondence_capture.py:160-173 adds verified aliases of every assigned user to party_addresses, and any address overlap triggers capture (200-207). Every message to/from an attorney's verified alias is copied into each matter they are assigned to, placing privileged mail on other clients' files.

reviews.correction: The mechanism is real and is deliberately covered by test_user_alias_matching.py:17-22. Scope is narrower than 'each matter they are assigned to'. The scheduled path only covers open matters with correspondence_rules.enabled (correspondence_capture.py:432-445), and that job is off by default (config.py:586). The manual scan only targets the one matter being scanned, but it still sweeps every alias message in the 7-day/50-message window into that matter. The query also does not filter on any 'active' assignment state, despite the comment at 160-162. Only aliases count, not the user's primary address.
reviews.evidence: correspondence_capture.py:160-173: the alias query joins MatterAssignment to UserAliasAddress on user_id, filters on is_verified, and merges the results into the same party-address set as client and party contacts. correspondence_capture.py:200-207: any intersection of the email's from/to/cc with party_addresses returns True. scan_and_capture (447-487) captures into every candidate matter that matches. So a message from or to attorney A's verified send-as alias about client X is filed onto client Y's matter whenever A is assigned to Y and Y has capture enabled. The scheduled job scans every connected user's mailbox (scheduler.py:1896-1916), so colleagues' copies also match. MatterAssignment (models/matter_assignment.py) has no active/ended column that the query could use.
reviews.fix_sketch: Keep staff aliases, and the assigned users' primary addresses, as a separate 'internal' set. Use it only to classify direction (is_outbound) and to exclude internal addresses from the match. Require (addrs - internal) & external_party_addresses, or a case-number hit, before capturing. Change _matter_party_addresses to return (external, internal). Update evaluate_matter_rules and invert test_verified_alias_matches_correspondence_party to assert that alias-only mail does NOT match. Add a test showing alias mail to matter X's client is not filed onto matter Y.

title: Timed task events land at the wrong hour on Outlook and Google
claim: task_notifications.py:252-267 sends due_time in the matter's intake timezone (the client's) or UTC when there is no intake (matter_followups.py:29-44), while the LawHand calendar renders the same due_time as browser-local wall time (calendar.py:38-48); there is no firm or user timezone. A 2:00 PM deadline shows 2:00 PM in LawHand but 9:00 AM CDT in Outlook.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/task_notifications.py:252-267 _task_timezone returns "UTC" for a task with no matter, and otherwise matter_timezone(). backend/app/services/matter_followups.py:29-44 reads MatterIntake.config['timezone'] (the client's timezone; the schema default is America/Chicago per schemas/matter_intake.py:91) and falls back to "UTC". Pushes send the naive due_time with that zone (google_calendar.py:55-61, microsoft_calendar.py:98-104; callers are task_notifications.py:473-480 and :515-517). backend/app/routers/calendar.py:38-48 emits the naive datetime.combine(due_date, due_time) with no offset, and its docstring says the browser reads it as the firm's local clock. Example: 14:00 on a matter with no intake is pushed as 14:00 UTC, which is 09:00 CDT, while LawHand shows 2:00 PM. Deadline sync uses yet another source, the browser timezone (api.js:2303, calendar.py:93).
reviews.correction: The core mismatch is real. "There is no firm or user timezone" is overstated: a firm-level TenantSettings.custom_config['firm_email_timezone'] exists (routers/firm_email_intake.py:61-69, :144), but only email intake uses it, not calendar pushes. When a matter has intake and the client shares the firm's timezone, the times line up. The wrong hour shows up for tasks without a matter, matters without intake, and clients in a different timezone from the firm.
reviews.fix_sketch: Choose one canonical timezone for task due_time and use it on both sides. For example, add a firm timezone setting (or reuse or generalize firm_email_timezone), store it on the task when the task is saved (or capture the browser timezone in the task form), have _task_timezone use it, and have /api/calendar/events emit an offset-aware start/end in that zone. Intake follow-ups that want client-local deadlines should convert to the canonical zone when they are written.

title: Key-date dedupe misses east of UTC+9 and beyond 100 events, creating duplicates on every sync
claim: Graph reads are normalized to UTC ('Prefer: outlook.timezone="UTC"', calendar_sync.py:100-122) and keyed on the UTC date [:10] (542-547) while events are created at 09:00 local (594); calendarView uses $top 100 with no @odata.nextLink, and Google uses maxResults 100 with no pageToken (344-350) over a 90-day window. Sydney/NZ firms and busy calendars get a new '[LawHand] ...' duplicate each sync.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/calendar_sync.py:119-122 sends Prefer: outlook.timezone="UTC", and _graph_event_datetime (54-74) converts timed values to UTC 'Z' strings. _existing_synced_keys keys on str(start)[:10] (542-547). Events are created at 09:00 in the caller's zone: naive datetime at line 594, then timezone_name from the browser via calendar.py:93 and api.js:2303. In Australia/Sydney (UTC+10/+11) or NZ, 09:00 local is 22:00/23:00 UTC the previous day, so the key never matches and every manual Sync creates another copy. At UTC+9, 09:00 is 00:00 UTC the same day and still matches. The Graph read is a single GET with $top 100 (lines 108, 125-137) and no @odata.nextLink loop. The Google read is a single GET with maxResults 100 (344-357) and no pageToken loop. Both are called with the 90-day window (572-576). tests/test_calendar_sync.py:478-531 covers only the UTC default.
reviews.correction: The east-of-UTC+9 miss affects Microsoft only. Google returns dateTime in the calendar's own zone (google_get_events 373-374), so its [:10] is the local date whenever the Google calendar's zone matches the browser zone. The page-size gap applies to both providers. An extra case: the read window starts at now (101, 340-342), while key dates from today are included (593). Syncing after 09:30 local therefore also re-creates today's key-date event.
reviews.fix_sketch: Best: fold this into the D11 marker-based identity and query by extended property instead of (subject, date), which removes both the timezone and the paging problems. Minimal fix: convert each read start to timezone_name before taking the date, follow @odata.nextLink and nextPageToken (or query by marker/subject filter), and start the read window at local midnight today. Add tests for Australia/Sydney and for more than 100 events.

title: Editing a scheduled event deletes and recreates it with the editor's token, re-inviting or orphaning
claim: Every PATCH (calendar.py:482-495) deletes and recreates the provider event using the editor's token rather than the creator's, the delete result is ignored (scheduled_events.py:125-142), and there is no creator/role check. Clients get a cancellation plus a new invite (and new Teams link) per edit; when another user edits or deletes, the original stays in the creator's calendar with the client still invited.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/calendar.py:482-495: every PATCH unconditionally calls delete_external_event, clears external_calendar_event_id/url/meeting_id/join_url, then calls create_external_event, all with user_id=str(current_user.id). No field-change check. The only frontend PATCH caller is the drag-move at CalendarPage.jsx:686, so every drag re-creates the event. backend/app/services/scheduled_events.py:125-142 discards the bool that ms_delete_event and google_delete_event return. calendar_sync.py:299-320 uses the editor's /me/events/{id}, where an event id from the creator's mailbox is not found; a 404 counts as success (line 320), so the original stays. Google returns False on a 404 (517), and that is ignored too. The PATCH and DELETE handlers (calendar.py:445-498, 501-523) filter by tenant only; they never compare created_by_user_id (models/scheduled_event.py:40) and do no role or matter-access check. eventIsMovable returns true for every scheduled_event (CalendarPage.jsx:131-133). When the editor has no calendar token, the create call raises and is caught (scheduled_events.py:90-91). The row keeps sync_status='error', the old external id is cleared, and the original is orphaned and untracked. Meanwhile the UI still reports success (CalendarPage.jsx:687, 824). Teams: ms_create_scheduled_event sets isOnlineMeeting again (280-282), so a new join URL is issued. Zoom meetings are also deleted and re-created (scheduled_events.py:141-142, 48-62).
reviews.correction: All the mechanics are confirmed. The client emails (a cancellation plus a new invite) apply to Outlook/Graph, where deleting an organizer's meeting sends cancellations and POST with attendees sends invites. The Google calls send no sendUpdates parameter, so Google guests get the event silently removed and re-added, with no emails by default.
reviews.fix_sketch: Only touch providers when start/end/timezone/attendees/title/description/provider fields actually changed. Update in place (Graph PATCH /me/events/{id}, Google events.patch with sendUpdates chosen deliberately) instead of delete+create, which keeps the Teams/Zoom join link. Run provider operations with the creator's token (row.created_by_user_id) rather than the editor's. Restrict PATCH/DELETE to the creator, admins or manage_matters holders. Check delete results and surface sync_status/sync_error in the response so the frontend stops reporting unconditional success.

title: Google scheduled events never send invitations or cancellations (no sendUpdates), and cannot carry a Meet link
claim: events.insert (calendar_sync.py:446-498, esp. 485-493) and delete (512-516) are called without sendUpdates, which Google treats as 'none', so attendees receive neither invites nor cancellations; Graph sends invites by default (scheduled_events.py:66-92). There is also no conferenceData/hangoutsMeet option; meeting_provider allows only none/teams/zoom (schemas/calendar.py:101-106).

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/calendar_sync.py:446-498 google_create_scheduled_event builds an event with attendees (482-483) and POSTs to /calendars/primary/events with json only and no params (485-493), so there is no sendUpdates. calendar_sync.py:500-516 google_delete_event DELETEs with no params. A grep for sendUpdates/conferenceData/hangoutsMeet across backend/app and frontend/src finds nothing. scheduled_events.py:66-90: the Microsoft branch calls ms_create_scheduled_event, which POSTs attendees to Graph /me/events (calendar_sync.py:276-286), and Graph invites them by default. ms_delete_event DELETEs /me/events/{id} (calendar_sync.py:316-319), and Graph cancels for the organizer. schemas/calendar.py:101-106 allows only meeting_provider none/teams/zoom. routers/calendar.py:367-374 ties Teams to the Microsoft calendar. routers/calendar.py:481-495: PATCH is implemented as a provider delete followed by a recreate, so every edit or drag-move of a Google event is also silent. CalendarPage.jsx:1422-1424 has an 'Attendee emails' field, so users expect invites.
reviews.correction: Accurate. The Meet part is a missing feature, not a defect. Google firms can still use Zoom or no link.
reviews.fix_sketch: Pass params={'sendUpdates':'all'} (or 'externalOnly') on the Google insert when attendees exist, and on google_delete_event. Better, make update a PATCH to the same event id with sendUpdates, so a move sends one 'updated' notice instead of a cancellation plus a new invite (this applies to Graph too). For Meet, add meeting_provider 'google_meet' to the schema validator and _validate_scheduled_payload (Google calendar required). Send conferenceData.createRequest {requestId: uuid4, conferenceSolutionKey:{type:'hangoutsMeet'}} with conferenceDataVersion=1, read join_url from hangoutLink or conferenceData.entryPoints, and add the option in the CalendarPage form. Add respx tests that assert the query params.

title: Cloud sync provider failures are recorded as successful syncs with 0 items
claim: On non-200 responses the provider loops break or return 0 instead of raising: Drive (cloud_sync.py:361-372), Gmail (493-501), Outlook (763-771), Graph files (1058-1064), SharePoint (641-661) and a missing token (330-332). The scheduler then records status='completed' (scheduler.py:1779-1790), contradicting the sync_all docstring (cloud_sync.py:75-77). Revoked consent or missing scopes show as a green 'completed, 0 ok' tile while the index goes stale.

reviews.correction: Line numbers are about 10 lines off in the current tree. Exceptions are now reported correctly: _run_provider_sync records them in failures and the scheduler writes a 'failed' run. Only non-200 HTTP responses and a missing token become a silent 'completed, 0'. The 'revoked consent' example is partly overstated. A revoked refresh token fails in token_vault._refresh_locked_row, which records refresh failure health, and admin integration health then shows a 'revoked'/'refresh_failed' warning. The sync-run row still says completed. The fully silent cases are 401/403/429/5xx with a still-valid token: missing Sites.Read.All at /sites/root, a Drive-scoped service-account token used for Gmail on Shared Drive tenants, throttling, or an access token revoked within the hour. A tenant with no Google credential also gets a 'google completed 0' run every interval, and a group is recorded 'completed' even when a sibling provider in that group failed.
reviews.evidence: cloud_sync.py:75-77: docstring says a failed provider must never read as zero items. cloud_sync.py:331-339: no token or NO_TENANT_DRIVE returns 0. cloud_sync.py:376-382: Drive non-200 logs and breaks, then commits and returns count. cloud_sync.py:503-511: Gmail list non-200 returns 0. cloud_sync.py:530-531: per-message non-200 silently continues. cloud_sync.py:651-671: SharePoint /sites/root non-200 leaves site_id None and returns 0; drives non-200 returns 0. cloud_sync.py:773-781: Outlook non-200 returns 0. cloud_sync.py:1068-1074: Graph files non-200 breaks. cloud_sync.py:268-296: _run_provider_sync only appends a failure on an exception. scheduler.py:1776-1790: records status='completed', items_ok=provider_total for each group. token_vault.py:280-312: refresh failures recorded on the credential row. admin.py:366-371: health warnings for revoked/refresh_failed. tests/test_cloud_sync_provider_failures.py covers only the exception path.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add a ProviderHTTPError(status) raised on non-200 listing responses in the Drive, Gmail, Outlook, SharePoint and _sync_graph_files paths, keeping any pages already upserted and committed. _run_provider_sync then records it with the status code, not the body. Return a sentinel or 'skipped' for no-token and NO_TENANT_DRIVE, and have the scheduler skip or record status='skipped' instead of completed. Record a group as 'completed' only when none of its providers failed. Honor Retry-After on 429. Add tests for 401, 403 and 429 per provider.

title: Cloud sync holds a tenants row lock across hundreds of provider HTTP calls
claim: Every _upsert runs SELECT tenants FOR UPDATE plus a migration lookup (cloud_sync.py:884-889), and commit happens only after the whole provider loop (e.g. Gmail at 509-562 makes ~200 sequential HTTP calls, ~3 DB statements per item). Other writes to the tenant row (settings, onboarding, cutover) block or time out during every sync.

reviews.correction: The mechanism is real, but the blast radius is wider than claimed and the long windows are narrower. Wider: a FOR UPDATE row lock on tenants conflicts with the FOR KEY SHARE that Postgres FK checks take. About 89 tables (documents, tasks, api_access_logs, durable_jobs, error_logs, and others) have an FK to tenants.id, so any insert of a tenant-owned row blocks until the sync commits, not just writes to the tenant row. The access-log middleware awaits its insert inside every request with lock_timeout 2s. During the window, every API request for that tenant is delayed up to 2s and its audit row is silently dropped. Narrower: the long window with HTTP calls under the lock is mainly Gmail (one metadata GET per message after the first upsert) and multi-page Drive/Graph listings. Outlook fetches all pages before any upsert, so its lock covers DB statements only. The migration reindex takes the lock only after discovery.
reviews.evidence: cloud_sync.py:893-899: every _upsert runs SELECT Tenant ... with_for_update() plus _latest_completed_migration. cloud_sync.py:520-563: the Gmail loop does a GET per message, then _upsert, with commit only at line 563 after the loop. cloud_sync.py:360-423: Drive pages are fetched between upserts, with commit at 423. cloud_sync.py:1060-1140: Graph pages are fetched between upserts, with commit at 1140. The comment at cloud_sync.py:688-689 says it commits per page, but it commits per call. cloud_sync.py:765-786: Outlook collects messages before upserting. storage_migration_reindex.py:79-98: discovery happens before the tenant lock. migrations/versions/039_api_access_log.py:43 and 001_initial_schema.py:104-107: real FKs to tenants.id. middleware/access_log.py:43-53: awaited in the request path. middleware/access_log.py:76-94: SET LOCAL lock_timeout='2s', and the comment documents the same KEY SHARE vs FOR UPDATE interaction for users. storage_migration.py:90,711 and cloud_init.py:325: other FOR UPDATE on tenant (cutover/init) that would wait.
reviews.fix_sketch: Do not hold any tenant lock across provider I/O. Collect normalized rows in memory per page or per provider. Then open a short write transaction: check the migration once, take the serialization lock, bulk-upsert with a single INSERT ... ON CONFLICT of many VALUES, and commit. For cutover serialization, use pg_advisory_xact_lock(hash(tenant_id)) in both cutover and sync writers instead of FOR UPDATE on the tenants row, so FK KEY SHARE and tenant settings updates are unaffected. Hoist _latest_completed_migration out of the per-row path.

title: Tenant OneDrive and SharePoint index sync lists only root-level items
claim: sync_onedrive uses /me/drive/root/children (cloud_sync.py:584-594) and sync_sharepoint uses /drives/{id}/root/children (663-680) with no recursion or delta, so matter files in subfolders are absent from firm-wide search unless a per-matter sync runs.

reviews.correction: The code facts are right. sync_onedrive lists only /me/drive/root/children and sync_sharepoint lists only /drives/{id}/root/children on the root site, with no recursion or delta. _sync_graph_files skips folder items and follows only @odata.nextLink. With the tenant token, /me/drive is the connecting admin's own OneDrive. Two points are overstated. First, 'absent from firm-wide search': the local index is only one source. Search always also runs live Graph /search/query (driveItem), which returns files at any depth when the token works, so subfolder files are missing only from the index fallback and index-scoped matter lookups. Second, 'unless a per-matter sync runs': the per-matter sync is also one level deep (children of the provisioned matter folder and durable parent IDs only), so files in nested subfolders stay unindexed even then. Google is unaffected because its files.list query is corpus-wide. The impact compounds with D50: if live Graph search 403s for per-user tokens, the index is the only source.
reviews.evidence: cloud_sync.py:582-601: sync_onedrive uses f"{GRAPH_BASE}/me/drive/root/children". cloud_sync.py:653-686: sync_sharepoint resolves /sites/root, then drives, then /drives/{id}/root/children. cloud_sync.py:1060-1085: _sync_graph_files follows only @odata.nextLink and skips items without 'file' (folders). cloud_sync.py:603-624 and 700-733: folder syncs list the direct children of given IDs only. cloud_sync.py:354-366: Google uses a corpus-wide files.list q, not per-folder. cloud_search.py:252-322: live _search_graph is scheduled alongside the index. cloud_search.py:323-330: search_index is always appended as the fallback. matters.py:3407: the per-matter sync route.
reviews.fix_sketch: Replace root-children listing with a Graph delta query scoped to the LawHand cloud root folder, not the drive root: /drives/{id}/items/{rootId}/delta. Persist the deltaLink per drive in sync_cursor for incremental runs, keep the MAX_FILES cap per run, and handle deleted items. Do the same, or a bounded BFS, for per-matter folder sync so matter subfolders are included. Scope to the LawHand root to avoid indexing an admin's personal OneDrive.

title: Per-user Graph search requests listItem without Sites.Read.All, likely 403ing all driveItem hits
claim: Global Graph search sends entityTypes ['driveItem','listItem'] (cloud_search.py:937-986) with the per-user token, but MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES has no Sites.Read.All (integrations.py:256-259). listItem requires it, so the request likely 403s and search_group returns None, giving users with a personal connection no OneDrive/SharePoint hits. PLAUSIBLE, needs live check.

reviews.correction: The code facts are confirmed. Global Graph search sends entityTypes ['driveItem','listItem'] in one request, and prefers the per-user token. MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES requests Files.ReadWrite.All but not Sites.Read.All, and a non-200 makes search_group return None, so that request contributes no file hits. Whether Graph actually returns 403 cannot be verified from the repo. It matches Graph's documented rule that listItem needs Sites.Read.All or Sites.ReadWrite.All. Three things mitigate it. The admin connect uses prompt=select_account, so a user token carries Sites.Read.All only if the admin granted consent for the whole organization. Folder-scoped matter searches use a different drive search endpoint and are unaffected. The local metadata index still runs as a fallback, though D49 shows it is thin for Microsoft. Also, the constant is at integrations.py:262-265, not 256-259.
reviews.evidence: cloud_search.py:930-936: entity_type_groups appends ['driveItem','listItem'] for onedrive/sharepoint. cloud_search.py:962-996: search_group POSTs /search/query and returns None on any non-200. cloud_search.py:1014-1027: None responses are skipped. cloud_search.py:1568-1578: _get_microsoft_token prefers get_fresh_user_token. cloud_search.py:916-919: the folder-scoped path is separate. cloud_search.py:323-330: the index fallback always runs. integrations.py:262-265: MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES has no Sites.Read.All. integrations.py:242-245: admin scopes include it. integrations.py:~510: admin authorize uses prompt=select_account, not admin_consent. tests/test_cloud_search.py:1021,1097,1144 pin the combined entityTypes but mock the HTTP layer.
reviews.fix_sketch: Send ['driveItem'] alone for OneDrive and SharePoint document search, since driveItem covers files in both. Alternatively, send listItem as a separate optional group so its 403 cannot suppress driveItem hits. On a 403 whose body mentions ListItem, retry once with driveItem only. Update the three tests in test_cloud_search.py. Adding Sites.Read.All to per-user scopes is the alternative, but it widens consent and needs a product/privacy decision.

title: Native Google Docs/Sheets are excluded from matter sync, firm-knowledge ingestion and search
claim: LEGAL_MIME_TYPES (cloud_sync.py:48-55) has no application/vnd.google-apps.* types; the matter-folder Drive query (cloud_sync.py:334-340) and document_sync (document_sync.py:22-28, 281-305) filter to PDF/DOCX/DOC/RTF/TXT, and the download uses alt=media (document_sync.py:370), which cannot fetch Docs; there is no files.export. Google Workspace firms drafting in Google Docs never see those documents in matters, search or AI context.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_sync.py:48-55: LEGAL_EXTENSIONS/LEGAL_MIME_TYPES contain no application/vnd.google-apps.* types. cloud_sync.py:341-345 (tenant index query) and :944-952 (matter-folder query) filter Drive to those types or to names containing an extension, so native Docs and Sheets never enter cloud_metadata_index. document_sync.py:22-28 and :281-305 apply the same filter, and :370 downloads with ?alt=media with no files.export. BUT cloud_search.py:628-690 (_search_google_drive, the live Drive search) has no MIME filter: it uses fullText contains plus a folder scope. cloud_search.py:1150-1156 plus :1425-1435 export google-apps.document, spreadsheet and presentation as text for content fetch. rag.py:1887-1905 uses this live search and fetch_contents for AI context (CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED=True by default, config.py:569). The matter cloud-files panel (matters.py:221-275) is also built from live cloud_search.search. The only frontend-free path is document_sync (routers/document_sync.py; no caller in frontend/src).
reviews.correction: The claim that firms 'never see those documents in matters, search or AI context' is wrong. Live Drive search, which is on by default, returns native Google Docs, including matter-folder-scoped searches in the matter panel and in RAG. Their text is exported for AI context. Native Docs are missing from three places. (1) cloud_metadata_index, both the tenant sync and the per-matter folder sync. So they miss the index-based title matches and the matter-scoped 'no keyword match' fallback (cloud_search.py:509-518). (2) The document_sync ingestion. This is API-only today, with no UI caller. (3) Any file whose body does not contain the matter-name keywords used by the matter panel. Cited line refs have drifted (cloud_sync query is now around 341-345).
reviews.fix_sketch: Add application/vnd.google-apps.document (and optionally .spreadsheet) to the Drive query clauses in cloud_sync.sync_google_drive and _sync_google_drive_folder, and to a separate GOOGLE_NATIVE_TYPES set. In document_sync.sync_google_drive, include the same types. In download_and_process, when the mime starts with application/vnd.google-apps., call files/{id}/export?mimeType=application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document (or application/pdf), mind the 10 MB export limit, and give the local file a .docx suffix. Add unit tests with mocked Drive responses.

title: Committed teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip is stale (old domain and Entra app id) and not rebuilt by CI
claim: The manifest inside the tracked teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip points at legalapp.perevagagroup.com and webApplicationInfo id c805316c-..., while teams-app/manifest.json (6-51) uses getlawhand.com and 062a7776-.... CI never rebuilds it, package.ps1 needs Windows (System.Drawing), TASKS 1402 says 'do not commit the zip' yet it is tracked and still marked PENDING (TASKS.md:2371-2378), and TASKS.md:146 is open. An admin who uploads the checked-in zip installs an app that loads the wrong host.

reviews.evidence: I unzipped teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip (tracked; git ls-files lists it). Its manifest.json uses developer 'Perevaga Group', https://legalapp.perevagagroup.com for all URLs and contentUrl/configurationUrl, validDomains ['legalapp.perevagagroup.com'] and webApplicationInfo id c805316c-ac2c-4f68-8ace-a5522889bf50. teams-app/manifest.json:6-51 uses https://getlawhand.com and 062a7776-84ae-4e04-ab4b-3194b6a8d551 with resource api://lawhand.onmicrosoft.com/.... teams-app/package.ps1 calls Add-Type System.Drawing and draws the outline icon with System.Drawing.Bitmap, which works only on Windows under .NET 6+. grep of .github/ finds no reference to teams-app or the zip, and the zip is not in .gitignore. TASKS.md:2371-2378 (1402 PENDING) says '**do not commit the zip**'. TASKS.md:146 ('Update Teams/Office manifests to the new app IDs') is unchecked.
reviews.correction: All facts are correct, but the impact is overstated. Firm admins do not get the package from this repo. The documented operator flow (docs/deployment/wellpled-rebrand-cutover.md:52-56) rebuilds it with package.ps1 -MicrosoftClientId ... -PublicHost ..., not by uploading the committed zip. Also, the Teams tab cannot work on any host until D17/D18 are fixed, so a stale zip adds little extra breakage. This is repo hygiene and ledger drift (TASKS 1402 also still describes /teams/tab and clarity-legal-teams.zip), so low rather than medium. teams-app/manifest.json itself already has the new app ID, so the TASKS.md:146 item is only partly outstanding.
reviews.fix_sketch: Run git rm teams-app/lawhand-teams.zip and add it to .gitignore. Replace package.ps1 with a cross-platform script (Python zipfile, or bash with zip) that renders manifest.json from env or arguments and zips the committed color.png and outline.png without regenerating icons. Optionally add a CI step that builds the package as a workflow artifact and validates it against the Teams manifest schema (validDomains matches the contentUrl host, and webApplicationInfo.id equals MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID). Update TASKS 1402 and TASKS.md:146 to reflect the real state.

title: Teams channel-tab save reports success without creating a working tab
claim: TeamsTabConfigPage calls setConfig only via window.microsoftTeams (TeamsTabConfigPage.jsx:69), which the ESM @microsoft/teams-js v2 import (line 2) does not define as a global; saveConfiguration swallows its own errors (79), so registerOnSaveHandler always calls notifySuccess (90) even when createTeamsLink failed. Admins can save a channel tab with no content URL or matter link and see no error.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/pages/TeamsTabConfigPage.jsx:2 imports only the ESM namespaces `app` and `pages` from @microsoft/teams-js. Lines 69-78 look up `window.microsoftTeams` and call setConfig only if it exists. No file in frontend/, office-addin/ or teams-app/ sets that global; grep finds only line 69. frontend/node_modules/@microsoft/teams-js/package.json:11-13 (v2.53.0) has `main` pointing at the UMD build and `module` at the ESM build. Vite resolves `module`, and nothing in dist/esm writes `window.microsoftTeams`, so setConfig is never called, even when everything succeeds. saveConfiguration (54-84) catches every error at 79-80 and only sets a flash message. The promise always resolves, so the handler at 88-91 always reaches notifySuccess and its .catch/notifyFailure branch cannot run. The page is the configurable-tab URL (teams-app/manifest.json:36-38 -> /teams/config; App.jsx:352-355, adminOnly). No frontend test covers the page.
reviews.correction: The claim understates the problem. setConfig is skipped on every save, not only when createTeamsLink fails, so no channel tab ever gets a contentUrl/entityId from this page. When createTeamsLink succeeds, the matter link row is created but the tab is still unconfigured. When it fails, neither is created, and Teams is still told the save succeeded.
reviews.fix_sketch: Call `teamsPages.config.setConfig({entityId: matterId, contentUrl: `${origin}/teams?matter=${matterId}`, websiteUrl, suggestedDisplayName})` from the ESM import instead of `window.microsoftTeams`. Split out the save logic so the Teams save handler receives a thrown error or a false result. Call `saveEvent.notifyFailure(detail)` when createTeamsLink or setConfig fails, and notifySuccess only after both succeed. Keep the flash message for the standalone admin route. Add a Vitest test that mocks @microsoft/teams-js and checks setConfig is called and that notifyFailure fires on an API error.

title: Teams personal tab shows 'No channels linked' to every non-admin
claim: GET /links goes through require_teams_enabled, which requires the admin role (teams_gate.py:64-66; routers/teams.py:155-157); TeamsTabPage.jsx:10-12 swallows the 403 and renders an empty list, so attorneys and staff conclude no matter channels exist.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/teams_gate.py:64-66: require_teams_enabled raises 403 'Admin access required' for any role other than admin. backend/app/routers/teams.py:155-157: GET /links calls require_teams_enabled. frontend/src/api.js:869-870 is a plain GET. frontend/src/pages/TeamsTabPage.jsx:9-14 catches every error with setLinks([]), and 67-68 then renders 'No channels linked.'. App.jsx:348-351 serves /teams (the manifest's static personal tab) to any authenticated user, not adminOnly.
reviews.correction: The mechanism is exactly as described. Severity is overstated: the list is informational only (team and channel names), and the tab's main actions (the Matters and Calendar links at TeamsTabPage.jsx:29-50) still work for non-admins. No data or workflow is affected. The scope is somewhat wider than claimed: admins see the same false empty state whenever Teams is disabled, not connected (409) or missing scopes (403), because every error is swallowed.
reviews.fix_sketch: Backend: split the gate. Add a require_teams_connected check (flag, active credential, scopes) with no admin requirement for GET /links, and keep the admin check for POST/DELETE and the other mutating endpoints. Frontend: record the error status in TeamsTabPage. On 403/409, show 'Teams isn't connected for your firm' or 'Ask an admin', and hide or disable the Configure link for non-admins. Add a backend test that staff can list links and a Vitest test for the error state. A minimal frontend-only fix (distinct error message) is possible but leaves non-admins unable to see channels.

title: Office add-in CSP frame-ancestors omits *.cloud.microsoft
claim: nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26 allows only *.office.com, *.office365.com, *.live.com and *.microsoft.com; Microsoft 365 web apps are moving to word/excel/outlook/m365.cloud.microsoft, and frame-ancestors checks every ancestor including the top-level page, so the task pane can be blocked in Office on the web / new Outlook.

reviews.evidence: nginx/snippets/office_addin.conf:26 sets frame-ancestors 'self' https://*.office.com https://*.office365.com https://*.live.com https://*.microsoft.com. The CSP wildcard *.microsoft.com does not match hosts under the separate .microsoft TLD such as outlook.cloud.microsoft or m365.cloud.microsoft. This location-level add_header is the only CSP on /office/: office-addin/nginx.conf:1-11 adds no headers, and the server-level CSP at nginx/nginx.conf:415/768 is not inherited because the location defines its own add_header. The snippet is included in both server blocks (nginx/nginx.conf:621,980). frame-ancestors checks every ancestor, including the top-level page.
reviews.correction: The code fact is certain. The real-world impact depends on Microsoft's rollout of the *.cloud.microsoft host domains, which is ongoing. Reviewers should also check *.sharepoint.com: Word and Excel on the web for work accounts usually run under a top-level tenant.sharepoint.com page, which the current list also leaves out. That needs a browser test to confirm. Office on the web sign-in is already broken by D20, so this matters once D20 is fixed.
reviews.fix_sketch: Extend frame-ancestors with https://*.cloud.microsoft, https://*.microsoft365.com and https://*.sharepoint.com (after testing it). Keep 'self' and the existing hosts. Add a small nginx config test or CI grep that asserts cloud.microsoft is present, and test sideloading in Word, Excel and Outlook on the web.

title: Outlook read-mode button uploads the full message body and then always fails as read-only
claim: The manifest advertises 'Review Outlook messages' on read items (office-addin/manifests/outlook.xml:13, 29-31, 41-53); main.ts:43-46 enables Propose without checking capabilities.writeEnabled, and the server rejects the plan with 'This Office host is read-only' (office_action_policy.py:72-73) after up to 50k characters of client email body were uploaded.

reviews.evidence: office-addin/manifests/outlook.xml:13 advertises 'Review Outlook messages...'. Lines 29-31 activate on FormType=Read, and 41-53 add a MessageReadCommandSurface button that opens the task pane. office-addin/src/hosts/outlookAdapter.ts:59-71 reports writeEnabled=false and supportedActions=[] in read mode, and captureContext (74-95) reads the full body (up to 50,000 chars). refreshProposeState (office-addin/src/main.ts:43-46) enables Propose only on authenticated, capturedContext and instruction, and never checks writeEnabled. main.ts:63-66 even labels it 'Current Outlook message'. propose() (main.ts:118-127) POSTs context and instruction to /office/plans. The service calls validate_context first (backend/app/services/office_assistant.py:117), and that raises read_only_host 'This Office host is read-only' (backend/app/services/office_action_policy.py:72-73). The router maps this to a 422 (backend/app/routers/office_assistant.py:34-44). The client preview would reject read items anyway (outlookAdapter.ts:100-102).
reviews.correction: The dead end is real. The privacy part is overstated: the body goes over TLS to LawHand's own API but is rejected before any token-budget check, LLM call, or OfficeActionRun/audit write (office_assistant.py:117-118), so nothing is stored or sent on to a model provider.
reviews.fix_sketch: Short term (add-in only): in Office.onReady/capture, if capabilities.writeEnabled is false, don't send the plan request. Disable Propose and show 'LawHand can change drafts only. Reply or compose to use it.' Or remove the MessageReadCommandSurface extension point and the FormType=Read rule and reword the manifest description. Longer term: if read-mode help such as a summary is wanted, add a read-only 'answer' plan type on the server that needs no write capability.

title: Office add-in session expires after 30 minutes with no refresh or re-auth
claim: authenticated is set once at startup (office-addin/src/main.ts:188-197); OfficeApi.request throws on any non-OK response (office-addin/src/api/officeApi.ts:21-28) and never calls /auth/refresh or re-runs session.ensure, while ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES=30 (config.py:42). A pane left open fails with 'Not authenticated' until reopened.

reviews.evidence: office-addin/src/main.ts:188-197 runs session.ensure once in Office.onReady and sets authenticated=true, and nothing sets it back. OfficeApi.request (office-addin/src/api/officeApi.ts:11-31) throws on any non-OK response and never retries or refreshes. A grep for 'refresh' in office-addin/src finds only refreshProposeState. The access_token cookie has max_age = ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES*60 (backend/app/routers/auth.py:727-734), and ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 30 (backend/app/config.py:42); only CI overrides it (ci.yml:380,603). Once the cookie expires, get_current_user raises 401 'Not authenticated' (backend/app/middleware/tenant.py:145-150), and main.ts:170 shows that message. A refresh cookie is set by the exchange (auth.py:735-742), and POST /auth/refresh (auth.py:2457-2490) could renew it, but the add-in never calls it.
reviews.correction: The claim is accurate. Detail: closing and reopening the pane recovers without user interaction, because ensure() finds a 401 and silently re-exchanges the NAA token, so this is a recoverable annoyance rather than a lockout. An extra effect the claim leaves out: if the token expires between plan creation and Apply, report() fails and the audit result is not recorded (main.ts:95-102). The claim only applies where cookies work at all (desktop), given D20.
reviews.fix_sketch: In OfficeApi.request, on a 401 call POST /auth/refresh once with credentials:'include' (or, as a fallback, session.ensure(naa)), then retry the original request. If that also fails, set authenticated=false, call refreshProposeState, and show 'Session expired - reconnecting'. Optionally refresh ahead of time on a timer (about 25 min) or on visibilitychange. Add a vitest case for 401, then refresh, then retry.

title: Word apply replaces the selection as plain text with no tracked changes
claim: wordAdapter.ts:99-103 uses insertText(..., replace), dropping mixed formatting, fields, cross-references and footnote references in the selection; WordApi 1.4 is detected (line 21) but changeTrackingMode is never enabled, so an AI rewrite in a negotiated draft leaves no redline.

reviews.evidence: office-addin/src/hosts/wordAdapter.ts:99-103 does `selection.insertText(action.content.text, Word.InsertLocation.replace)` inside Word.run with no other calls. The capture at :32-39 loads only `selection.text`, so the model never sees formatting, fields or footnote references. Line 21 only reports WordApi_1_4 in the capabilities object. A grep for changeTracking/trackChanges/insertHtml/insertOoxml across office-addin/src finds nothing, so the add-in never sets context.document.changeTrackingMode. The backend prompt allows only format 'text' (backend/app/services/office_assistant.py:38). The whole surface sits behind OFFICE_ASSISTANT_ENABLED=False plus a pilot tenant allowlist (backend/app/config.py:111-115, backend/app/services/office_access.py:13-48).
reviews.correction: 'Leaves no redline' holds only when Track Changes is off in the document. Office.js edits follow the document's current tracking mode, and negotiated drafts often already have tracking on, so the replacement is tracked there. The real gap is that the add-in never turns tracking on and never warns when it is off. The loss of mixed run formatting, fields, cross-references and footnote references on a plain-text replace is accurate. The feature is off by default and pilot-only.
reviews.fix_sketch: In WordAdapter.execute, when WordApi 1.4 is supported, load context.document.changeTrackingMode. If it is off, either set it to Word.ChangeTrackingMode.trackAll for the edit (optionally restoring it afterwards) or ask the user to confirm an untracked edit in the preview. Before applying, check whether the selection holds fields, footnotes or content controls (selection.fields / footnotes / contentControls, or getOoxml) and block or warn. Longer term, replace only the changed words (diff-based range edits) so run formatting survives.
