title: Office add-in audit-failure status is wrong on reject and overwritten on apply
claim: report() always says 'The Office change completed, but LawHand could not record its audit result' (office-addin/src/main.ts:101), including after a Reject where nothing changed (154-165); on a successful apply, setStatus('Approved change applied.') at line 142 immediately overwrites the audit-failure message, so unaudited AI changes go unnoticed.

reviews.evidence: office-addin/src/main.ts:95-103: report() catches any reportResult error and always sets 'The Office change completed, but LawHand could not record its audit result.' reject() (:154-165) first sets 'Proposed change rejected...' (:163), then awaits report() (:164) last, so on failure the wrong 'change completed' text stays on screen. apply() (:139-145) awaits report() (:140), then setStatus('Approved change applied.') at :142 replaces the error, and capture() at :145 replaces it again ('Reading...' then 'Context captured...', :107/:115). The stale and failed branches (:147, :149) also overwrite it. On the server, record_result rejects a late applied report with expired_plan (backend/app/services/office_assistant.py:250-255, via the router at backend/app/routers/office_assistant.py:109-112), which is one realistic trigger. The OfficeActionRun row stays 'proposed'.
reviews.correction: Accurate as described. Severity lowered because the proposal itself is always audited server-side (OfficeActionRun status='proposed', backend/app/services/office_assistant.py:200-223), so an admin still has a trace. What is lost is the final outcome and the user's awareness of it. It only happens when the result POST fails, and only in pilot tenants.
reviews.fix_sketch: Make report() return a boolean (or take the result status) and build the message after it: for 'applied' show 'Change applied, but LawHand could not record the audit result' as an error. For 'rejected', 'stale' and 'failed', use outcome-specific wording (for example 'Rejected; audit not recorded'). Do not call capture() in a way that clears the error, or run capture first and set the combined status last. Optionally queue the result in memory or localStorage and retry the POST once.

title: Office planner sends Word selection/Outlook body to the Standard LLM route without the data-class check
claim: office_assistant.create_plan (office_assistant.py:115-150) always resolves use_premium=False and sends up to 50k chars (schemas/office_assistant.py:44-67) without calling route_matter_context_allowed; Standard is public-general by default (llm_routing.py:354-370), while chat enforces the gate (chat.py:2421-2430). In pilot tenants confidential document/email text can reach a provider not cleared for client data.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/office_assistant.py:117 calls resolve_llm_route(db, user.tenant_id, use_premium=False). Lines 118-150 serialize the whole context (Word selection up to 50k chars / Outlook body up to 50k, backend/app/schemas/office_assistant.py:44-67) and call self.llm.complete directly. route_matter_context_allowed is never called and no privacy mode is applied. standard_matter_context_allowed (backend/app/services/llm_routing.py:354-370) defaults to False unless a profile or platform setting allows it. route_matter_context_allowed (:373-430) also returns False for customer, explicit and tenant routes. Chat enforces the gate at backend/app/routers/chat.py:2427-2443 (blocks matter sources and attachments via _assert_public_general_sources_allowed, :733-743, and forces privacy_mode, :746-753). The AI broker enforces it too (backend/app/services/ai_request_broker.py:259-264). There is no equivalent check anywhere in backend/app/routers/office_assistant.py:66-84. Scope is limited by OFFICE_ASSISTANT_ENABLED=False and the pilot allowlist, plus a bypass for demo-tier tenants (backend/app/services/office_access.py:42-48).
reviews.correction: Accurate. Note that the Office text is not formally 'matter context'. It is closest to a chat attachment, which chat blocks on a public-general Standard route, so the gap is real. Exposure is limited to pilot and demo tenants while the global flag is on.
reviews.fix_sketch: In create_plan, after resolving the route, call `await route_matter_context_allowed(db, user.tenant_id, use_premium=False, route=route)`. If it returns False, either retry on the Premium route when that route is cleared, or raise OfficePolicyError('route_not_cleared_for_client_data'). Map that error to 409 in the router. Expose the result in GET /api/office/policy so the task pane can disable Propose with an explanation. Add tests for a public-general Standard route and for a BYOK route.

title: Office plan usage is recorded at $0 because costing matches the gateway alias
claim: _usage_record prices route.model (office_assistant.py:75-85), a LiteLLM alias like 'lawhand-standard' (config.py:267); calculate_cost only matches claude/gemini/deepseek substrings and returns 0 with a warning (billing.py:60-66). Chat uses the provider-reported model (chat.py:2916). Office AI spend is invisible in usage and billing.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/office_assistant.py:75-85 prices model=route.model. LLMRoute.model returns gateway_alias (backend/app/services/llm_routing.py:81-83), which defaults to 'lawhand-standard' (backend/app/config.py:267). calculate_cost (backend/app/services/billing.py:36-66) matches ':free', claude/anthropic, gemini, gpt-4/azure and deepseek; anything else logs a warning and costs 0. create_plan passes no usage_sink to llm.complete (office_assistant.py:134-150). Chat captures response.model through usage_sink (backend/app/services/llm.py:380-384) and prices model_used = llm_usage.get('model') or route.model (backend/app/routers/chat.py:2916, 2973-2981). cost_usd is summed in the admin, platform and licensing reports (backend/app/routers/admin.py:489, platform.py:633, licensing.py:106).
reviews.correction: Only the dollar cost is $0. Token counts are recorded in UsageRecord (office_assistant.py:96-97) and count toward the token budget (backend/app/services/usage_limits.py:28), so Office usage is not invisible in usage. calculate_cost also matches gpt-4/azure/anthropic, not just claude/gemini/deepseek. A profile alias that contains a vendor name would be priced. billing.py:60-62 says LiteLLM's spend ledger is the canonical reconciliation source. Chat only avoids the problem if LiteLLM returns the underlying model name in response.model.
reviews.fix_sketch: Pass a usage_sink dict to self.llm.complete in create_plan. Then price and store model_used = usage_sink.get('model') or route.model in _usage_record, and keep final_model=gateway_alias. Add a unit test in which the provider reports a claude model and cost_usd > 0. Longer term, add an alias-to-price map so gateway aliases are priced directly.

title: Workspace MCP client registrations hard-expire after 30 days regardless of use
claim: WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_REGISTRATION_DAYS=30 (config.py:444) and is_active requires expires_at > now (workspace_mcp_client.py:73-79); the token endpoint calls _active_client before refresh (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:704-705) and only updates last_used_at (806), never extending expiry, although grants last 90 days (config.py:443). Actively used connectors get invalid_client on day 31.

reviews.evidence: config.py:444 sets WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_REGISTRATION_DAYS=30, and config.py:443 sets GRANT_DAYS=90. The env files keep 30 (docker-compose.prod.yml:77, .env.prod.example:374). DCR sets expires_at=now+30d (routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:374-375). models/workspace_mcp_client.py:73-79 is_active requires expires_at > now. The token endpoint calls _active_client (routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:705; helper 193-199 raises invalid_client) before any grant type, including refresh. The only write on success is client.last_used_at (806). Nothing in backend/app extends WorkspaceMCPClient.expires_at: grep finds only DCR creation and platform.py:2082-2108, which counts expired clients. Grants run a fixed 90 days (services/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:779-780). Research MCP has the same pattern (research_mcp_oauth.py:296-297).
reviews.correction: Accurate. Details: expiry is counted from client registration, not from each user's grant. A host that registers once and serves many users (the Copilot Studio style) breaks every user on day 31, including anyone who consented on day 30. Existing access tokens (60 min or less) keep working until they expire, because resource calls do not re-check the client. The DCR response includes client_id_expires_at, so a strictly RFC 7591 client could re-register, but grants are bound to client_id and every user would still have to consent again. Operators can soften this by raising the value to 90 (the maximum allowed by config.py:1204), but they cannot remove it.
reviews.fix_sketch: Make registration expiry sliding. On a successful authorization_code or refresh exchange, set client.expires_at = max(client.expires_at, now + WORKSPACE_MCP_CLIENT_REGISTRATION_DAYS). Alternatively, expire only clients that have no active grant and whose last_used_at is older than N days, via a cleanup sweep. Keep hard expiry for never-used registrations to limit DCR spam. Apply the same to research MCP. Add a test that a refresh on day 29 extends expiry and a refresh on day 45 succeeds.

title: RFC 8707 resource parameter is mandatory at authorize and on every token grant including refresh
claim: resource: str = Query(...) (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:407-418) makes a missing resource a FastAPI 422 instead of an OAuth redirect error, and the token endpoint returns invalid_target when resource is absent for all grant types including refresh_token (706-708). Generic OAuth brokers (Teams Developer Portal, Power Platform, Gemini Enterprise) may not send it and fail at sign-in or first refresh.

reviews.evidence: routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:417 `resource: str = Query(...)`. A missing parameter fails FastAPI validation with a default 422: main.py registers no RequestValidationError handler, only HTTPException, storage-policy and generic handlers at 889-938. Lines 429-430 return invalid_target for an unknown resource. Token endpoint 706-708: resource = form.get('resource') or ''; if not allowed, invalid_target. This runs before the grant_type branch, so it covers refresh_token too (the refresh branch at 745-775 re-checks the resource bound at issue time anyway). No test covers a missing resource (grep for invalid_target in backend/tests finds only an unrelated test).
reviews.correction: Code facts are exact. Two refinements. (1) The authorize endpoint never uses OAuth redirect errors for any failure: _oauth_error at 100-105 always returns JSON. So the real problem is that a missing resource fails at all, not the 422 format. (2) The MCP authorization spec requires clients to send resource on both authorization and token requests, so MCP-native hosts (Claude, Copilot Studio or M365 DCR flows) are unaffected. The risk applies to generic OAuth configurations such as Gemini Enterprise's manual client ID/secret setup and Teams Developer Portal OAuth registration. Those send the standard parameters and may not send resource, especially on token or refresh requests. This matters only once D21 is fixed.
reviews.fix_sketch: Make resource optional. At authorize: `resource: str | None = Query(None)`, defaulting to workspace_resource_uri() when absent, and still rejecting an unknown value. At the token endpoint: if resource is absent, use the resource bound in the stored code or refresh payload (already checked at 721, 767) instead of returning invalid_target. Optionally catch validation errors on the authorize route and redirect to redirect_uri with error=invalid_request when client_id and redirect_uri are valid. Add tests for authorize, code exchange and refresh without resource. Mirror the change in research MCP.

title: Workspace MCP consent is all-or-nothing: one scope outside the user's role blocks the connection
claim: Consent is refused (403) unless every requested scope is in _allowed_user_scopes (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:487-495, 184-190; mapping 73-84), and the protected-resource challenge asks for all known scopes (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:144-150). A firm-wide Copilot/Gemini agent therefore fails for roles lacking manage_intake/manage_documents, with no indication which permission is missing.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:73-84 maps each scope to required capabilities (intakes:read needs manage_intake; templates:propose needs manage_documents; documents:read/propose need manage_matters+manage_documents). :184-190 _allowed_user_scopes keeps only the scopes whose required caps are a subset of the user's caps. :487-495 GET consent request raises 403 'Your current LawHand permissions do not allow the requested access' unless requested scopes (minus offline_access) is a subset of that set. :576-581 decision repeats the check with 'Requested access is unavailable'. :245-249 token/refresh re-checks the same subset. backend/app/services/workspace_mcp_protocol.py:133-150 builds the WWW-Authenticate challenge with scope=all KNOWN_WORKSPACE_SCOPES, and :266-271 / :299 advertise all scopes. frontend/src/pages/WorkspaceMcpAuthorizePage.jsx:33 shows only the generic backend detail. It never names the missing capability. Mitigating: backend/app/services/capabilities.py:36-48 gives the seeded 'User' role manage_matters+manage_intake+manage_documents and Administrator every capability, so default roles are not blocked. Only custom roles are (the comment at :40-41 does anticipate intake/reception roles that omit capabilities). A platform-operator-only diagnostic at backend/app/routers/platform.py:2144-2155 lists per-scope requirements, but its mapping differs from the router's: documents:read there needs only manage_documents.
reviews.correction: The mechanism is real: consent is all-or-nothing, the challenge requests every scope, and the error is generic. The impact is overstated. The default seeded roles (User, Administrator) have every capability the scopes need, so a firm-wide agent fails only for users in custom roles that omit manage_intake, manage_documents or manage_matters. The Accountant and Client roles lack manage_matters and would reasonably be blocked anyway. A platform operator diagnostic can show per-scope eligibility, but nothing is exposed to the firm user or admin. That diagnostic's scope map has also drifted from the enforcing map.
reviews.fix_sketch: Two options. The minimum fix: in the 403 at workspace_mcp_oauth.py:491-495 and :578-581, list the scopes the user cannot receive and the capability each one needs, and show that on the consent page. The fuller fix: support scope down-scoping per RFC 6749 section 3.3. Grant requested ∩ allowed when the intersection is non-empty. Store the narrowed scopes in the pending request and grant, and return the narrowed 'scope' in the token response. Render 'not available with your role' items on the consent page. Per-tool capability checks (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:107-130) and the token-time recheck (:245-249) still enforce the boundary. Also derive platform.py:2144-2155 from _SCOPE_APP_CAPABILITIES so the diagnostic cannot drift.

title: MCP consent screen trusts a self-asserted client_name and admins cannot allowlist clients
claim: Any DCR client picks its client_name (workspace_mcp_oauth.py:365-372); the consent API returns only id and name (496-504) with no redirect host, publisher or verification, and WorkspaceMcpAuthorizePage.jsx:70 renders that name. The only controls are tenant/user on/off (workspace_mcp_access.py:31-43), contradicting docs/byo-harness-channel-contract.md:78-83. A registration named 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' can phish consent.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:316-372: DCR accepts any 1-200 character client_name and stores it verbatim (:328-333, :365-367). The only validation is on redirect URIs. backend/app/services/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:239-263 validate_redirect_uri accepts any HTTPS host (or http loopback), so an attacker can register a client named 'Microsoft 365 Copilot' with redirect https://attacker.example/cb. The authorize endpoint at :393-437 needs no login and redirects to the SPA consent page. GET request at :496-504 returns client {id, name} only: no redirect host, software_id, registration date or verification status. frontend/src/pages/WorkspaceMcpAuthorizePage.jsx:70 renders request.client?.name as 'Application'. backend/app/services/workspace_mcp_access.py:31-43 and the user flag at workspace_mcp_oauth.py:231-235 and :536-543 are the only controls. The WorkspaceMCPClient model (backend/app/models/workspace_mcp_client.py:15-52) and TenantSettings have no allowlist field. workspace_mcp_oauth.py:98-107 notes the pilot allowlist was retired. DCR is off by default (backend/app/config.py:463), but scripts/prod_env_preflight.sh:611-612 requires it to be true whenever workspace MCP is enabled in production. Mitigation: the consent copy at WorkspaceMcpAuthorizePage.jsx:81-84 tells users to approve only cleared applications.
reviews.correction: The core finding stands. Two points of nuance. The exposure exists only where WORKSPACE_MCP_ENABLED is on, but prod preflight then forces DCR on, so every production deployment with workspace MCP is exposed. docs/byo-harness-channel-contract.md:78-80 ('The firm decides which external accounts and vendors it permits') is a governance statement, not an explicit promise of a technical allowlist. 'Contradicting' is therefore slightly strong, but the firm has no technical means to enforce that decision.
reviews.fix_sketch: (1) On the consent page, show the redirect host(s), software_id and version, and the registration age. Show an 'Unverified application' badge unless the client matches a platform-maintained registry of verified clients (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot Studio and so on) keyed on exact redirect_uri or software_statement. (2) At DCR, reject or flag client_names that impersonate registry entries. (3) Add a tenant-admin policy: 'allow any client' vs an allowlist of verified clients or redirect hosts, stored in TenantSettings. Enforce it in get_workspace_authorization_request, decide_workspace_authorization and _load_grant_actor, and expose it in Admin settings. (4) Audit consent grants with the redirect host.

title: BYOK silently falls back to platform providers, and reconfiguring without the key erases it
claim: In llm_routing.py:540-573, decrypt failure or a missing key (bare except at 545-546) lets resolution continue to profile and platform routes. configure_customer_llm replaces customer_llm_config and keeps encrypted_api_key only if api_key is resent (admin.py:1557-1577) yet returns ok with use_customer_llm=true. This violates 'no platform fallback unless the firm explicitly authorizes one' (docs/standard-premium-byok-billing-plan-2026-08-16.md:212-213).

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/llm_routing.py:534-571: the BYOK branch runs only if decrypt_token succeeds. :543-546 wraps decrypt_token(ts.customer_llm_config.get('encrypted_api_key','')) in a bare 'except Exception: pass'. backend/app/services/token_vault.py:96-97 decrypt_token('') raises InvalidToken, which is swallowed. With raw_key empty, execution falls through to profile, tenant and platform routes (:573-640) with no log or error. backend/app/routers/admin.py:1557-1577 overwrites customer_llm_config with {endpoint, deployment} and adds encrypted_api_key only if body.api_key is truthy. It also accepts use_customer_llm=true with no key on first enable, and returns status ok. Additional bypasses: an explicit requested_model (:511-522) and the Background tier (:488-508, deliberate) skip BYOK entirely. Scope limiters: the only caller is frontend/src/api.js:921-924, with no page using it, so BYOK is API-only. docs/standard-premium-byok-billing-plan-2026-08-16.md:205-218 describes lines 212-213 as the future BYOK product and says 'The existing BYOK schema and direct-routing code are migration material, not a customer launch surface.' llm_routing.py:373-402 route_matter_context_allowed already refuses matter context on the 'customer' route. No test covers the fallback. Only backend/tests/test_onboarding.py:189-200 sets the flag.
reviews.correction: The fail-open fallback and the key-erasing reconfigure are exactly as described. The 'violates the plan' framing is overstated: the cited plan lines describe a future replacement BYOK product, and the same section declares the current code non-launch migration material. Nothing in the UI can configure BYOK (API only), so few if any firms can be in this state. One twist in the claim's favor: a working BYOK route is blocked from matter context (llm_routing.py:394-402), while the fallback platform/profile route may admit it. A silent fallback can therefore send matter data to platform providers that a working BYOK route never would.
reviews.fix_sketch: In resolve_llm_route, when use_customer_llm is true and the key is missing or undecryptable, log a warning and return a route the broker refuses (for example resolved_route='customer-unavailable', or raise a route-config error). Fall back only when an explicit tenant flag such as customer_llm_config['allow_platform_fallback'] is set. In configure_customer_llm, keep the existing encrypted_api_key when api_key is omitted and the provider is unchanged, require api_key on first enable, and call invalidate_llm_route_cache(tenant_id). Add a GET status endpoint returning key_present, provider and endpoint host. Add tests for the decrypt-failure and missing-key paths.

title: BYOK Azure endpoint is accepted without the /openai/v1 path and never connection-tested
claim: The byok_security normalizer (byok_security.py:67-73) keeps whatever path the admin supplied and LLMService points the plain OpenAI client at it (llm.py:272-275); the portal resource URL (https://x.openai.azure.com/) is accepted though OpenAI-SDK calls need /openai/v1/. No test at save time (admin.py:1536-1571), and llm_availability probes only gateway aliases (llm_availability.py:40-130). Admins can save a 'working' config where every AI call fails.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/byok_security.py:38-73: for 'copilot' the host must end in an Azure suffix (:58-59). The path is kept as supplied and gets a trailing slash (:67-73), so 'https://x.openai.azure.com/' normalizes to itself. There is no check for /openai/v1/. backend/app/services/llm.py:255-275 _client_for builds AsyncOpenAI(api_key=..., base_url=<that URL>), so chat calls go to https://x.openai.azure.com/chat/completions, which Azure does not serve. The OpenAI-SDK-compatible path is /openai/v1/. backend/tests/test_byok_security.py:36-40 shows the intended form ('.../openai/v1' becomes '.../openai/v1/') but nothing enforces it. backend/app/routers/admin.py:1536-1577 validates only format and commits without a live test. backend/app/services/llm_availability.py:1-4 and :40-47 probe platform gateway aliases ('active customer LLM routes' means platform tiers), not tenant BYOK. The same API-only and non-launch caveats apply as for D66: frontend/src/api.js:921-924 has no UI caller, and docs/standard-premium-byok-billing-plan-2026-08-16.md:209-218 lists 'key test/rotation' as future BYOK work.
reviews.correction: Technically accurate: the resource URL is accepted, and no save-time or availability test exists for BYOK. Severity is lower than stated because there is no UI to save this config (API only), and the plan explicitly treats the current BYOK path as non-launch migration material with key testing planned. Also, 'every AI call fails' covers only BYOK-routed non-matter calls. Matter-context calls are already refused on the customer route (llm_routing.py:394-402), and Background-tier calls never use BYOK.
reviews.fix_sketch: In normalize_customer_llm_endpoint('copilot'), map an empty or '/' path to '/openai/v1/', and reject any path other than /openai/v1/ (or the documented Foundry equivalents). In configure_customer_llm, run a bounded connection test before commit (AsyncOpenAI(...).models.list() or a 1-token chat against the deployment, 10s timeout, error redacted) and return a 400 with the provider status on failure. Add unit tests for the resource-URL normalization.

title: BYOK Gemini only supports a global AI Studio key with no paid-tier, region or Vertex controls
claim: The only Gemini option is the fixed generativelanguage.googleapis.com endpoint with an API key (byok_security.py:10-32); nothing checks the key belongs to a paid Cloud-Billing project, there is no regional/Vertex option, and the default model is hard-coded gemini-2.0-flash (llm_routing.py:555). A free-tier key can expose client content to provider training; residency-constrained firms cannot use their own Gemini.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/byok_security.py:10 fixes GEMINI_OPENAI_ENDPOINT to https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/, and :29-32 rejects any other Gemini endpoint. There is no Vertex AI or regional option and no tier or billing check. backend/app/routers/admin.py:1507-1512 CustomerLLMConfigRequest has only provider, api_key, endpoint and deployment, with no data-policy, region or tier fields. backend/app/services/llm_routing.py:552-557 falls back to model 'gemini-2.0-flash' only when no deployment is supplied, because validate_customer_llm_deployment (byok_security.py:76-86) makes deployment optional for Gemini. It tries ts.default_llm_model first, which normally holds a platform gateway alias that Google would not recognize. docs/standard-premium-byok-billing-plan-2026-08-16.md:205-218 already lists 'provider-specific DPA, region, retention, and enterprise-account checks' as future BYOK work and calls the current path non-launch migration material. frontend/src/api.js:921-924 has no UI caller. llm_routing.py:394-402 blocks matter context on the customer route, which limits what client content reaches Gemini through BYOK.
reviews.correction: The facts are right: global AI Studio endpoint only, no paid-tier/region/Vertex controls, hard-coded default model. It is a known, documented product gap in a non-launched, API-only path, not a defect in a shipped feature. Exposure of 'client content' is also reduced because route_matter_context_allowed refuses matter context on the customer route. Non-matter prompts (drafting, chat) can still reach a free-tier key. One further issue: the default-model fallback prefers ts.default_llm_model, typically a LiteLLM alias, before the hard-coded Gemini id, so a Gemini BYOK tenant can end up sending an alias Google rejects.
reviews.fix_sketch: This needs a product decision under the planned BYOK redesign. Either keep BYOK disabled server-side, gated by a feature flag defaulting off, until it is rebuilt, or add a Vertex AI adapter (project, region, service-account credentials via token_vault) and a required admin attestation that an AI Studio key is on a paid Cloud Billing project. Require an explicit Gemini model, validated against the provider's models.list at save time, instead of the hard-coded default. Never reuse ts.default_llm_model (a gateway alias) for a direct-provider route.

title: 'copilot'/'gemini' BYOK path is mislabelled as a subscription and bypasses the LiteLLM gateway
claim: The admin endpoint says 'use their own LLM subscription (Gemini/Copilot)' (admin.py:1509-1521) but provider 'copilot' is an Azure OpenAI resource (byok_security.py:33-58; config.py:155 'Azure OpenAI (Copilot backend)'; tenant.py:221-226). The stored key bypasses the LiteLLM gateway (llm.py:261-275) and skips gateway accounting metadata (llm.py:351), contradicting TASKS.md:2622 (direct paths removed) and ECO-20 (TASKS.md:479-481) and the plan (docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:55-57). AZURE_OPENAI_* and GEMINI_API_KEY settings are dead (config.py:156-161). Invites the misconception that a firm's M365 Copilot licence powers LawHand and escapes gateway approval/metering.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/admin.py:1509 (provider comment "gemini" | "copilot"), 1515-1521 (POST /admin/customer-llm/configure, docstring 'use their own LLM subscription (Gemini/Copilot)', guarded only by tenant require_admin). backend/app/services/byok_security.py:9-58: 'gemini' is pinned to generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai, while 'copilot' requires an Azure OpenAI endpoint (*.openai.azure.com etc.) and a deployment (73-83), so it is Azure OpenAI BYOK, not M365 Copilot. backend/app/services/llm_routing.py:529-571: when use_customer_llm is set it returns resolved_route='customer' with the decrypted key and a hard-coded 'gemini-2.0-flash' default. backend/app/services/llm.py:252-275 (_client_for builds AsyncOpenAI directly against the tenant endpoint, bypassing LiteLLM) and 350-355 (litellm_metadata only when `not customer_api_key`). backend/app/config.py:156-162: AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT/KEY/DEPLOYMENT and GEMINI_API_KEY are defined, and a repo-wide grep finds no other reference, so they are dead. backend/app/models/tenant.py:221-226 comment 'use their own Gemini/Copilot subscription'. TASKS.md:2622 marks the direct Azure/Gemini paths as removed [x]. TASKS.md:479-481 ECO-20 and docs/workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:55-57 forbid treating a Copilot or Gemini subscription as capacity. Mitigations I found: frontend/src/api.js:921-924 exports configureCustomerLLM/resetCustomerLLM but no component imports them, so no UI reaches this. llm_routing.py:384-401 treats the 'customer' route as fail-closed for confidential matter context. chat.py:1255-1268, 2970-2980 and 4010-4020 still write usage records (tokens) for customer routes, at zero cost.
reviews.correction: The mislabel, the gateway bypass, the dead settings and the policy contradiction are all real. It is overstated in three ways. (1) No UI exposes the feature: it is reachable only when a tenant admin calls the API directly. (2) It does not fully escape metering. LiteLLM gateway accounting and approval are bypassed, but the app still records tokens in usage_records (at $0), and the route cannot receive matter context (fail-closed). (3) ECO-20 is an open [ ] roadmap item, not a shipped guarantee. The contradiction is with TASKS.md:2622 [x] and the plan's policy line. Nothing in the code claims an M365 Copilot licence is used. The risk comes from naming and docstrings.
reviews.fix_sketch: Product decision first. Option A (recommended, small): remove BYOK. Make resolve_llm_route ignore use_customer_llm, return 410 from /admin/customer-llm/configure, drop configureCustomerLLM/resetCustomerLLM from api.js, delete AZURE_OPENAI_* and GEMINI_API_KEY from config.py, and add a migration to null out existing customer_llm_config. Option B: keep BYOK but rename provider 'copilot' to 'azure_openai' (accept the old value as an alias), rewrite the admin.py, tenant.py and llm_routing comments to say 'your own Azure OpenAI / Gemini API key (not a Microsoft 365 Copilot or Google One subscription)', and send BYOK through LiteLLM as tenant-scoped model deployments that hold the tenant key so gateway metadata, approval and fallback still apply. Drop the hard-coded 'gemini-2.0-flash' default. Under either option, update TASKS.md 1202/ECO-20 and add a test that customer routes carry gateway metadata or are rejected.

title: Microsoft 365 / Google disconnect is not exposed in the admin UI, does not revoke at the provider, and does not purge synced data
claim: POST /integrations/microsoft/disconnect and /google/disconnect exist (integrations.py:2105-2166) but api.js has no wrapper (api.js:798-835) and ProviderCard shows only Connect/Re-authorize (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:760-769). The endpoints delete tokens locally (token_vault.py:382-399) without revoking at Microsoft/Google, and leave Gmail subjects, snippets and participants in cloud_metadata_index. The legal notice (LegalNoticePage.jsx:58) and admin guide (04-integrations.md:85-91) promise an in-app disconnect, which Google Limited Use verification relies on.

reviews.evidence: Backend: POST /microsoft/disconnect and /google/disconnect (integrations.py:2105-2166) call _revoke_all_provider_tokens (integrations.py:2064-2101), which decrypts every tenant and per-user token and calls revoke_provider_token. For Google that POSTs to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke (token_vault.py:360-379, 399-409). For Microsoft, revoke_microsoft_token is a deliberate no-op because there is no per-token revoke API (token_vault.py:382-396). Git history shows the helper existed before the review (02f6a72, 2026-09-16). Neither endpoint touches CloudMetadata. The model stores title, owner_email, participants and snippet (cloud_metadata.py:28-70), and Gmail/Outlook sync writes subjects, participants and 500-char snippets (cloud_sync.py:535-557, 795-813). The only CloudMetadata deletes are in storage_migration*.py. search_index always runs regardless of credentials ('Always include the locally-synced metadata index', cloud_search.py:321-333), so the stale email metadata stays searchable after disconnect. DELETE /cloud-search/cache clears only the Redis cache (cloud_admin.py:616-637). Frontend: on origin/main, api.js has no Google/Microsoft disconnect wrapper and ProviderCard shows only Connect/Re-authorize. On this branch HEAD, api.js:838-839 adds disconnectCloudProvider and IntegrationsPanel.jsx:268-287, 1004-1011 adds a confirmed Disconnect button (tests at IntegrationsPanel.test.jsx:431-448). Promises: LegalNoticePage.jsx:58 ('An administrator may disconnect Google at any time from the workspace integration settings') and 04-integrations.md:85-91.
reviews.correction: 'Does not revoke at Google' is wrong: Google tokens (tenant and every per-user token) are revoked at the provider before deletion, and were before the review. Microsoft revocation is absent because of a platform limitation, and this is documented in code. 'Not exposed in the admin UI' is true on origin/main but fixed on this branch (ca6812e, PR #610 unmerged). What remains fully true: disconnect never purges cloud_metadata_index. Gmail/Outlook subjects, snippets, participants and Drive/OneDrive titles stay stored and returned by search_index. The new confirm dialog does not mention this. There is also no per-user self-disconnect.
reviews.fix_sketch: In both disconnect endpoints, after revocation run delete(CloudMetadata).where(tenant_id==..., provider==...) and invalidate the cloud-search Redis cache (cache_manager.invalidate_cloud_search_cache), inside the same transaction. Alternatively, filter search_index to providers with an active TenantCredential as defense in depth. Update the confirm copy to state that the search index is cleared and that Microsoft access must also be removed in Entra (Enterprise applications) because Microsoft has no per-token revoke. Add a per-user disconnect endpoint (revoke plus delete the UserOAuthToken for the caller) surfaced in ConnectedAccountsCard. Add backend tests asserting that index rows are gone and that search returns nothing post-disconnect.

title: Admin OAuth errors always land on /onboarding and the Cloud section never shows the connect result
claim: _error_redirect sends every admin-intent error to /onboarding?error=... even when onboarding is completed (integrations.py:1789-1807); on success the redirect to /admin?tab=integrations&integration=cloud&connected=<provider> is ignored because IntegrationsPanel never reads connected/error (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:145-158), unlike ZoomPanel.jsx:89-105 and CalendarPage.jsx:508-548. A completed tenant sees the error above 'Setup Complete!' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:73-77, 717), contradicting 04-integrations.md:47,51.

reviews.evidence:
Backend (same on main and HEAD): _error_redirect (integrations.py:1790-1807) returns /onboarding?error=&provider=

for every non-zoom-phone, non-user intent, with no onboarding_completed check. By contrast, _post_connect_redirect checks Tenant.onboarding_completed and sends completed tenants to /admin?tab=integrations&integration=cloud&connected=

(integrations.py:1756-1775). invalid_state paths call _error_redirect with the default intent 'admin' (integrations.py:509-514, 735-740), so they also land on /onboarding, which is an adminOnly route (App.jsx:500-501). OnboardingWizard reads ?error into a banner (OnboardingWizard.jsx:70-72 at HEAD). The banner renders above all step content (OnboardingWizard.jsx:312-321), including STEP.COMPLETE, which a completed tenant resolves to (OnboardingWizard.jsx:56-60, 705-712 'Setup Complete!'). Panel: on origin/main, IntegrationsPanel has no URLSearchParams/useSearchParams/location.search (grep exit 1), so ?connected was ignored. On this branch HEAD, readConnectReturn (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:155-165, 180, 337-348) shows the connected and error notices. The error branch is still unreachable, because the backend never sends admin errors to /admin. Docs 04-integrations.md:47 and :51 are unchanged.
reviews.correction: The success half ('Cloud section never shows the connect result') is fixed on this branch (ca6812e, not yet on origin/main). The error half remains on both. After PR #610 the error message is also friendlier (shared oauthErrorMessage), but it still appears in the setup wizard above 'Setup Complete!'. The impact is confusing navigation with an obvious 'Go to Admin Panel' exit, not a failure to connect, so medium is overstated.
reviews.fix_sketch:
Make admin-intent errors return to the panel for completed tenants. The cheapest route is to store a return_to ('admin' or 'onboarding') in the OAuth state meta at connect time: handleReauthorize passes &return_to=admin, and the wizard omits it. _error_redirect(provider, code, intent, return_to) then emits /admin?tab=integrations&integration=cloud&error=&provider=

, which readConnectReturn already renders. For invalid_state, where no meta exists, fall back to a completed-tenant DB lookup like _post_connect_redirect does, or keep /onboarding. Update test_google_onboarding_callback.py and test_onboarding_step_plumbing.py, strip error/connected params after showing them (history.replaceState, as ZoomPanel.jsx:101-105 does), and align 04-integrations.md:47,51.

title: Saving a SharePoint library silently switches the primary storage provider
claim: SharePointBindingCard always sends is_primary: true (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:485-493); the backend sets primary_cloud_provider='sharepoint' (cloud_admin.py:397-405) and the panel updates the selector (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:338), bypassing PrimaryCloudSelector's confirmation (351-354). The binding is stored 'configured' with no write check, repointing all new matter writes without warning.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/components/IntegrationsPanel.jsx:620-628: SharePointBindingCard.handleSave always sends `is_primary: true`. The claim cited :485-493, but the code has moved. :469-474: onSaved calls `setPrimaryCloud(binding?.is_primary ? 'sharepoint' : primaryCloud)`. :486-490 and :491-547: PrimaryCloudSelector requires a 'Confirm change' step and warns that writes fail if the provider is not connected. The SharePoint card has no such step; its button reads only 'Save SharePoint binding' (:712-716). backend/app/routers/cloud_admin.py:115-122: SharePointBindingRequest.is_primary defaults to True. :381-406: the handler stores the binding with health='configured' and makes no Graph write or permission probe. When is_primary is set it runs only assert_provider_change_allowed (storage_migration.py:703-731), which blocks during an active or completed migration, and then sets primary_cloud_provider='sharepoint'. backend/app/services/cloud_init.py:1312-1320: sharepoint writes then resolve drive_id from this binding.
reviews.correction: Line numbers are stale: is_primary is at IntegrationsPanel.jsx:627, the onSaved handler is at :469-474, and the confirmation comment is at :486-490. 'Silently' is a bit strong. The card text says the library is 'used for matter folders and uploads', and the provider selector shows 'Microsoft SharePoint' after saving. There is still no warning that the firm-wide primary provider will switch. The backend also refuses the switch (409) during an active or completed storage migration.
reviews.fix_sketch: In SharePointBindingCard, add a 'Make this the primary provider for new matter documents' checkbox. Default it to checked only when primaryCloud is already 'sharepoint' or unset. When saving would change the primary provider, show the same amber confirm step that PrimaryCloudSelector uses. Pass the checkbox value as is_primary. In the backend, change the SharePointBindingRequest.is_primary default to False. Before setting health, do a cheap Graph probe on the drive (GET /drives/{id}/root, or create and delete a temp folder). Store the result as health 'verified' or 'write_failed' and return 424 if the probe fails.

title: 'Granted by' never renders and the deactivated-grantor warning is never shown
claim: ProviderCard reads info.service_account_email (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:723-725) but GET /admin/permissions never returns it (admin.py:1706-1797; only the test fixture IntegrationsPanel.test.jsx:69 has it). The 'User X who granted consent is deactivated' warning exists only in /admin/integrations/health (admin.py:365-376), whose client getIntegrationsHealth (api.js:799-800) is never called. Admins cannot see who owns the firm grant before offboarding them.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/components/IntegrationsPanel.jsx:956-961 (the claim cited :723-725): the 'Granted by' line and the 'act as' text read info.service_account_email. :5 and :250-258: the panel's only data source is getAdminPermissions(). backend/app/routers/admin.py:1640-1798: audit_provider returns scopes, freshness and tier fields but no service_account_email or grantor fields. Only the test fixture has the field (IntegrationsPanel.test.jsx:77 asserts it at :152). admin.py:309-398: /admin/integrations/health resolves the grantor and builds the 'User X who granted consent is deactivated' warning at :367-369. frontend/src/api.js:799-800: getIntegrationsHealth is defined, but a repo-wide grep finds no caller. Counter-evidence: admin.py:240-306 deactivate_user returns 400 'This user granted org-wide OAuth consent... Re-authorize with another admin first' unless force=true. frontend/src/pages/AdminPage.jsx:558-576 turns that error into a destructive confirm dialog ('Deactivate consent owner?'). licensing.py:183-194 also warns when the grantor loses their license.
reviews.correction: The dead 'Granted by' line and the unused health warning are real. The claimed impact is overstated. Admins do get a blocking warning before offboarding the consent owner: the backend returns 400 and AdminPage shows a confirm dialog. What is missing is the ability to see the grant owner ahead of time on the Integrations page. The post-hoc 'grantor is deactivated' warning after a forced deactivation is also never shown. Line refs are stale: the UI is at IntegrationsPanel.jsx:956-961 and the fixture at test:77.
reviews.fix_sketch: In admin.py audit_provider, add service_account_email, granted_by_user_email and granted_by_user_active, plus a 'warning' string built the same way as integration_health at :367-377. The simplest route is to factor the grantor lookup into a shared helper. Render the grantor and the amber warning in ProviderCard. Then either delete getIntegrationsHealth or have the hub use it. Update IntegrationsPanel.test.jsx so the fixture matches the real payload, and add a backend test for the new fields.

title: Cloud Search reports Available/Connected/Enabled while the connection is broken
claim: The hub pill returns 'Available' for any cloud tone except 'off', including 'Needs attention' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:106-110). The Cloud Search status endpoint filters only is_active, not health, so revoked/refresh_failed credentials show 'Connected' (cloud_admin.py:170-176, 257-263), and it hard-codes enabled: True even in its error branch (219-238, 267-272); CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:52-57,73 ignores status:'error'.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/components/IntegrationsHub.jsx:46-52: cloudStatus returns tone 'warn'/'Needs attention' for overall_health 'attention_needed'. :106-110: the Cloud Search status returns {tone:'ok', label:'Available'} for anything other than tone 'off', including 'warn'. backend/app/routers/cloud_admin.py:170-177: credentials are filtered only on is_active. :258-268: any active credential is reported as connected=True. :220-240: the exception branch returns 'enabled': True with status 'error'. :270-275: the success path also hard-codes enabled: True and ignores the CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED master flag (config.py:569, which cloud_search.py:577 honours). frontend/src/pages/CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:40-57,73,95 never reads status.status or status.error, so the error payload renders as 'Enabled', '0 items indexed' and 'Not connected... Connect in Settings'. Counter-evidence: backend/app/services/token_vault.py:77-89 sets is_active=False whenever health becomes 'revoked' (invalid_grant). integration_observability.py:35-38 derives 'revoked' only from is_active False, and :59-78 re-activates only on fresh consent.
reviews.correction: Revoked credentials do NOT show 'Connected'. Every path that sets health='revoked' also sets is_active=False, so the is_active filter excludes them. Only 'refresh_failed' (a transient refresh error) and 'missing_scopes' credentials show as Connected. 'Needs attention' can also come from missing scopes or from the other provider, so 'Available' is not always wrong. The hard-coded enabled:True is worse than claimed because it also ignores the CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED flag. Severity is low: the adjacent Cloud accounts card already shows 'Needs attention'.
reviews.fix_sketch: Backend: return 'enabled': settings.CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED, and 'enabled': None or False in the error branch. Include cred.health per provider and set connected only when health is not in {'revoked','refresh_failed'}, or add a 'degraded' flag. Hub: map cloud tone 'warn' to {tone:'warn', label:'Check cloud connection'}. CloudSearchAdmin: when status.status === 'error', render an error banner with a retry instead of the Enabled badge, and show a warning badge per provider when health is not healthy.

title: No per-user disconnect for personal Microsoft/Google connections
claim: The Microsoft and Google disconnect endpoints (integrations.py:2105-2167) are admin-only and delete every user's UserOAuthToken for the tenant; unlike Zoom's per-user disconnect (integrations.py:2368-2391), there is no self-service endpoint or frontend control (api.js exposes only Zoom/QBO helpers, api.js:900-914, 2840). An attorney cannot revoke LawHand's Mail.Read/Mail.Send/Files access to their own mailbox without an admin disconnecting the whole firm.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/integrations.py:2105-2134 (microsoft) and 2137-2166 (google) raise 403 unless user.role=='admin'. They then call _revoke_all_provider_tokens (2060-2103, which revokes every TenantCredential and UserOAuthToken for the provider) and delete both the tenant's TenantCredential and every user's UserOAuthToken for that provider. By contrast, zoom_disconnect (integrations.py:2369-2391) lets any user delete only their own UserOAuthToken (user_id == user.id). A grep for delete(UserOAuthToken) finds only 2127, 2159 and 2385, so no per-user Microsoft/Google path exists. ConnectedAccountsCard.jsx (rendered in ProfilePage.jsx:278) shows personal Microsoft/Google status from /auth/calendar-providers (auth.py:2730-2790) but has no disconnect control.
reviews.correction: Minor inaccuracy: api.js is not limited to Zoom/QBO helpers. It also exports disconnectCloudProvider (api.js:838-839), used by the admin IntegrationsPanel (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:281), but that helper hits the firm-wide admin endpoints, so the conclusion stands. Partial mitigation: a user can revoke consent in their Microsoft or Google account portal, and LawHand then reports refresh_failed (auth.py:2760-2777). The encrypted refresh token row still stays in LawHand's database.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add POST /integrations/{microsoft|google}/disconnect/me for any authenticated user. It selects UserOAuthToken rows WHERE tenant_id=current, user_id=current and provider=p, calls the existing revoke_provider_token for each (reusing the _revoke_all_provider_tokens body), deletes them, and leaves TenantCredential alone. Audit the per-user token consumers (calendar_sync, microsoft_mail/google_mail capture, teams, document_sync, cloud_search) so they degrade to 'not connected' cleanly, and tear down any per-user watch or subscription state. Frontend: add disconnectMyCloudAccount(provider) in api.js and a 'Disconnect' button with confirm copy in ConnectedAccountsCard for connected or needs_reconnect providers, stating that the firm connection is unaffected. Add backend tests for self-scope and for leaving other users' and tenant credentials intact.

title: 'Connect in Admin > Integrations' is a silent dead end for non-admin users
claim: The empty Cloud Files state calls navigate('/admin') (MatterDetailPage.jsx:1302-1309), but /admin is a financeOnly ShellRoute (App.jsx:490-491) and ProtectedRoute redirects users without finance access to their default route (App.jsx:210-212). Other non-actionable admin pointers: CloudFolderCard copy (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:219-223), StorageReadinessNotice.jsx:30, and the send error 'Reconnect ... in Integrations' (connected_mail.py:233-239).

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/pages/MatterDetailPage.jsx:1302-1309: when !cloudFiles.connected the panel shows 'No cloud integrations connected.' and a button that calls navigate('/admin'). App.jsx:490-491 declares /admin as ShellRoute financeOnly. App.jsx:173-180 hasFinanceAccess needs view_billing or manage_billing (or the legacy admin/accountant role). App.jsx:211-213 redirects everyone else to user.default_route || '/matters', silently. Even for admins, AdminPage.jsx:1395-1404 opens the first tab (Users), not Integrations, because no ?tab=integrations is passed. The connected:false branch also appears on any fetch error, since loadCloudFiles' catch sets {connected:false, files:[]} (MatterDetailPage.jsx:560-566), and backend matters.py:227-235 returns connected:false only when the tenant has no active TenantCredential. The CloudFolderCard failure copy (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:218-222) points at 'Administration → Integrations → Cloud'. backend/app/services/connected_mail.py:233-239 builds 'Reconnect <provider> in Integrations ...' and uses it both for per-user sends (line 277) and for the firm mailbox (line 424).
reviews.correction: The core dead-end CTA is real. Two of the listed 'other pointers' are overstated. StorageReadinessNotice.jsx:30 already says 'Your workspace administrator can repair the connection in Cloud settings' and offers a working 'Check connection again' retry, so it is correctly aimed at an admin and is not a dead end. The connected_mail message misdirects rather than dead-ends: for a personal-mailbox send, the actual fix is in Profile → Connected accounts (ProfilePage.jsx:278), not 'Integrations'. The empty state appears only for tenants with no active cloud credential, or after a load error. That limits reach, so low rather than medium.
reviews.fix_sketch: In MatterDetailPage, render the CTA only when the user can reach the integrations tab (admin, or finance roles whose adminTabsFor includes integrations), and navigate to '/admin?tab=integrations'. Otherwise show 'Ask your firm administrator to connect Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace.' Make loadCloudFiles' catch set an error state ('Cloud files could not be loaded - Retry') instead of connected:false. Make the CloudFolderCard failure copy role-aware in the same way. In connected_mail._reconnect_detail, take a firm_mailbox flag: for personal sends say 'Reconnect Microsoft 365 in Profile → Connected accounts', and for the firm mailbox say 'Ask an administrator to reconnect in Admin → Integrations'.

title: 'Connect Calendar' button silently requests mailbox read/send and full file access
claim: The CalendarPage button 'Connect Calendar' / 'Connect your calendar to sync events' (CalendarPage.jsx:862-871) redirects immediately (778-781) to intent=user, which requests MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES 'offline_access User.Read Mail.Read Mail.Send Files.ReadWrite.All Calendars.ReadWrite' or Google gmail.readonly, gmail.send, calendar and drive (integrations.py:256-265), with no explainer before consent.

reviews.correction: The code matches the claim. The Calendar 'Connect Calendar' button redirects straight to intent=user, and that requests mail read, mail send, all-files access and calendar scopes. 'Silently' goes too far, though. Google always shows its consent screen listing the scopes, because the connect URL sets prompt=consent. Microsoft uses prompt=select_account, so its consent screen appears unless consent was already granted; in tenants with org-wide admin consent the user may see nothing. The gap is that LawHand shows no explanation of its own and the label understates the grant. An explanation already exists on the Profile page (ConnectedAccountsCard lists what connecting allows), but the Calendar button and the Reconnect link in the banner bypass it. Also, when connectProvider is null the button defaults to 'microsoft', even for Google-only firms.
reviews.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarPage.jsx:862-871 shows the Connect button, rendered only when calendarProvider is null. CalendarPage.jsx:778-781: handleConnectCalendar calls connectCalendarIntegration(connectProvider || 'microsoft'). frontend/src/api.js:2309-2311 sets window.location.href to /integrations/{provider}/connect?intent=user with no dialog. backend/app/routers/integrations.py:256-265 defines MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES as 'offline_access User.Read Mail.Read Mail.Send Files.ReadWrite.All Calendars.ReadWrite' and GOOGLE_USER_SCOPES as gmail.readonly, gmail.send, calendar and drive (Mail.Send and gmail.send come from backend/app/services/connected_mail.py:44-45). integrations.py:482 and 487-494 use the Microsoft user scopes with prompt=select_account. integrations.py:703-711 uses Google user scopes with prompt=consent. frontend/src/components/ConnectedAccountsCard.jsx:4-24 and 108-121 already hold the plain-language 'What connecting allows' copy, used only from ProfilePage.jsx:278.
reviews.fix_sketch: Export the PROVIDERS 'allows' copy from ConnectedAccountsCard, or move it to a shared module. In CalendarPage, change handleConnectCalendar and the banner's Reconnect button to open a small confirm dialog that names the provider, lists those permissions and has Continue/Cancel; call connectCalendarIntegration only on Continue. Rename the button to 'Connect Microsoft 365' or 'Connect Google', or add a 'Manage connected accounts' link to /profile. Let the user pick a provider when the tenant has both, instead of defaulting to microsoft. Add a Vitest check that clicking Connect shows the permission list before any redirect.

title: Matter cloud 'connected' is true when any tenant credential exists, including Zoom
claim: _build_matter_cloud_files_response returns connected=True if any active TenantCredential exists, including zoom/zoom_phone (matters.py:227-235; integrations.py:978, 1183-1185). The UI then shows 'Connected', a 'Cloud' badge on every conversation and 'Cloud context active — AI chats here have access to matter files from your connected OneDrive, SharePoint, and Google Drive' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:99-103, 1279-1283, 1809-1815).

reviews.correction: Accurate. Two further cases also count as connected: a Microsoft-only tenant still gets copy naming Google Drive, and an is_active credential whose health is refresh_failed still counts as connected.
reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/matters.py:221-235: _build_matter_cloud_files_response selects every TenantCredential with is_active true and no provider filter, and returns connected false only when there are none. matters.py:252-278 returns connected:true on every other path. backend/app/routers/integrations.py:975-986 (zoom) and 1182-1195 (ZOOM_PHONE_PROVIDER) insert TenantCredential rows, so a tenant with only Zoom has creds. The route is at matters.py:2878-2889 and is also reused by the cloud-sync response at matters.py:3414-3426. frontend/src/pages/MatterDetailPage.jsx:1279-1283 shows the 'Connected' badge. MatterDetailPage.jsx:99-103 and 1835 pass cloudConnected={cloudFiles?.connected} to show a 'Cloud' badge on every conversation. MatterDetailPage.jsx:1809-1815 shows the 'Cloud context active' text naming OneDrive, SharePoint and Google Drive unconditionally.
reviews.fix_sketch: Backend: filter the credential query to provider in ('microsoft','google'), and optionally drop health=='refresh_failed'. Return connected plus a providers list, e.g. the intersection of the connected storage providers with the keys of matter.cloud_folder (onedrive, sharepoint, google_drive). Frontend: render the Cloud Context notice and the Cloud badge only when that list is non-empty, and name only those providers (e.g. 'AI can read this matter's SharePoint folder'). Add a backend test for a tenant with only Zoom credentials (expect connected false) and a frontend test for the provider-specific copy.

title: Matter cloud-file errors are shown as 'no files' or 'not connected'
claim: Any fetch error sets {connected:false} and renders 'No cloud integrations connected' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:560-567); a backend search exception such as an expired token returns {files:[], connected:true} (matters.py:259-263), rendering 'No cloud files found matching this matter.' (MatterDetailPage.jsx:1310-1313); MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:407-413 also swallows errors. No reconnect action is shown.

reviews.correction: The core is real, but the mechanism cited for an expired token is wrong. An expired or revoked token does not reach the except branch at matters.py:259-263. CloudSearchService._prefetch_token turns lookup failures into None, get_fresh_user_token returns None when a refresh fails, the provider is then skipped, and per-source failures are swallowed. The normal return then produces connected:true with an empty list, so the result is the same ('No cloud files found matching this matter.'). The except branch covers only unexpected errors. 'No reconnect action is shown' is not quite right: after a fetch error the connected:false state shows a 'Connect in Admin → Integrations →' button that navigates to /admin. That is the wrong action for a transient error and for non-admins, but it is not absent. In MatterDocumentsTab the swallowed error only hides the Synced Cloud Files section; it shows no false message.
reviews.evidence: frontend/src/pages/MatterDetailPage.jsx:560-567: loadCloudFiles catch sets {connected:false, files:[]}. MatterDetailPage.jsx:1302-1309 then renders 'No cloud integrations connected.' with navigate('/admin'), and 1310-1313 renders 'No cloud files found matching this matter.' when files is empty. backend/app/routers/matters.py:259-263: the except branch returns {files:[], connected:True}. backend/app/services/cloud_search.py:134-137 (docstring: failures swallowed per source), 185-204 (provider skipped when the prefetched token is None) and 351-364 (_prefetch_token returns None on exception). backend/app/services/token_vault.py:438-474: get_fresh_user_token returns None when there is no row or no refresh token, or the refresh fails. frontend/src/components/MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:407-413: .catch(() => {}), and 736 renders the section only when cloudFiles.length > 0.
reviews.fix_sketch: Backend: have CloudSearchService.search report per-provider outcomes, e.g. a list of {provider, status: ok|no_token|needs_reconnect|error|timeout}. _build_matter_cloud_files_response should return that as provider_status, and the except branch should return connected:true with error:'search_failed' instead of a bare empty list. Frontend: keep a separate error state for fetch failures instead of mapping them to connected:false, and show 'Couldn't load cloud files' with a Retry button. When a provider needs reconnecting, show a role-aware action: admins get the /admin integrations deep link, users get /profile Connected accounts. In MatterDocumentsTab, surface the same error state instead of hiding the section. Add tests for the token-expired path (empty list plus needs_reconnect) and for a fetch error rendering Retry rather than 'not connected'.

title: Calendar move/delete always claims the connected calendar was updated, ignoring the provider result
claim: After updateScheduledEvent the UI always shows 'Moved ... and updated the connected calendar.' (CalendarPage.jsx:684-687), ignoring the sync_status/external_calendar_event_id/calendar_provider the PATCH returns (calendar.py:481-497) and showing it even for local-only events; syncMessageForScheduledEvent (CalendarPage.jsx:294) is not reused. Delete always says 'Event deleted from LawHand and its connected calendar.' (CalendarPage.jsx:819-823) while delete_external_event discards the boolean from ms_delete_event/google_delete_event (scheduled_events.py:125-143; calendar_sync.py:306-320) and the route returns 204 regardless (calendar.py:501-521). Attorneys believe external meetings moved or were cancelled when they were not.

reviews.correction: Accurate, and the backend is somewhat worse than described. ms_delete_event treats HTTP 404 as success, and both move and delete use the acting user's token against /me/events rather than the event creator's. When a colleague moves or deletes someone else's event, the call returns 404 and counts as 'success' while the real event survives. PATCH deletes and then re-creates: if the delete silently fails and the create succeeds, the provider calendar ends up with a duplicate event. The Zoom delete result is also discarded. The frontend test CalendarPage.scheduled-events.test.jsx:65-74 expects an error for a failed external delete, which the backend never returns. syncMessageForScheduledEvent cannot be reused unchanged because its wording is create-specific ('Event created…').
reviews.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarPage.jsx:684-687: after updateScheduledEvent it always shows the 'Moved “…” and updated the connected calendar.' message and ignores the response, even when event.calendar_provider is null. CalendarPage.jsx:292-329 defines syncMessageForScheduledEvent, used only for create at 802. CalendarPage.jsx:814-823: delete always shows 'Event deleted from LawHand and its connected calendar.' backend/app/routers/calendar.py:444-497: PATCH calls delete_external_event (482), then create_external_event, and returns ScheduledEventResponse with sync_status, sync_error, external_calendar_event_id and calendar_provider (backend/app/schemas/calendar.py:146-166). calendar.py:500-521: DELETE ignores the external result, deletes the row and returns 204. backend/app/services/scheduled_events.py:125-142: delete_external_event returns None and discards the booleans from ms_delete_event, google_delete_event and zoom delete_meeting. backend/app/services/calendar_sync.py:299-320: ms_delete_event returns False when there is no event_id or token, and counts 404 as success. calendar_sync.py:500-518 does the same for google_delete_event. backend/app/services/token_vault.py:438-474: get_fresh_user_token returns None rather than raising. frontend/src/pages/CalendarPage.scheduled-events.test.jsx:65-74 tests an error path the backend never produces.
reviews.fix_sketch: Frontend, which can ship alone: build the move message from the PATCH result with a variant of syncMessageForScheduledEvent that takes a verb. It should say 'Moved X.' for local-only events, 'Moved X and updated your Outlook/Google calendar' only when external_calendar_event_id is present and sync_status != 'error', and otherwise 'Moved in LawHand, but the connected calendar could not be updated' with reconnectProvider. For delete, stop claiming external deletion when calendar_provider is null. Backend: make delete_external_event return a result such as {calendar: deleted|not_found|skipped|failed, meeting: …}. Use the token of event.created_by_user_id rather than the acting user's, and stop treating a Graph 404 from a non-owner as success. In PATCH, record a failed old-event delete in sync_error, or skip re-creating so no duplicate is made. For DELETE, either return 200 with {external_deleted} or return 424/409 and keep the row, so the UI can offer Retry or Delete-locally-anyway. Add backend tests for each case: no token, 404, non-creator acting.

title: Consent copy and admin/user/setup docs omit Mail.Send/gmail.send and write-all-files access
claim: Code requests Mail.Send and Files.ReadWrite.All in Microsoft admin and user sets and gmail.send in Google admin/user/solo sets (integrations.py:241-272; connected_mail.py:44-45) and sends via /me/sendMail and messages/send. Yet the onboarding wizard says 'read mail, read files' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:420), the hub card says 'Mail and calendar access for enabled workflows' (IntegrationsHub.jsx:71-75), the admin data-visibility guide omits Mail.Send and says Gmail 'does not authorize sending' (16-integration-data-visibility.md:42, 60-62), docs/integrations-setup.md:42-53 lists no Mail.Send and 'Gmail read', docs/virtual-document-assistant-plan.md:544-545 says read-only, and the user transparency guide omits send (16-integration-transparency.md:39-47, 63-69; it also wrongly says documents are not copied locally at line 119 and links to missing chapters at 125-126). Customer security records and consent disclosures under-report send/write permission.

reviews.evidence: The code requests the send scopes. MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES and MICROSOFT_USER_SCOPES include Mail.Send and Files.ReadWrite.All; the Google admin, user and solo sets include gmail.send (backend/app/routers/integrations.py:242-278; constants at connected_mail.py:44-45). Sends go via /me/sendMail and /users/me/messages/send (connected_mail.py:92, 178). The under-reporting is real in these places: OnboardingWizard.jsx:415 says 'Read all users, read mail, read files (OneDrive + SharePoint), read/write calendars'. Admin guide 16-integration-data-visibility.md:42 lists the MS scopes without Mail.Send; :60 omits gmail.send; :62 says Gmail 'is read-only... the current grant does not authorize sending', which is false. Table rows :30 and :32-33 also say Gmail read-only. docs/integrations-setup.md:46-47 omits Mail.Send and :71-72 says 'Gmail read'. docs/virtual-document-assistant-plan.md says the mail integrations 'use read-only scopes'. User guide 16-integration-transparency.md:39-47 and :63-69 omit send. Its line 119 says documents are 'not copied into a LawHand datastore', which is contradicted by the local-save fallback (MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:446-449) and by the guide's own lines 53 and 75. Links at :125-126 point to /guide/documents-and-cloud-files and /guide/calendar-tasks-and-key-dates, but the actual slugs are matters-and-documents and tasks-calendar-communications. GuideViewer.jsx:94-96 silently redirects an unknown slug to chapter 1. The hub card (IntegrationsHub.jsx:71-75) says only 'Mail and calendar access for enabled workflows'.
reviews.correction: Overstated in two respects. (1) 'Write-all-files' is omitted only in the onboarding wizard copy. The admin guide (:42, :44 calls Files.ReadWrite.All 'broad'), the setup doc (:43, :46-47), and the user guide (:44, :68, :53, :75) all disclose read/write file access. (2) Not every consent disclosure under-reports. The IntegrationsPanel pre-connect card lists each required scope with labels including 'Send email as the connected account' and 'Read and write every file...' (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:24-50, 763-771). The public requirements scope matrix (frontend/src/marketing/integration-scopes.json:10, 22, 42, 48) includes Mail.Send and gmail.send and is tested against the backend constants (backend/tests/test_public_integration_scopes.py). The Microsoft and Google consent screens also list the scopes. The hub-card bullet is vague rather than false. The affirmatively false statements are admin guide line 62, the plan doc's 'read-only' line, and user guide line 119.
reviews.fix_sketch: Correct the copy: OnboardingWizard.jsx:415 should add 'send mail as the connected account' and change 'read files' to 'read and write files'. Better, render it from the same SCOPE_LABELS as IntegrationsPanel. Add a send-mail bullet to the IntegrationsHub cloud card. In the admin guide, add Mail.Send and gmail.send to :42 and :60, rewrite :62, and update table rows :30-33. Update docs/integrations-setup.md:46-47 and :71-72, and the read-only sentence in docs/virtual-document-assistant-plan.md. In the user guide, add send bullets at 39-47 and 63-69, rewrite 119 to cover synced copies and the local-save fallback, and fix links 125-126 to /guide/matters-and-documents and /guide/tasks-calendar-communications. Optionally extend test_public_integration_scopes.py to assert that the platform docs mention every requested scope. No backend code changes; the docs/ markdown files also change. Separately, product may want least-privilege consent (drop Mail.Send unless sending is enabled), but that is not needed to fix the disclosure.

title: Backend container lacks metric-compatible Office fonts for DOCX-to-PDF signing copies
claim: backend/Dockerfile:27-36 installs only fonts-liberation and fonts-nanum; there is no Carlito/Caladea (Calibri/Cambria metrics) or Aptos substitute, and the team's validation does not certify production LibreOffice conversion (docs/template-studio-word-source-review.md:62). Signed PDFs can reflow, moving signature captions across pages.

reviews.evidence: backend/Dockerfile:27-36: the final stage installs only libgl1, libglib2.0-0, fonts-nanum, fonts-liberation and libreoffice-writer. There is no fonts-crosextra-carlito or caladea, no DejaVu, and no fontconfig alias anywhere in the repo: a search for *.conf font files and for calibri/carlito/aptos in backend/app found nothing. backend/app/services/docx_to_pdf.py:85-112 runs soffice headless with a fresh profile and the default system fontconfig. backend/app/config.py:242 sets DOCX_PDF_CONVERSION_ENABLED=True by default. backend/app/routers/document_templates.py:4708-4719 converts the filled DOCX and reports 'PDF ready for signature', so this LibreOffice output is the signing copy. docs/template-studio-word-source-review.md:62 says the validation used desktop Word and does 'not certify production LibreOffice conversion'. Without Carlito, Calibri falls back to a font with different metrics, so line and page breaks differ from Word.
reviews.correction: The divergence is from the Word original, not something that appears silently after review. Saving a PDF requires a fresh previewId (usePrepareFill.js:443-446), and the preview evidence stores output_sha256 (document_templates.py:3531-3547). The attorney therefore previews the same reflowed PDF that is saved and signed. There is also no free metric-compatible substitute for Aptos, so adding Carlito/Caladea fixes Calibri/Cambria documents but not Aptos ones.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add fonts-crosextra-carlito, fonts-crosextra-caladea and fonts-dejavu-core to the final-stage apt install in backend/Dockerfile. Optionally add a /etc/fonts/conf.d alias mapping Calibri to Carlito and Cambria to Caladea. For Aptos, document the limitation or add a warning at template intake when the DOCX declares fonts not installed in the container (read word/fontTable.xml). Bump _DOCX_PDF_RENDERER_VERSION so old preview evidence is invalidated. Add a container-level CI smoke test that converts a Calibri/Cambria fixture and asserts page count and that the signature block stays on the expected page.

title: Live DOCX-to-PDF preview spawns unbounded LibreOffice processes in the API worker
claim: The render-file preview calls docx_to_pdf_bytes per request with no semaphore or queue (document_templates.py:3510-3523); only the source-preview cache is single-flight (template_source_preview.py:35-37). Auto-preview re-fires 650 ms after typing (usePrepareFill.js:13, 79, 425-428), and each conversion starts soffice with up to 60 s timeout (docx_to_pdf.py:92-116), so concurrent users can exhaust API CPU/memory.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/document_templates.py:3510-3523 calls docx_to_pdf_bytes directly with no semaphore or queue. The save path at 4708-4715 does the same. backend/app/services/template_source_preview.py:35-38 is the only single-flight guard, and it covers only source previews. backend/app/services/docx_to_pdf.py:92-116 starts a new soffice process per call with wait_for(timeout=60s) by default (config.py:244). Prod runs 4 uvicorn workers (docker-compose.prod.yml:110). The only other bound is the general per-user limit of 600 requests per hour (middleware/rate_limit.py). frontend/src/components/prepare/usePrepareFill.js:13 sets AUTO_PREVIEW_DELAY_MS=650 and :424-429 schedules the auto-preview.
reviews.correction: Auto-preview does not fire on every keystroke. handleRender returns early while a render is in flight (usePrepareFill.js:350-353, 'Serialize expensive renders'). The auto effect is also suppressed while rendering, after a previewId exists, or when the same input key was already tried (424-428). Each browser session therefore has at most one conversion in flight. On the server, the route SELECTs the template row WITH FOR UPDATE (document_templates.py:3452-3459) and keeps that lock until the commit after conversion (3576). This serializes concurrent conversions of the same template. It also pins a DB connection and row lock for up to 60 s per request, so DB pool and lock contention is as likely a failure mode as CPU. Conversions across different templates and tenants remain uncapped per worker, so the core claim of no global bound holds.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add a process-wide asyncio.Semaphore in docx_to_pdf.py, sized from a new setting such as DOCX_PDF_MAX_CONCURRENT=2 per worker, with a short bounded acquire wait. When it times out, raise a DocxToPdfError('busy') that the routes map to 503 with Retry-After. Do not hold the FOR UPDATE lock or DB transaction during conversion: load and verify the template, convert, then re-lock and check that the version is unchanged before writing preview evidence. Longer term, move conversion to a dedicated converter sidecar or queue (for example unoserver or Gotenberg) with a warm LibreOffice instance.

title: Most Graph/Google call sites have no 429/Retry-After handling; syncs truncate silently and calendar pushes are lost
claim: Only provider_http.graph_request retries. Calendar (calendar_sync.py:124-141, google_calendar.py:100-166, microsoft_calendar.py:165-198), cloud sync (cloud_sync.py:343-372, 1058-1064), cloud_search, cloud_init, document_sync, directory (user_sync.py:130-145) and discovery (storage_discovery.py:214-250) use raw httpx and break or return empty on any non-200; task pushes are fire-and-forget with no durable retry. Throttled large firms get partial indexes and permanently stale calendar copies with no alert.

reviews.evidence: provider_http.py:104-140: provider_request retries 429 and 5xx with Retry-After backoff. It is reached through graph_client.graph_request (graph_client.py:20-37) and also through google_client.google_request/gmail_request (google_client.py:20-58). Raw httpx with no retry: microsoft_calendar.py:165-198 (logs a warning and returns None), google_calendar.py:100-166 (same), calendar_sync.py:124-141 (one $expand fallback, then raises ValueError telling the user to 'Connect Calendar'), cloud_sync.py:369-382 and 1058-1070 (logs, then break; the partial count is returned as success, so _run_provider_sync at 270-300 records no failure), user_sync.py:130-145 (raises RuntimeError), storage_discovery.py:214-250 (raises ValueError). Task calendar pushes go through _fire_and_log (task_notifications.py:36-50) called from push_task_to_calendars (270-316), which is a bare asyncio.create_task with no outbox or durable retry. No calendar reconciliation job exists (grep found none).
reviews.correction: 'Only graph_request retries' is wrong: google_request and gmail_request retry through the same provider_request, covering Gmail and matter_documents Google calls. Not every site fails silently. user_sync, storage_discovery and calendar reads raise visible errors; they just are not retried, and calendar reads wrongly tell the user to reconnect. The silent truncation is real in cloud_sync (Drive and Graph listings break, and the partial count reads as success). But the scheduler re-runs it every CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN=15 (config.py:583) with no pruning, so partial indexes are transient, not permanent. 'Permanently stale' is accurate only for fire-and-forget task calendar pushes, which stay stale until the task is next edited.
reviews.fix_sketch: Move the calendar, cloud_sync, cloud_search, cloud_init, document_sync, user_sync and storage_discovery raw httpx calls onto graph_request/google_request, or a shared provider_request with an injected client, so 429 and 5xx get bounded Retry-After backoff. After retries run out in _sync_graph_files and the Drive listing, raise ProviderThrottled or ProviderError instead of break, so _run_provider_sync records a failure and the admin sync status shows it. Replace _fire_and_log calendar pushes with a durable job (the existing durable-job infrastructure) keyed by task_id, with retry/backoff and a last-error field shown on the task. On 429 in calendar reads, show a 'provider busy, try again' message instead of 'Connect Calendar'.

title: Google 403 rate-limit responses are treated as auth failures (no backoff, 'Reconnect' shown)
claim: provider_http.py:95-100 turns every 401/403 into ProviderAuthError without checking the reason, but Google returns 403 rateLimitExceeded/userRateLimitExceeded; connected_mail maps this to REAUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED (connected_mail.py:267-280). Throttled users are told to reconnect and nothing is retried.

reviews.evidence: provider_http.py:95-96 raises ProviderAuthError for any 401/403 without reading the body's error reason. provider_request (133-137) retries only 429 and 5xx, so a 403 rate limit is never retried. gmail_request (google_client.py:42-58) goes through this path. connected_mail._attempt_provider (connected_mail.py:267-280) maps ProviderAuthError to EmailDeliveryResult.REAUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED with _reconnect_detail ('Reconnect Google in Integrations to grant permission...', 233-238). email.py:90-95 turns that into a 503 'needs to be reauthorized', and matters.py:2853-2860 shows that detail. Nothing in backend/app matches 'rateLimitExceeded' or 'userRateLimitExceeded'. The same 403-to-auth mapping is in matter_file_store._raise_for_download_response (matter_file_store.py:1566-1578), and esignature.py:463-467 surfaces it as 'The document storage connection needs to be reconnected'.
reviews.correction: The core claim holds, and the scope is broader: Drive document downloads (matter_file_store, used by e-sign and others) also misreport throttling as reconnect. 'Nothing is retried' is by design for sends: max_retries=0 at connected_mail.py:97 and :181 avoids duplicate delivery. The defect on sends is the misleading classification and message, not the missing retry. Read paths (gmail_read_mail) do fail to retry a 403 rate limit.
reviews.fix_sketch: In _raise_for_provider_response, and the matching matter_file_store._raise_for_download_response, parse the JSON error body on 403.
