If error.errors[].reason is in {rateLimitExceeded, userRateLimitExceeded, dailyLimitExceeded, quotaExceeded} or error.status == 'RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED', raise ProviderThrottled (with retry_after) instead of ProviderAuthError. In provider_request, treat that case as retryable, like 429, for requests where max_retries > 0. Add a ProviderThrottled branch in connected_mail._attempt_provider that returns FAILED with 'Google is rate-limiting this mailbox; try again shortly' and DELIVERY_NOT_ATTEMPTED. Add unit tests in test_provider_http.py and test_connected_mail.py.

title: BK28/ECO ledger in TASKS.md is stale: shipped items unchecked and plan current-state gaps outdated
claim: TASKS.md:395-518 heads the epic '(PLANNED)' with every ECO item unchecked, although ECO-17 (Personal Google mode, integrations.py:266-286; CHANGELOG.md:279-289), ECO-24..28 (docs/sms-provider-operations.md:11-40; propose_client_sms) and parts of ECO-01/04 shipped. The plan still says 'personal Gmail directory sync fails' (plan:64) and that trial_ends_at is unread (plan:66, 262-265), fixed in 2026.09.11.8. Planning against it duplicates shipped work.

reviews.evidence: TASKS.md:395 heads the epic 'BK28 ... 2026-08-27 (PLANNED)', and every ECO-01..ECO-29 item on lines 411-517 is '- [ ]'. Personal Google mode has shipped: integrations.py:272-289 (GOOGLE_SOLO_SCOPES, _google_scopes_for_mode, _google_account_mode_matches) and CHANGELOG.md:4, 292 and 298 ('present Personal Google setup without a false Workspace-directory sync'). SMS consent provenance, STOP/START, signed callbacks and the inbound review queue are documented in docs/sms-provider-operations.md:1-40. propose_client_sms exists in automation_capabilities.py:533-540 and chat_tools/handlers.py:157. Trial operator controls are at CHANGELOG.md:326, and the 2026.09.11.8 trial fix is at CHANGELOG.md:762-767 ('Signup previously wrote a 14-day trial_ends_at that nothing read'). The plan doc still says 'personal Gmail directory sync fails' (workspace-ecosystem-trials-onboarding-plan-2026-08-27.md:64) and that the trials gate ignores trial_ends_at (line 66 and 262-265). Its SMS row (line 69) still lists no consent provenance, callbacks, STOP/HELP or agent proposal.
reviews.correction: The staleness is real, but this is an internal planning ledger with no runtime or customer impact, so medium severity is overstated; low fits. The CHANGELOG line references in the original finding (279-289, 312-318, 752-758) have moved; the current evidence is at CHANGELOG.md:4, 292, 298, 326 and 762-767. Whether ECO-24..28 are fully done, rather than 'largely' done, needs acceptance-gate review (for example, ECO-26 alert categories and ECO-29 gates).
reviews.fix_sketch: Update TASKS.md BK28: change the header status to IN PROGRESS. Tick ECO-17 and the shipped parts of ECO-24/25/27/28, and ECO-01/04 where done, with a short evidence note (CHANGELOG version and file). Split any remaining acceptance-gate work into explicit sub-items. In the plan doc's leverage table (lines 60-70) and section 3 (262-265), replace the outdated gaps with the current state and cite 2026.09.11.8 and the Personal Google release. Docs only.

title: /api/integrations/status reports Personal Google tenants as missing the directory scope
claim: google_required is always GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES (integrations.py:1856) with no effective_required_scopes for the personal tier, so missing_scopes includes admin.directory and reconnect_required is true (1904-1921); /admin/permissions handles this correctly (admin.py:1702). Teams pages and future status consumers misreport healthy personal tenants.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/integrations.py:1896-1897 (HEAD; the cited 1856 is now the function signature): ms_required = MICROSOFT_ADMIN_SCOPES and google_required = GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES, both unconditional. google_missing (1946-1951) is computed against GOOGLE_ADMIN_SCOPES, which includes admin.directory.user.readonly (integrations.py:245-252). A personal tenant connects with GOOGLE_SOLO_SCOPES (266-271, selected by _google_scopes_for_mode, 274-279), which omits that scope, so missing_scopes includes it and reconnect_required (1959-1961) is true. The same file's callback audits the row against the solo scopes, so the stored health stays 'healthy', which makes the status payload internally inconsistent. admin.py:1702-1704 calls provider_capabilities.effective_required_scopes (capabilities.py:79-88) and handles this correctly. The same bug affects Microsoft consumer accounts (ms_required includes User.Read.All; effective_required_scopes strips it for CONSUMER). The only consumers of /integrations/status are frontend/src/api.js:861-862, TeamsPanel.jsx (107-111, 126-175) and TeamsTabConfigPage.jsx:28. Both read only status.microsoft fields (connected, teams_connected, teams_missing_scopes, capabilities.teams, account_type), not google or reconnect_required/missing_scopes.
reviews.correction: The backend inconsistency is real and also affects personal Microsoft accounts via User.Read.All. But no current UI reads google.missing_scopes or reconnect_required from this endpoint, and the Teams pages only read Microsoft Teams fields. So 'Teams pages misreport healthy personal tenants' is refuted: the endpoint's response is wrong, but no current screen shows it.
reviews.fix_sketch: In integration_status, compute ms_required and google_required via cap.effective_required_scopes(provider, <admin scope list>, row.account_type), or pick GOOGLE_SOLO_SCOPES when google_row.account_type == 'personal'. Use the result for both missing_scopes and required_scopes. Better, share one helper with admin.get_permissions_audit so the two endpoints cannot diverge. Add tests for a personal Google and a consumer Microsoft row expecting reconnect_required=False.

title: Google domain-wide delegation is configuration-only and scope comments are misleading
claim: google_service_account.py:1-41 says DWD is used for directory and mail, but no caller passes subject and GOOGLE_IMPERSONATE_SUBJECT (config.py:175-178) is never read; DRIVE_SCOPES is described as 'least privilege' but is the full drive scope. Operators may configure DWD expecting it to work and reviewers may think scopes were minimized.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/google_service_account.py:8-13: the docstring says domain-wide delegation via subject is 'Used for directory and mail operations'. get_access_token (108-112) accepts subject=, but the only callers pass scopes alone: google_service_account.py:241 (get_access_token(DRIVE_SCOPES) inside prefer_service_account) and cloud_init.py:1069-1070. A grep for GOOGLE_IMPERSONATE_SUBJECT finds only config.py:175-178 (the declaration) and docs/storage-root-ownership-and-handoff.md:49 and 81, which advertise it to operators. No code reads it. google_service_account.py:38-41 says 'Least privilege for the document root' but DRIVE_SCOPES = ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive'], the full Drive scope.
reviews.correction: Accurate. One nuance: the full drive scope is probably needed, because the service account must reach the admin-created lawhand-records root and all files in the Shared Drive, which drive.file would not allow. The defect is the misleading comment, not necessarily the scope choice. Also, a single deployment-global GOOGLE_IMPERSONATE_SUBJECT could never work across tenants, so wiring it up as-is would be wrong.
reviews.fix_sketch: Remove GOOGLE_IMPERSONATE_SUBJECT from config.py and the ops doc, or mark it 'reserved / not implemented'. Rewrite the module docstring to say delegation is not used. Reword the DRIVE_SCOPES comment to explain why the full drive scope is required (Shared Drive content-manager access to admin-created roots). If DWD is ever wanted for directory or mail, design it per tenant (a subject stored on TenantCredential plus a customer Admin-console grant), not as a global setting.

title: Revoked user tokens stay in the capture roster and are refreshed on every use
claim: _locked_user_token does not filter health='revoked' (token_vault.py:213-231), so each correspondence cycle, search and push retries refresh and logs a failure (scheduler.py:1896-1952), producing repeated failures rather than a single 'user must reconnect' state.

reviews.correction: Revoked tokens are re-refreshed on every use and each correspondence cycle records a failure. That part is real. 'Rather than a single user-must-reconnect state' is overstated: health stays 'revoked' (token_vault.py:88 guard), and summarize_user_tokens counts revoked as needs_reauth (integration_observability.py:81-102), so a reconnect state already exists. The problem is extra noise and wasted refresh calls on top of it. The scheduled noise also only occurs when CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_ENABLED=True, which defaults to False (config.py:586). I did not individually verify the 'search and push' paths. They share get_fresh_user_token, so they behave the same way.
reviews.evidence: token_vault.py:213-231: _locked_user_token selects on user/tenant/provider only, with no health filter. token_vault.py:437-472: get_fresh_user_token refreshes whenever the access token has expired and a refresh token exists, with no health check. token_vault.py:77-89: invalid_grant sets health='revoked' but keeps encrypted_refresh_token, so the next call POSTs to the token endpoint again (_refresh_locked_row 281-300) and logs a warning. scheduler.py:1896-1952: the roster query has no health filter. Each failure logs a warning, writes capture_integration_error (an error_logs row, with no dedupe in error_tracker.capture_error) and a failed IntegrationSyncRun, every CORRESPONDENCE_CAPTURE_INTERVAL_MIN (30) minutes.
reviews.fix_sketch: In get_fresh_user_token, return None without calling the provider when token_row.health == 'revoked'. clear_refresh_failure already resets health on re-consent, so that is safe. Filter the correspondence roster (scheduler.py:1896-1901) with UserOAuthToken.health != 'revoked'. Optionally, record one integration error when health first turns revoked instead of one per cycle. Add unit tests for the short-circuit and the roster filter.

title: ms_read_mail_tenant is dead and broken
claim: microsoft_mail.py:101-134 passes the Graph user id as the LawHand user_id to get_fresh_user_token, so every user is skipped; there are no callers. A trap for anyone building tenant-wide capture on it.

reviews.correction: Accurate. Even if the ids lined up, the delegated token reads /me, so the function could never read other users' mailboxes. It is fundamentally unusable, not just mis-keyed.
reviews.evidence: microsoft_mail.py:101-134: iterates Graph /users and passes uid=user['id'] (an Entra object id) to ms_read_mail_user, which calls get_fresh_user_token (microsoft_mail.py:19-22). That filters UserOAuthToken.user_id == uid (token_vault.py:219-227), and that column is a LawHand user UUID, so no row is found. It returns None, RuntimeError is raised, and the user is silently skipped (130-132). ms_read_mail_user also reads /me/messages (microsoft_mail.py:50) with the per-user delegated token. grep: the only reference outside the definition is backend/tests/test_mail_provider_clients.py:147-166, which mocks ms_read_mail_user.
reviews.fix_sketch: Delete ms_read_mail_tenant and its test (test_mail_provider_clients.py:146-166). If tenant-wide capture is wanted later, build it on an app-only token and /users/{id}/messages with a proper Entra-id to LawHand-user mapping.

title: Background calendar pull hides provider token failures
claim: The 5-minute pullProviderChanges catches every error and does nothing (CalendarPage.jsx:610-624) and keeps no last-synced time, so stale Outlook/Google events remain with no warning after a token expires.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarPage.jsx:610-624: pullProviderChanges calls syncCalendarDeadlines(provider,false), and the catch block is empty (comment: 'Connection health messaging is handled by explicit sync and provider status'). On failure providerEvents is left as it was, so the old events stay merged into the view by fetchEvents (588-604). Provider status (getCalendarProviders, around line 525) runs only in a mount-time effect, so a token that fails mid-session is never shown. The backend turns token and read failures into HTTP 424 (routers/calendar.py:72-82; calendar_sync.py:329-338 and 357-361), and the axios response interceptor handles only 401 (api.js:257-264), so the 424 reaches this empty catch. No lastSynced or last_synced state exists in CalendarPage.jsx.
reviews.correction: Accurate. In practice this happens when the refresh token is revoked or refresh fails, not on ordinary access-token expiry, because get_fresh_user_token refreshes those.
reviews.fix_sketch: In the catch, store providerPullError (status plus detail) and show a non-blocking banner, e.g. 'Couldn't refresh Outlook events. Reconnect' with the existing reconnect action. Keep lastProviderPullAt in state and show 'Outlook events as of HH:MM' next to the Sync button. Optionally dim provider events when the last pull failed. Clear the error on the next successful pull. Add a vitest case for a rejected poll.

title: Google Drive firm-knowledge import query ANDs MIME and extension, skips Shared Drives and does not page
claim: document_sync.py:281-305 joins the mime and extension clauses with ' and ' (cloud_sync.py:339 uses OR), has no supportsAllDrives/includeItemsFromAllDrives, and uses pageSize=min(max_files,100) with no nextPageToken. .odt/.wpd files, extensionless files and Shared Drive files are never imported and counts cap at 100.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/document_sync.py:281-292 builds query_parts=[mime OR-clause, ext OR-clause] and joins them with ' and ' (line 291). cloud_sync.py:346 unions them with 'or'. document_sync.py:296-304: params contain only q, pageSize=min(max_files,100), fields (with no nextPageToken) and orderBy. There is no supportsAllDrives, includeItemsFromAllDrives or corpora, and there is no paging loop. :435-462 get_sync_stats asks for max_files=500 but gets at most 100. .odt/.wpd/.docm MIME types are not in LEGAL_MIME_TYPES (:22-28), so the AND excludes them. Callers: routers/document_sync.py:75-80 and durable_job_worker.py:202-207. There is no frontend caller (grep of frontend/src for sync/documents finds nothing), so this is an API-only admin path.
reviews.correction: Accurate. Additional context: the endpoints (/api/sync/documents/*) are not wired into the SPA, which limits user impact. The same no-paging, 100-item cap also affects document_sync.sync_onedrive and sync_sharepoint (:154-158, :231-237). The alt=media download at :370 also lacks supportsAllDrives=true, so Shared Drive items would fail to download even if they were listed.
reviews.fix_sketch: Change ' and '.join to ' or ' (or reuse cloud_sync's clause builder). Add supportsAllDrives=True, includeItemsFromAllDrives=True and corpora='allDrives'. Loop on nextPageToken until len(results)>=max_files. Add supportsAllDrives=true to the alt=media download URL. Apply @odata.nextLink paging to the OneDrive and SharePoint listings. Add unit tests for the query string and paging.

title: SharePoint index sync ignores the bound site and indexes /sites/root
claim: sync_all calls sync_sharepoint(db, tenant_id) without the sharepoint_binding site_id (cloud_sync.py:145-152, 622-700), so the admin-bound matter library is not indexed and intranet root-site files appear in firm search instead.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_sync.py:145-152: sync_all calls self.sync_sharepoint(db, tenant_id) with no site_id. cloud_sync.py:622-700: with no site_id it resolves /sites/root, enumerates its drives and lists only /drives/{id}/root/children (non-recursive) through _sync_graph_files (:1034-1135). The binding is stored at TenantSettings.custom_config['sharepoint_binding'] (cloud_admin.py:382-405; cloud_init.py:815-825) and is never read by cloud_sync. Scheduled every 15 min when CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED (scheduler.py:804-815; config.py:583). Per-matter sync_matter_folders does index bound-library matter folders through sharepoint_refs (cloud_sync.py:250-264).
reviews.correction: The core defect is real: the scheduled sync ignores the bound site and indexes top-level files of /sites/root libraries. The impact is overstated in two ways. First, even with site_id passed, sync_sharepoint lists only root/children of each library, so matter subfolders would still not be indexed. Second, bound-library matter folders are indexed by the per-matter 'Sync folder' path. Root-site files would already show up in firm search through live Graph search, so the index adds only a few top-level items. 'Instead' is not accurate.
reviews.fix_sketch: In sync_all, load cloud_init._get_sharepoint_binding. If a binding exists, sync its drive_id from the tenant's LawHand root folder (cloud_root_folder['sharepoint'].id) recursively, or through the drive delta API, capped at MAX_FILES. Skip the /sites/root fallback when a binding exists. Add a test that asserts the bound site/drive is requested.

title: Per-matter 'Sync folder' reports 'synced' when providers failed
claim: sync_matter_folders only logs provider exceptions (cloud_sync.py:222-266) and the router returns status 'synced' with counts (matters.py:3407-3425), so users think the matter's cloud files are current when listing failed.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/cloud_sync.py:219-264: each provider call in sync_matter_folders is wrapped in try/except, which only runs logger.warning, and there is no failures list. By contrast, sync_all uses _run_provider_sync (:268-297), which records failures. Non-200 folder listings also just break without raising (:977-983). routers/matters.py:3406-3425 returns status 'synced' unconditionally along with sync_counts. matters.py:236-258: the files list comes from live cloud_search, which also swallows errors and returns []. frontend/src/components/MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:127-141 always shows a success toast, 'Synced N cloud files', on any 2xx response.
reviews.correction: Accurate. Beyond the claim, provider HTTP errors (non-200) are also silent, not only exceptions. The files shown come from live search rather than the sync, so a failed sync plus an empty or partial live search still reports success.
reviews.fix_sketch: Have sync_matter_folders collect {provider, error_type} failures, as sync_all does, and treat a non-200 listing as a failure (raise or record). In the router, return status 'partial' or 'failed' plus a failures list when any provider failed. In MatterDocumentsTab.handleSync, show a warning toast naming the failed provider(s) when failures are present. Add backend and frontend tests.

title: Manual directory sync result and failures are invisible to the admin
claim: The durable user_sync job raises without record_sync_failure and skips Google if Microsoft raises (durable_job_worker.py:405-434). The 'Sync now' UI uses a fixed 4 s timer and one shared syncing flag for both provider cards (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:114-126, 271-282), then silently reloads with no success/failure/count; errors go to a banner that never clears. The card keeps showing the last 'ok' sync after a failed run.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/durable_job_worker.py:405-434: _run_user_sync calls sync_microsoft_users and sync_google_users directly, with no try/except, no record_sync_failure and no record_integration_sync_run. Compare sync_all (user_sync.py:376-395), which records failures, and the scheduler path (scheduler.py:2029-2063). Providers are iterated as sorted(set(providers)), and 'google' sorts before 'microsoft', so a Google exception skips Microsoft. The trigger (routers/scheduler.py:143-170) returns a job_id that the UI ignores. frontend/src/components/IntegrationsPanel.jsx:196-208: handleSyncNow uses one shared syncing flag, waits a fixed 4000 ms, re-reads getAdminPermissions, and shows no result. Both cards get syncing={syncing} (401, 415), and the button reads 'Syncing…' (985-992). The error is set to 'Failed to trigger sync.' and not cleared at the start of the next sync. The card status line comes from TenantCredential.last_user_sync_status and last_user_sync_at (admin.py:1720-1725; IntegrationsPanel.jsx:965-968). A failed manual run leaves these at the previous 'ok', so the card shows 'last run <old time>'.
reviews.correction: The provider order is reversed: Google runs first (alphabetical sort), so Microsoft is skipped when Google raises. The cited frontend line ranges are stale; the code is now at IntegrationsPanel.jsx:196-208, 390-416 and 965-992. The error banner does clear: setError(null) runs in the disconnect and other handlers (e.g. 279) and on reload, but not on a successful retry of Sync now. The old timestamp is still shown, so a careful admin could tell the run did not update. Only the failure itself is invisible.
reviews.fix_sketch: Backend: in _run_user_sync, wrap each provider in try/except. On error call user_sync.record_sync_failure and record_integration_sync_run(status='failed'), then continue with the next provider. Raise or return an aggregated error at the end so the durable job still reads failed, or simply delegate to user_sync.sync_all. Record completed runs too. Frontend: clear the error at the start of handleSyncNow. Keep syncing per provider, or relabel the button as a tenant-wide sync. Poll a job-status endpoint using the returned job_id (or poll getAdminPermissions until last_sync_at changes, with a timeout), then show 'Synced N users (X new)' or the failure text.

title: Teams notification cards are posted as the consenting admin, not a bot
claim: teams_notify.py:150-171 posts cards with delegated ChannelMessage.Send (teams.py:401-406) using the consenting user's or tenant credential's token; there is no bot identity, so deadline alerts appear 'from' a partner.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/teams_notify.py:150-171 resolves one token through teams_service.resolve_token(tenant_id, user_id) and posts through send_channel_message. Both production callers (scheduler.py:1280 deadline_approaching, durable_job_worker.py:652 voice_call_captured) pass no user_id, so services/teams.py:64-142 always falls back to the TenantCredential. services/teams.py:40-46 lists only delegated scopes (ChannelMessage.Send and others), and 364-406 POSTs /teams/{id}/channels/{id}/messages with that bearer token. The TenantCredential is the delegated authorization-code token of the admin who ran admin connect (routers/integrations.py:563-605 stores access/refresh token plus granted_by_user_id). Graph posts delegated channel messages as that user. teams-app/manifest.json has no `bots` entry and config.py defines no bot credentials.
reviews.correction: Minor precision: in practice the cards are always posted as the admin who consented through the tenant credential, never as 'the consenting user' of an individual token, because no caller passes user_id.
reviews.fix_sketch: Register an Azure Bot / Bot Framework app. Add a `bots` entry to the Teams manifest and store conversation references when the app is installed in a team or channel. Send deadline and voice cards as proactive bot messages with the bot's app credentials, not the delegated Graph token. Graph application permissions cannot post normal channel messages (only migration), so a bot is required. A cheaper interim option is per-channel Workflows/incoming webhooks, which post as the 'Workflows' app, or at least labelling each card 'Automated LawHand alert'.

title: Word stale-check fingerprints only the selected text
claim: wordAdapter.ts:30-54 hashes the selected text (sha256) with no position or paragraph identity, so re-selecting identical boilerplate elsewhere applies the plan there without a stale warning.

reviews.evidence: office-addin/src/hosts/wordAdapter.ts:32-41 fingerprints only `{ text: selection.text }` (via office-addin/src/contracts/fingerprint.ts:17-21) and uses that one hash as both documentFingerprint and selectionHash (:46, :52). execute() (:83-93) re-captures the current selection and compares only these hashes (validatePlan in office-addin/src/contracts/validation.ts:140-143 and :158-160, plus the anchor check at wordAdapter.ts:92). If the user selects identical text anywhere else, even in a different document, it passes and is replaced. By contrast, excelAdapter.ts:42-49 includes range.address in its fingerprint. The window is limited by the plan TTL (OFFICE_PLAN_TTL_SECONDS=300, backend/app/config.py:119; expiry check at validation.ts:144-148).
reviews.correction: Accurate. Beyond the claim, the check does not bind to the document either, so a plan can be applied to matching text in a different open document within the 5-minute TTL.
reviews.fix_sketch: Bind the plan to a location. At capture time, keep a tracked Word.Range (context.trackedObjects.add, or a saved range reused through Word.run(savedRange, ...)). At apply time, check that it still equals the current selection with range.compareLocationWith (WordApi 1.3), or insert a hidden bookmark or content control at capture and resolve it at apply. As a cheaper step, add Office.context.document.url, the paragraph index and the neighbouring paragraph text to the fingerprint payload.

title: Add-in limits are hard-coded; /api/office/policy and OFFICE_MAX_WORD_CHARACTERS are ignored
claim: Word/Excel limits are constants (wordAdapter.ts:13, excelAdapter.ts:13); /api/office/policy (routers/office_assistant.py:47-63) is never called, and the schema caps Word text at 50,000 regardless of OFFICE_MAX_WORD_CHARACTERS (schemas/office_assistant.py:46). Changed limits yield unexplained 422s or silently no effect.

reviews.evidence: office-addin/src/hosts/wordAdapter.ts:13 DEFAULT_MAX_CHARACTERS=50_000, used at :31 only when request.maxCharacters is absent; office-addin/src/main.ts:108 calls adapter.captureContext() with no args, so the constant always applies. excelAdapter.ts:13 DEFAULT_MAX_CELLS=2_500 (:34), and outlookAdapter.ts:13 works the same way. office-addin/src/api/officeApi.ts:33-47 calls only /office/plans and /office/plans/{id}/result. Nothing in office-addin/src calls /office/policy; only backend/tests/test_office_assistant.py hits the route. The GET /policy route is at backend/app/routers/office_assistant.py:47-63 and returns settings.OFFICE_MAX_*. backend/app/schemas/office_assistant.py:46-47 hard-caps text max_length=50_000 and char_count le=50_000. :52-56 caps Excel rows, columns and matrix rows at 2_500 each, not total cells. backend/app/services/office_action_policy.py:84,92,115 enforce the configurable settings (defaults at config.py:120-122). The whole surface is off by default: config.py:112 OFFICE_ASSISTANT_ENABLED=False, plus the pilot allowlist.
reviews.correction: The 'silently no effect' part is accurate. Raising OFFICE_MAX_WORD_CHARACTERS/OFFICE_MAX_EXCEL_CELLS above the defaults changes nothing, because the client blocks at capture with its hard-coded 50,000 / 2,500 and the Word schema also caps at 50,000. The 'unexplained 422s' part is overstated. Lowering a limit makes office_action_policy raise context_too_large, which the router maps to 422 {code, message:'Word selection is too large'}. officeApi.ts:21-28 extracts detail.message and main.ts:170 shows it in the status line. So the user gets a readable message, but only after writing an instruction and without the numeric limit. A truly unexplained 422 (a pydantic list-shaped detail, which falls through to 'Office assistant request failed (422)') only happens if the client-side cap is raised above the schema cap. Impact is limited to pilot tenants because the feature is off by default.
reviews.fix_sketch: 1) In main.ts, after session.ensure(), call a new OfficeApi.getPolicy() (GET /office/policy). Store maxWordCharacters, maxExcelCells and maxOutlookCharacters, and pass them into adapter.captureContext({maxCharacters, maxCells}), including the internal re-captures in the adapters (e.g. have the adapter hold the policy). 2) In schemas/office_assistant.py, replace the literal 50_000 cap with a high absolute ceiling (e.g. 1_000_000) or validate against get_settings(), so office_action_policy is the single configurable gate. 3) In OfficeApi.request, render list-shaped pydantic detail arrays into a readable message.

title: Office exchange denies demo tenants that the plan endpoints allow
claim: The exchange calls require_office_pilot_tenant directly (auth.py:1777), while plans use require_office_for_user, which exempts billing_tier=='demo' (office_access.py:42-48). Sales demos cannot sign in unless also allowlisted.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/routers/auth.py:1796 (not :1777) calls require_office_pilot_tenant(user.tenant_id) in the /auth/office/exchange handler. backend/app/services/office_access.py:42-48 require_office_for_user exempts tenant.billing_tier=='demo' and is used by backend/app/routers/office_assistant.py:54,74,107. The divergence is real. However, the exchange first resolves the user at auth.py:~1768-1790 by (entra_tenant_id, entra_object_id) or by oauth_provider=='microsoft' plus a matching subject, and returns 403 unless exactly one user matches. Synthetic sales-demo workspaces are created in backend/app/routers/demo.py:241-263 with billing_tier='demo' and a user with oauth_provider='demo', oauth_subject=session_id and no Entra ids. Those users fail the identity lookup before the pilot check is reached. The only other demo-tier source is the operator-only 'demo' plan (backend/app/services/plans.py:64-69, public_signup=False). The add-in's cookie fallback (office-addin/src/auth/officeSession.ts:67-83) does not help cross-site.
reviews.correction: The gate inconsistency is real, but 'sales demos cannot sign in unless allowlisted' misattributes the cause. Self-serve/synthetic demo users have no Microsoft identity, so the exchange rejects them with 403 'Office identity is not linked to exactly one LawHand user' whatever the allowlist says. Aligning the gate alone would not let those demos sign in. Only an operator-provisioned demo-tier tenant whose user signed in with Microsoft hits the allowlist difference. The line reference is also stale (1796, not 1777).
reviews.fix_sketch: Decide the policy first. If demo tenants should reach Office, replace require_office_pilot_tenant(user.tenant_id) at auth.py:1796 with require_office_for_user(user) (user.tenant is already selectinload'ed). Then add a demo sign-in path for the add-in, because demo users lack Microsoft identities. That could be a Microsoft-linked demo seat, or accepting an existing LawHand session. If demo tenants should not reach Office, drop the demo exemption from require_office_for_user so both paths fail closed identically. Either way, add a test asserting the exchange and the plan endpoints agree.

title: Missing OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE produces a bogus '/office.access' scope and bypasses the not-configured guard
claim: docker-compose.hypervisor.yml:411 builds VITE_OFFICE_API_SCOPE as ${OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE:-}/office.access, never empty, bypassing the 'Office SSO is not configured' guard (officeSession.ts:40-42) and surfacing an opaque MSAL error.

reviews.correction: The compose line always yields a non-empty scope, but the guard is only bypassed when OFFICE_ENTRA_CLIENT_ID is set and OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE is empty. In the default case (both empty, .env.hypervisor:95-96), !clientId still trips 'Office SSO is not configured'. That exact misconfiguration is rejected by scripts/prod_env_preflight.sh:443-455, which deploy_prod.sh:126 and deploy_skynet_runner.sh:54-56 run before deploying. Only deploy_dev1.sh (no preflight) or manual compose builds are exposed.
reviews.evidence: docker-compose.hypervisor.yml:411: VITE_OFFICE_API_SCOPE: ${OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE:-}/office.access (never empty). office-addin/src/main.ts:16-20 passes it straight into OfficeSession. office-addin/src/auth/officeSession.ts:40-42 checks only for truthiness of clientId and apiScope, so '/office.access' passes and MSAL is asked for an invalid scope (55-64). scripts/prod_env_preflight.sh:447-453 errors unless the audience equals api://<client-id> whenever the client id is set. scripts/deploy_dev1.sh has no preflight call.
reviews.fix_sketch: Either use conditional interpolation in compose, VITE_OFFICE_API_SCOPE: ${OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE:+${OFFICE_ENTRA_API_AUDIENCE}/office.access} (Compose v2 supports :+), or harden the add-in guard to reject scopes that do not match /^api:\/\/[^/]+\/.+/, or both. Optionally have deploy_dev1.sh run the Office section of the preflight.

title: Workflow-run MCP tool schemas use nested $defs/$ref that Copilot Studio drops
claim: WorkflowRunInput nests RunStepInput and SourceBinding lists (workflow_run_contract.py:85-94) and the tool schema is emitted directly from model_json_schema() (workspace_mcp_protocol.py:230-236), producing $defs/$ref and anyOf-null unions; Copilot Studio documents that reference-type inputs are filtered, so propose/resume_workflow_run may silently not appear.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/workflow_run_contract.py:67-94: WorkflowRunInput has steps: list[RunStepInput] and source_bindings: list[SourceBinding]. RunStepInput.references is dict[str, ResultReference]. backend/app/services/workspace_mcp_protocol.py:230-236: _as_mcp_tool passes spec.args_model.model_json_schema() through unchanged. automation_capabilities.py:247-273: propose_workflow_run uses args_model=WorkflowRunInput and resume_workflow_run uses ResumeWorkflowRunInput. I generated both schemas with pydantic 2.13 against a stubbed import (scratchpad/schema_check.py). WorkflowRunInput emits top-level $defs {ResultReference, RunStepInput, SourceBinding} with items/additionalProperties $ref. ResumeWorkflowRunInput (:162-174) emits a flat schema (expected_version int, missing_arguments object, run_id uuid string) with no $defs/$ref. Neither model has Optional fields; the only anyOf is ResultReference.path items [string, integer], with no null branch. The Copilot Studio filtering documentation could not be checked because learn.microsoft.com is blocked by the egress proxy.
reviews.correction: Only propose_workflow_run has $defs/$ref. resume_workflow_run is flat and would not be filtered for reference-type inputs. These models produce no 'anyOf-null' unions (only string|integer). Whether Copilot Studio really drops $ref tools is plausible but was not verified here. Impact is limited to the propose_workflow_run tool on Copilot Studio hosts.
reviews.fix_sketch: In _as_mcp_tool, post-process the schema by inlining $defs/$ref. None of these models is recursive, so a small resolver that substitutes #/$defs/X and drops $defs is enough. Optionally collapse anyOf [T, null] to T without the field in required, for broad host compatibility. Add a unit test asserting that no advertised workspace MCP tool schema contains '$ref' or '$defs'.

title: MCP tool results carry relative links and internal file-server paths
claim: search_firm_memory returns unc_path, share_id and owner and a relative '/firm-memory?...' lawhand_url (chat_tools/handlers.py:246-261); source chips use relative '/api/documents/{id}/download' (396), contrary to docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:395. External assistants cannot deep-link and internal SMB topology leaks into third-party history.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/chat_tools/handlers.py:220-277: search_firm_memory returns unc_path (hit.path), share_id and owner, plus lawhand_url as the relative f"/firm-memory?matter=...&file=..." (:255-260). :390-399: _resolve_source_chips returns the relative url /api/documents/{id}/download, commented as 'origin-relative... the frontend re-bases it'. propose_task and the other propose handlers return these as 'sources' (:1145-1169 and others), and workspace_mcp_protocol.py:537-561 passes handler results to MCP clients unchanged. By contrast, handlers.py:1877 builds an absolute task_url from settings.FRONTEND_URL. Mitigating evidence: automation_capabilities.py:354-366 says search_firm_memory is workspace_mcp-only and deliberately 'Returns... canonical UNC paths for copying, safe LawHand result links'. backend/tests/test_firm_memory_workspace_mcp.py:125-129 asserts that unc_path starts with \\FILESERVER and that lawhand_url is the relative path. docs/workspace_mcp_adapter.md:395-396 says raw provider URLs and storage object IDs 'are not exposed as model tools'.
reviews.correction: The relative URLs are a real defect for external MCP clients, which cannot resolve them. The rest is overstated. Returning UNC paths is a documented, tested design choice ('for copying'), not an accidental leak. The adapter doc line is about which tools exist, not about result payload fields, so it is not a clear contradiction. share_id and owner exposure is the only questionable extra. Whether SMB paths and owners should reach third-party assistants is a product and privacy decision.
reviews.fix_sketch: Build absolute links with settings.FRONTEND_URL (for lawhand_url) and the API origin (for source chip urls) when context.channel == 'workspace_mcp'. Keep relative forms for in-app chat, or have the frontend accept absolute URLs. Drop share_id and owner from MCP hits unless a use case needs them. Optionally put unc_path behind a tenant setting. Update test_firm_memory_workspace_mcp.py:126-129 and the adapter doc.

title: communications:propose consent label omits SMS drafting
claim: The label 'Draft client email proposals without sending' (services/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:46) understates the scope, which also authorizes propose_client_sms (automation_capabilities.py:532-547).

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:46 labels communications:propose 'Draft client email proposals without sending'. backend/app/services/automation_capabilities.py:532-547: propose_client_sms requires the same scopes (matters:read, contacts:read, communications:propose). It inherits the default audiences ('matter_chat','workspace_mcp') from line 192, so it is exposed over Workspace MCP. workspace_mcp_protocol.py:406-433 dispatches it after only a scope and capability check (with an explicit idempotency key for SMS). The label also appears on the consent screen (routers/workspace_mcp_oauth.py:119) and in AS/PRM metadata. A second copy of the same text is at frontend/src/workspaceMcp.js:9. No test pins the label text.
reviews.correction: Accurate. Scope note: the misleading text is in two places (backend WORKSPACE_SCOPE_LABELS and frontend/src/workspaceMcp.js:9), so the fix is not backend-only.
reviews.fix_sketch: Change the label in both places to 'Draft client email and SMS proposals without sending'. Option: bump CONSENT_VERSION so existing grants show the new wording at the next consent. Longer-term option: split out a separate communications:propose_sms scope so SMS drafting can be consented to on its own. Add a test that every capability's required_scopes label names its channel.

title: AI request broker checks data class before resolving the route, skipping the BYOK fail-closed rule
claim: _enforce_policy calls route_matter_context_allowed without a route (ai_request_broker.py:255-272), then resolve_llm_route (317-321) may return the BYOK 'customer' route, which llm_routing.py:383-402 says must fail closed for confidential data. Affects flagged prospect-confidential after-call preparation (after_call_preparation.py:204-219); chat blocks the same case.

reviews.evidence: ai_request_broker.py:210-272: _enforce_policy calls route_matter_context_allowed(db, tenant, use_premium=...) at 259 and 264 without route=. llm_routing.py:373-430: the 'customer' fail-closed rejection (394-396) runs only when route is not None. With route None, the function falls through to profile.standard_allow_matter_context or standard_matter_context_allowed (430). The broker resolves the route only afterwards (ai_request_broker.py:317). resolve_llm_route checks BYOK before profiles and returns resolved_route='customer' (llm_routing.py:529-570). _execute_chat then sends customer_api_key/provider/endpoint to the tenant's provider (ai_request_broker.py:544-546; llm.py:268-275). The only confidential caller is after_call_preparation.py:201-224 (PROSPECT_CONFIDENTIAL, RouteTier.STANDARD, default chat transport). Chat passes route= (chat.py:2421-2429, 724; retrieval_planner.py:148), so it fails closed for the same tenant. Gates: VIRTUAL_ASSISTANT_ENABLED and AFTER_CALL_CONCIERGE_ENABLED both default False (config.py:284-285; broker _surface_enabled 202-205).
reviews.correction: Accurate, but three conditions must all hold: both assistant flags are on (off by default), the tenant has use_customer_llm with a decryptable key, and its profile or platform Standard policy allows matter context. There is also a related latent gap the claim does not name: MATTER_CONFIDENTIAL on the PREMIUM tier skips the check entirely (ai_request_broker.py:255-258). It has no current caller.
reviews.fix_sketch: In execute(), resolve the route before the confidential-data check. Then pass it through: _enforce_policy(db, request, tier, route) calls route_matter_context_allowed(..., use_premium=tier is PREMIUM, route=route, route_tier=tier) for both PROSPECT_ and MATTER_CONFIDENTIAL on every non-background tier, including PREMIUM. Add broker tests: a BYOK 'customer' route with a PROSPECT_CONFIDENTIAL request raises AIRequestDenied, and a profile route is still allowed.

title: Onboarding 'Sync Users' button does not run a sync
claim: handleSyncUsers (OnboardingWizard.jsx:133-151) only persists step numbers (POST /admin/onboarding/step/{n} writes onboarding_step, onboarding.py:203-221) and advances to Review, relying on the post-connect background sync; if that failed the admin sees '0 users imported'.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/pages/OnboardingWizard.jsx:128-146 (current HEAD 96f26e3; the claim's 133-151 is shifted by 5 lines): handleSyncUsers calls advanceStep(STEP.SYNC), loadStatus(), then advanceStep(STEP.REVIEW) if the stale `status` closure shows a connected provider. It never calls a sync API, and its catch cannot fire because advanceStep swallows errors (lines 110-118). backend/app/routers/onboarding.py:203-221 update_onboarding_step only sets tenant.onboarding_step and commits. The only sync the wizard relies on is the best-effort background task integrations.py:1670-1730 (_schedule_user_sync_post_connect -> _sync_users_post_connect_with_session). That task logs failures and calls record_sync_failure, and the wizard never shows either. A real endpoint exists but the wizard does not use it: backend/app/routers/user_sync.py:35-90 (POST /api/sync/users/{microsoft,google,all}, which also advances SYNC->REVIEW, registered at main.py:509). The Review step (OnboardingWizard.jsx:634-640) shows 'No users were imported yet. You can sync again from the Admin panel later.' when totalSynced==0.
reviews.correction: The line numbers moved to 128-146. The admin does not see the literal text '0 users imported'. They see 'No users were imported yet...' with per-provider rows showing 0. There is also a worse case the claim misses. synced_users counts every user whose oauth_provider matches (onboarding.py:145-165), so an admin who signed in with Microsoft or Google SSO counts themselves. After a failed sync the Review step can then say '1 users were imported from your directory.'
reviews.fix_sketch: Add an api.js helper syncAllUsers() that calls POST /sync/users/all, or the per-provider route for the connected provider, skipping personal Google. In handleSyncUsers, await it, and show the added/updated counts plus any per-provider error. On failure, keep the admin on the Sync step with Retry and 'Continue anyway' buttons. Use the data returned by loadStatus() rather than the stale `status` state. Optionally base the Review count on the sync result, or exclude the admin, so it reports only real directory imports.

title: Microsoft token-exchange failure is shown as a Google error; consent errors get a generic message
claim: OAUTH_ERROR_MESSAGES.token_exchange_failed says 'Google authorization could not be completed' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:35-39), but the Microsoft callback emits the same code (integrations.py:545); access_denied, consent_required, interaction_required, invalid_state and oauth_failed all fall back to one generic message (line 77), with no Global Administrator guidance.

reviews.evidence: On current HEAD the problem was fixed in commit ca6812e. The Google-only OAUTH_ERROR_MESSAGES map is gone; `git show ca6812e^:frontend/src/pages/OnboardingWizard.jsx` lines 35-39 and 78 show the old defect. OnboardingWizard.jsx:15,72 now calls oauthErrorMessage(code, searchParams.get('provider')). frontend/src/utils/oauthErrors.js:16-38 names the provider ('Microsoft 365 authorization could not be completed' for token_exchange_failed/no_access_token). It also has separate messages for access_denied (cancelled), consent_required (an administrator must approve LawHand), interaction_required/login_required, invalid_state (took too long / other tab), account_mode_mismatch and identity_verification_failed. backend/app/routers/integrations.py:545 still emits token_exchange_failed for Microsoft, but _error_redirect (1790-1807) always appends &provider=microsoft, so the right provider is named. Tests: frontend/src/utils/oauthErrors.test.js asserts the Microsoft wording and the consent_required admin-approval text.
reviews.correction: The claim describes code from before ca6812e. Small gaps remain. 'oauth_failed', which covers any provider error outside the allowlist at integrations.py:1779-1787, still gets the generic message. The consent_required text says 'an administrator', not a specific Entra role such as Global Administrator. Any admin-approval denial that arrives as access_denied is worded as a cancellation.
reviews.fix_sketch: No fix needed for the claim as written. An optional polish would pass a sanitised Entra error_subcode or AADSTS code through the allowlist, so an admin-approval denial is not worded as a cancellation, and would name the Entra admin roles in the consent_required message.

title: Hub Teams pill and Teams panel use different sources and contradict each other
claim: The hub uses permissions.microsoft.capabilities.teams (IntegrationsHub.jsx:153-161), which depends on account_type that /admin/permissions does not backfill (admin.py:1648-1652 vs 322-324); TeamsPanel uses /integrations/status teams_connected (TeamsPanel.jsx:105-108), which backfills and honours TEAMS_FEATURE_ENABLED (integrations.py:1844-1865). Admins get contradictory states and a reconnect loop.

reviews.evidence: The hub pill (frontend/src/components/IntegrationsHub.jsx:153-163) reads summary.permissions.microsoft.capabilities.teams. The summary comes only from getAdminPermissions() (IntegrationsHub.jsx:353-369). /admin/permissions (backend/app/routers/admin.py:1640-1700) queries TenantCredential at 1648-1652 without calling account_detect.backfill_unknown_credentials. By contrast, /integrations/health backfills at admin.py:322-324 and /integrations/status at integrations.py:1844-1848. capabilities._teams (backend/app/services/capabilities.py:139-158) never looks at TEAMS_FEATURE_ENABLED. /integrations/status computes teams_connected = settings.TEAMS_FEATURE_ENABLED and connected and no missing scopes (integrations.py:1861-1863), and TeamsPanel uses that (TeamsPanel.jsx:105-114). The flag defaults to True (backend/app/config.py:128). Since ca6812e, TeamsPanel.jsx:137-165 shows non-actionable gate cards for a personal Microsoft account and for 'permissions granted but Teams switched off', so no reconnect button appears. The hub pill now reads 'Account type not confirmed' for a null or unknown account type (IntegrationsHub.jsx:161). Backfill is one-shot and persisted (account_detect.py:140-143).
reviews.correction: ca6812e already fixed the reconnect loop and the 'Not available on this account' label for unknown account types. The two views still use different sources, but they now disagree only in edge cases. First, on a deployment with TEAMS_FEATURE_ENABLED=False (not the default), the hub says 'Connected' while the panel says 'Teams is not enabled for this workspace'. Second, for a legacy credential that has not been backfilled, or whose detection failed, the hub says 'Account type not confirmed' while the panel may be fully usable. The unknown-type case fixes itself once the panel's backfill succeeds.
reviews.fix_sketch: Use one source. Either (a) in /admin/permissions, call account_detect.backfill_unknown_credentials before audit_provider, and pass settings.TEAMS_FEATURE_ENABLED into capabilities._teams so it returns status 'disabled' when the flag is off, and map 'disabled' to an 'off' pill in the hub; or (b) have the hub's Teams status read getIntegrationStatus().microsoft.teams_connected, teams_missing_scopes and account_type, which is exactly what TeamsPanel uses. Add a hub test for the flag-off case.

title: Destructive integration actions run without confirmation
claim: Storage migration 'Abandon' (StorageMigrationPanel.jsx:113-116, 140), Zoom/Zoom Phone 'Disconnect' and 'Clear tenant app' (ZoomPanel.jsx:108-119, 134-145, 164-176) and Cloud Search 'Invalidate Cache' (CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:328-352) act on one click, unlike QBOPanel.jsx:146-147.

reviews.evidence:
These actions run on one click with no confirmation:
- Storage migration Abandon: frontend/src/components/StorageMigrationPanel.jsx:113-116, button at 140, no confirmAction.
- Zoom meetings Disconnect: ZoomPanel.jsx:108-119, wired at 338-343.
- Zoom Phone Disconnect: ZoomPanel.jsx:134-145, wired at 266-270.
- Clear tenant app: ZoomPanel.jsx:164-176, button at 655-660. The backend DELETE /zoom-phone/app-credentials (integrations.py:1586-1610) deactivates both the app and the grant credential.
ZoomPanel.jsx contains no 'confirm' at all. The intended pattern exists in QBOPanel.jsx:146-147 (confirmAction with destructive:true) and in IntegrationsPanel.jsx handleDisconnect (~268-275). Cloud Search Invalidate Cache (frontend/src/pages/CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:328-352) calls DELETE /admin/cloud-search/cache (backend/app/routers/cloud_admin.py:616-638). That endpoint only clears the tenant's cached search results so the next query runs fresh. storage_migration.abandon (backend/app/services/storage_migration.py:655-672) only sets phase='abandoned' and completed_at.
reviews.correction: Invalidate Cache is not destructive: the cache rebuilds on the next query, so it does not need a confirmation step. At most, its success toast should reflect a 'cache_disabled' response. Abandon does not discard migration evidence. It is irreversible, though: the migration becomes terminal and cannot be resumed. The four real cases are Abandon, the two Zoom Disconnects and Clear tenant app.
reviews.fix_sketch:
Wrap handleDisconnect, handlePhoneDisconnect and handleClearPhoneApp in ZoomPanel, and abandon in StorageMigrationPanel, with await confirmAction({title, message, confirmLabel, destructive:true}). Suggested consequence text:
- Zoom Phone: new calls stop being captured until someone reconnects.
- Clear tenant app: the current grant is disconnected and the client secret and webhook secret must be entered again.
- Zoom meetings: meeting links stop being created.
- Abandon: the migration closes, cannot be resumed and must be restarted from discovery.
Add one test per handler that asserts a cancelled confirm does not call the API.

title: Admin connect endpoints return raw JSON errors on top-level navigation
claim: The 501/428/403/400 responses in the Microsoft connect (integrations.py:431-448) and google_connect (664-687) endpoints are HTTPExceptions rendered as {"detail": ...}; the admin panel's Connect button is always enabled (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:760-769), unlike onboarding which disables it until agreements are ready (OnboardingWizard.jsx:411-412).

reviews.evidence: microsoft_connect (backend/app/routers/integrations.py:425-448) raises HTTPException 501 when OAuth is not configured, 428 when agreements block connection, and 403 when a non-admin uses intent=admin. google_connect (656-687) raises the same three plus 400 for a bad account_mode. The global handler in backend/app/main.py:889-911 returns JSONResponse({'detail': ..., 'request_id': ...}), so a top-level navigation lands on raw JSON. IntegrationsPanel.jsx:256-266 handleReauthorize navigates with window.location.href to those endpoints. The NotConnectedCard Connect button (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:786-794, previously 760-769) has no disabled prop, and the panel loads neither agreement status nor OAuth-configured status. OnboardingWizard.jsx:407 and 433 disable the connect buttons with disabled={!agreementReady}. The 428 applies only when the tenant has no active cloud credential and agreements are blocking, or are enforced but incomplete (backend/app/services/compliance.py:282-316). That fits a tenant that chose 'Set up later' and then clicks Connect in Admin. No backend test pins these status codes (only test_onboarding_step_plumbing.py tests the guard function itself).
reviews.correction: The panel line numbers moved after ca6812e (button now ~786-794). From the admin-only panel, only the 501 (deployment without an OAuth client) and the 428 (deferred-setup tenant with no credential under agreement enforcement) are realistic. The 403 needs a non-admin and the 400 needs a hand-edited account_mode, so neither comes from the panel UI. An expired session gives a JSON 401 through the same path.
reviews.fix_sketch: In both connect endpoints, replace the pre-authorize HTTPExceptions with _error_redirect(provider, code) for top-level navigations (Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate or Accept: text/html). Suggested codes: oauth_not_configured, agreements_required, admin_required, invalid_account_mode. Route admin-intent errors for completed tenants to /admin?tab=integrations instead of /onboarding. Add matching messages to frontend/src/utils/oauthErrors.js. In IntegrationsPanel, load the agreement status the wizard already uses and disable Connect with an explanation while it is blocking. Add backend tests for the redirect codes.

title: In-product and doc navigation points to locations that do not exist
claim: Wizard says 'Admin > Integrations > Cloud > Storage migration' (OnboardingWizard.jsx:538-540) but it is under Advanced and needs manage_integrations (IntegrationsHub.jsx:238-257); CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:95 says 'Settings > Integrations'; TeamsPanel.jsx:133 names an 'Integrations tab' without a link; docs describe missing Shared Drive/root-repair controls (21-onboarding-and-storage-setup.md:54,63) and send folder repair to SMB 'File Shares' (18-cloud-provider-support.md:97); the 'MCP Servers' button (UserMcpAccess.jsx:411-417) silently falls back to Overview without manage_integrations.

reviews.evidence: Checked on the branch HEAD (96f26e3) and on origin/main. That function requires manage_integrations only when the session carries a capabilities array. (2) CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:95 still says 'No admin token. Connect in Settings → Integrations.' CloudSearchAdmin is mounted inside the Integrations hub (IntegrationsHub.jsx:27), and connecting happens in the Cloud section. (3) Teams: origin/main TeamsPanel.jsx:133 names 'the Integrations tab' with no link. At HEAD, TeamsPanel.jsx:19,135-136 links to /admin?tab=integrations&integration=cloud (ca6812e). (4) Docs: 21-onboarding-and-storage-setup.md:54 sends malformed-root repair to Advanced → Storage migration, but StorageMigrationPanel.jsx:130-140 only offers start migration (optional root folder ID), reconcile, abandon and cutover, with no root-repair action. :63 says to add the service account 'directly under Document storage', but the Document storage disclosure (IntegrationsPanel.jsx:420-485) has only the primary provider, 'Create missing matter folders' and the SharePoint binding, with no Shared Drive or service-account control. 18-cloud-provider-support.md:97 says to 'reprovision those folders in File Shares', which is the SMB section (IntegrationsHub.jsx:114, 299 smb→file-shares). (5) MCP: the UserMcpAccess.jsx:411-417 button calls onNavigateMcp → AdminPage.jsx:1527 → selectIntegrationSection('mcp') (AdminPage.jsx:1445-1449). IntegrationsHub.jsx:476-478 falls back to 'overview' when the section is not in the permitted lists.
reviews.correction: The Teams item is already fixed on this branch (ca6812e, unmerged PR #610) but is still present on origin/main. The MCP silent fallback only affects admin-role users with a custom role whose capabilities array omits manage_integrations: the system Administrator role gets every capability (capabilities.py:37), and a session with no capabilities array passes canOperateIntegrations. The 'needs manage_integrations' condition for Storage migration applies only in that case. The docs item on line 54 is half right: the navigation path is correct, but the target has no repair control. The rest holds.
reviews.fix_sketch: Copy and docs only. Change the wizard text to 'Admin → Integrations → Advanced → Storage migration' and make it a Link to /admin?tab=integrations&integration=storage-migration. Change CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:95 to 'Connect Microsoft 365 or Google under Cloud accounts' with a link to integration=cloud. In 18-cloud-provider-support.md:97, replace 'File Shares' with 'Integrations → Cloud → Document storage → Create missing matter folders'. In 21-onboarding...md, reword :54 to 'contact support (or re-run Storage step)' until a repair control exists, and reword :63 so the Shared Drive and service-account work happens in the Google Admin console, not in LawHand. In UserMcpAccess, hide or disable the MCP Servers button (or show 'requires Manage integrations') when canOperateIntegrations(user) is false. Add a unit test for that gate.

title: Cloud Search copy hard-codes a 15-minute sync interval
claim: CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:390 states 15 minutes, but the interval is CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN and the job runs only if enabled (scheduler.py:804-809).

reviews.evidence: CloudSearchAdmin.jsx:390 (same on origin/main) renders the literal 'Metadata sync runs automatically every {15} minutes'. The actual schedule is scheduler.py:804-815: the job is added only if settings.CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED, with minutes=settings.CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN. It also runs only in the process with RUN_SCHEDULER (main.py:300). Defaults are config.py:569 CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED=True and config.py:583 CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN=15. No env or compose file in the repo overrides the interval; only ci.yml:1131 disables cloud search, for CI. scheduler.py:112 (AGENT_REGISTRY) already formats the real interval ('Every {N} minutes'). The status endpoint cloud_admin.py:155-200 does not return the interval or the enabled flag.
reviews.correction: The hard-coded value equals the shipped default, so the copy is accurate in every configuration present in the repo. It is wrong only when an operator overrides CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN or disables CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED. The impact is minor drift.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add sync_enabled (settings.CLOUD_SEARCH_ENABLED) and sync_interval_min (settings.CLOUD_METADATA_SYNC_INTERVAL_MIN) to the /cloud-search/status response. Render 'every N minutes' from them, or 'Automatic sync is off' when disabled. A copy-only alternative is to say 'Metadata syncs automatically on a schedule' without a number.

title: Document Open links use the stored web URL instead of the /open resolver
claim: MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1140, 1280, 1406 link to doc.cloud_url (persisted storage_path) rather than /matters/{m}/documents/{d}/open, which resolves a fresh editing URL from durable IDs (matter_documents.py:719-747) and is already used by ActionProposalCard.jsx:584-586. After a rename/move in SharePoint/OneDrive, Open 404s.

reviews.evidence: MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:1140 and 1406 link to `doc.cloud_url || getMatterDocumentDownloadUrl(...)`, and 1278-1286 link to `doc.cloud_url`. cloud_url is the persisted storage_path whenever that is an http(s) URL (models/matter_document.py:204-209). storage_path is rewritten only by storage migration (storage_migration.py:607), never when a file is renamed or moved at the provider. The resolver GET /matters/{m}/documents/{d}/open (matter_documents.py:718-747) calls matter_file_store.get_matter_file_open_url, which reads a fresh webViewLink or webUrl by provider_object_id (matter_file_store.py:311-361). ActionProposalCard.jsx:584-586 and TaskBoard.jsx:1067 already use it, and provider_object_id and provider_drive_id are included in MatterDocumentResponse (schemas/matter_document.py:43-45).
reviews.correction: The file lives at frontend/src/components/chat/ActionProposalCard.jsx, not components/. 'Open 404s after a rename or move' does not apply to every provider. This part rests on provider URL formats, not on repo code: Google Drive webViewLinks are ID-based and survive renames and moves, and SharePoint/OneDrive Office documents usually get Doc.aspx?sourcedoc={GUID} webUrls. The breakage is mostly path-based webUrls, such as PDFs and images in SharePoint or OneDrive for Business, and moves across libraries. The resolver also fails with 409 for legacy rows that have no provider_object_id (MatterFileMetadataError is a MatterFileReadError), so a blind swap would break those rows.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add getMatterDocumentOpenUrl(matterId, docId) to api.js. In the three places in MatterDocumentsTab, use it when doc.provider_object_id is set and storage_backend is google_drive, onedrive or sharepoint; otherwise fall back to doc.cloud_url, then to the download URL. Keep the labels as they are and update MatterDocumentsTab.test.jsx.

title: Documents tab repeats the slowest live cloud search
claim: MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:407-413 calls getMatterCloudFiles on mount although MatterDetailPage already ran it ('by far the slowest request', MatterDetailPage.jsx:569-575), and swallows errors.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/components/MatterDocumentsTab.jsx:407-413 runs getMatterCloudFiles(matterId) in an unconditional mount effect and ends with .catch(() => {}), so errors are dropped and the Cloud Files block (lines 736-745) just never renders. frontend/src/pages/MatterDetailPage.jsx:560-576 already calls loadCloudFiles once the matter has loaded, and the comment there calls it 'by far the slowest request this page makes'. MatterDetailPage.jsx:1680-1690 renders MatterDocumentsTab only while activeTab==='documents' and does not pass it the parent's cloudFiles. The tab therefore remounts, and fetches again, every time the user switches back to Documents. backend/app/routers/matters.py:221-263 (_build_matter_cloud_files_response) runs a live CloudSearchService.search over drive, onedrive and sharepoint each time within CLOUD_SEARCH_UI_BUDGET_SECONDS. backend/app/services/cloud_search.py has no cache. onCloudFolderChange (MatterDetailPage.jsx:1686-1690) also makes the parent re-run loadCloudFiles, so provisioning costs two searches.
reviews.correction: Accurate. The waste is worse than one duplicate per page load: the tab fetches again on every visit to Documents, because the tab is conditionally mounted.
reviews.fix_sketch: Lift the data. Pass the parent's cloudFiles?.files, plus loadCloudFiles as a reload callback, into MatterDocumentsTab as props (e.g. cloudFiles, onReloadCloudFiles), and delete the tab's own useEffect fetch. Keep onSynced so the tab can override locally after a manual sync, or have it call the parent's setter. If the tab must stand alone elsewhere, fetch only when the prop is undefined. Surface a small 'Cloud files could not be loaded - Retry' line instead of swallowing the error.

title: Correspondence load failure renders as an empty archive
claim: MatterCorrespondenceTab.jsx:570-573 does .catch(() => setItems([])), rendering 'No correspondence captured yet. Configure capture rules, then click Scan now' (683-689) on API/permission errors.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/components/MatterCorrespondenceTab.jsx:566-575: the load() callback calls getMatterCorrespondence(...).then(setItems(...)).catch(() => setItems([])), and there is no error state anywhere in the component (state declared at 556-564). Lines 682-689: when items.length === 0 the tab renders 'No correspondence captured yet.' and 'Configure capture rules, then click Scan now to archive matching emails.' A 403 (ethical wall or permission), a 500 or a network failure therefore looks exactly like an empty archive.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add const [loadError, setLoadError] = useState(''). In load(), clear it on start. In the catch, set it from err.response?.data?.detail or a fallback, and do not clear items (or set [] and flag the error). Render role=alert text with a 'Retry' button that calls load() before the empty-state branch. Show the 'Configure capture rules / Scan now' copy only when the load succeeded and returned zero items. Add a vitest case for the rejected promise.

title: Filled sample documents uploaded as template sources stay on LawHand host disk
claim: Template intake invites filled samples (TemplatesPage.jsx:843) and document_templates.py:760-790 persists these originals under UPLOAD_DIR, whereas matter files go to the customer's own cloud (matter_file_store.py:1-8). Client PII stays outside the firm's retention/eDiscovery controls.

reviews.evidence: frontend/src/pages/TemplatesPage.jsx:843 tells users 'Filled or handwritten entries help locate reusable details' and accepts scans. backend/app/routers/document_templates.py:760-790: _persist_template_source writes the bytes under settings.UPLOAD_DIR/{tenant}/templates/{id} (config.py:489 defaults UPLOAD_DIR to /app/uploads, host disk). At 2762-2791 the upload-from-sample flow stores the canonical sample bytes (the original, or a PDF converted from an image) as source_storage_path. Copy and derive flows at 3037-3057, 3146-3158 and 3265-3273 also write an 'original-*' evidence copy of the retained original into each new template's directory. matter_file_store.py:1-8 routes matter files to OneDrive, SharePoint or Drive (with a legacy local fallback). Extra finding: delete_template (4417-4436) unlinks only source_storage_path. source_evidence_storage_path files and the template directory are never removed, so a filled original can outlive the template's deletion.
reviews.correction: The core is accurate. Context: LawHand's own database already holds client PII (matters, contacts, intakes), so these template sources are one of several PII stores outside the firm's M365/Workspace retention, not a unique exception. The orphaned evidence copy after deletion is an aggravating detail the claim does not mention.
reviews.fix_sketch: Short term: on template delete, remove the evidence file and rmtree the template source directory, after checking it is under the expected root. Add intake copy telling users to redact or use a blank sample, and optionally store only the reviewed, templatized copy once field review is done. Longer term: store template sources in the tenant's cloud (a firm Templates folder through matter_file_store-style routing), keeping the sha256 integrity contract. Alternatively, document the retention and encrypt at rest with a purge policy.

title: Microsoft integration is hard-wired to the commercial cloud
claim: login.microsoftonline.com and graph.microsoft.com are hard-coded in 18 modules (e.g. storage_discovery.py:18, 30-32; cloud_folder_audit.py:140-145) and continuation-URL validators reject other hosts, so GCC High/DoD/21Vianet tenants cannot use LawHand.

reviews.evidence: backend/app/services/storage_discovery.py:18 GRAPH='https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0'; :30-32 _safe_graph_url requires hostname=='graph.microsoft.com'. backend/app/services/cloud_folder_audit.py:141-145 rejects continuation URLs whose netloc != 'graph.microsoft.com'. 22 backend/app modules hard-code the hosts, e.g. GRAPH_BASE constants in cloud_init.py:27, teams.py:30, cloud_search.py:56, cloud_sync.py:44, matter_file_store.py:60, cloud_admin.py:28; authority URLs in routers/auth.py:1339,1383, routers/integrations.py:503,543, token_vault.py:238, teams_voice.py:864, routers/teams.py:402. backend/app/utils/oauth_security.py:19 fixes the JWKS URL and :145 rejects any issuer not starting with https://login.microsoftonline.com/. config.py:106-108 exposes only MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/TENANT_ID, with no cloud, authority-host or Graph-host setting. The add-in authority is env-configurable (office-addin/src/main.ts:18 VITE_OFFICE_ENTRA_AUTHORITY), but backend token verification is not.
reviews.correction: The count is 22 backend modules, not 18. 'Cannot use LawHand' is overstated. GCC High, DoD and 21Vianet tenants cannot use Microsoft sign-in or any M365 integration (OneDrive/SharePoint storage, Outlook mail, calendar, Teams, the Office add-in exchange). LawHand itself still works through password login (routers/auth.py:2024 /login, :1865 /register) and non-Microsoft storage. GCC (Moderate) uses the worldwide endpoints and is unaffected.
reviews.fix_sketch: Add a MICROSOFT_CLOUD setting (global|usgov|usgovdod|china) that maps to an authority host (login.microsoftonline.com / login.microsoftonline.us / login.partner.microsoftonline.cn) and a Graph host (graph.microsoft.com / graph.microsoft.us / dod-graph.microsoft.us / microsoftgraph.chinacloudapi.cn). Export GRAPH_BASE and AUTHORITY_BASE from services/graph_client.py and replace the 22 module-level constants. Make the continuation validators (storage_discovery._safe_graph_url, cloud_folder_audit) compare against the configured host. Parametrize the oauth_security JWKS URL and issuer prefix. Document a separate Entra app registration per cloud, since tokens cannot cross clouds. Realistically this is a per-deployment setting, not per tenant.

title: Office add-in roadmap has no live TASKS entries; the only item refers to the removed word-addin prototype
claim: TASKS.md:958-959 still says 'Ship the Word add-in properly ... or archive it' though word-addin/ was replaced by office-addin/ (docs/office-document-assistant-plan.md:355); Office plan Slices 1-5 (259-306) and W2 Template Builder have no TASKS entries.

reviews.evidence: TASKS.md:958-959 (under '## Add-on Modules Roadmap — Sprints B-F', :904) still reads 'Ship the Word add-in properly (it hardcodes http://localhost:8000/api ...) or archive it'. word-addin/ no longer exists in the repo, and docs/office-document-assistant-plan.md:355 records its removal. So that entry is stale. However, TASKS.md:3001-3011 has '### BK18. Office document assistant integration (P0, LARGE)', which links docs/office-document-assistant-plan.md and lists open checkbox entries for Slice 0 through Slice 5 plus the write-safety invariant. It sits under '## Backlog — Integration Health & Module Restoration' (:2778). The plan's slices at docs/office-document-assistant-plan.md:259-306 are therefore tracked. A grep of TASKS.md for 'Template Builder' or 'W2' finds nothing, so W2 (docs/template-studio-clio-parity-execution-status.md:187-191) has no entry. TASKS.md:962 reuses the ID 'BK18' for 'Author the four Mediation prompt templates', which collides with :3001.
reviews.correction: The claim that the Office roadmap has no live TASKS entries is false: BK18 at TASKS.md:3001-3011 tracks Slices 0-5. What holds: the Sprint F item at :958-959 still refers to the removed word-addin/ prototype; W2 Template Builder has no TASKS entry; the BK18 ID is used twice (:962 and :3001); and Slice 0 (:3005) is still unchecked although office-addin/ appears to deliver it. The real issue is ledger hygiene, not an invisible roadmap.
reviews.fix_sketch: Replace TASKS.md:958-959 with a pointer to BK18 (or mark it done: word-addin removed, superseded by office-addin/). Tick or annotate BK18 Slice 0 with the office-addin evidence. Renumber the Mediation-templates BK18 at :962 (and its mention at :893) to a free ID. Add a W2 Template Builder entry referencing docs/template-studio-clio-parity-execution-status.md:187-191, including the WordApi 1.3 capability spike.
